001_1948-10-04_Dayton, Ohio_38_143685_bo.report_summary:
**Witness:** Maj. C. M. Smartt, pilot and ordnance officer with the 2349 AF Ordnance at Hamilton Air Force Base. He and his co-pilot were flying a C-47 transport at 6,000 feet near Dayton, Ohio, on 4 October 1948 at approximately 1430 hours local time.

**Sighting:** Smartt reported observing three or four (initially reported as 15 to 20) silvery white, metallic, teardrop-shaped objects, each approximately 1.5 feet long and 9 inches across. The objects appeared one at a time at intervals of three or four minutes. Visibility was hazy at 15 miles. His attention was drawn to the objects when some came close enough that he and his co-pilot had to duck to avoid what appeared to be an impending collision through the aircraft nose.

**Object:** The objects were described as silver or silvery white teardrops with metallic appearance. They showed a slight tail but no evidence of exhaust. Each object remained in view for only about one second due to their apparent high speed.

**Tactics:** The objects traveled in a straight line in a general easterly direction with a gradual descent, passing from view under the wing of the C-47. No sound was noticed. Smartt compared the sighting to dumping half a gallon of water 200 yards in front of an approaching aircraft about 200 feet above it, with the water taking teardrop shape.

**Note:** Significant discrepancies were noted in Smartt's reports. His first report claimed 15-20 objects, while his later account reduced this to three or four. Initially he stated some objects traveled upward and some downward with no definite course; later he omitted any mention of upward movement. The water-dump analogy suggests a simultaneous group sighting rather than objects appearing singly at intervals, creating ambiguity about what was actually observed.
001_1948-10-04_Dayton, Ohio_38_143685_bo.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** C. M. Smartt少校，汉密尔顿空军基地(Hamilton Air Force Base)第2349航空军械部队的飞行员兼军械官。1948年10月4日当地时间约1430时，他和副驾驶员驾驶一架C-47运输机在俄亥俄州代顿(Dayton, Ohio)附近6,000英尺高度飞行。

**Sighting:** Smartt报告观察到三或四个（最初报告为15至20个）银白色金属质感的泪滴形物体，每个约1.5英尺长、9英寸宽。这些物体以三到四分钟的间隔逐个出现。当时能见度为15英里，天气朦胧。他注意到这些物体是因为有些物体靠得太近，以至于他和副驾驶员不得不低头躲避看似即将通过机头发生的碰撞。

**Object:** 这些物体被描述为银色或银白色泪滴状，具有金属外观。它们显示出轻微的尾部，但没有排气迹象。由于明显的高速运动，每个物体在视野中仅停留约一秒钟。

**Tactics:** 这些物体沿直线向大致东方移动并逐渐下降，从C-47机翼下方消失在视野中。未注意到任何声音。Smartt将此次目击比作在接近中的飞机前方200码、上方约200英尺处倾倒半加仑水，水呈泪滴状。

**Note:** Smartt的报告中存在明显差异。他的第一份报告声称有15-20个物体，而后来的陈述将数量减少到三或四个。最初他表示一些物体向上移动、一些向下移动且无明确路线；后来他省略了任何关于向上移动的提及。倾倒水的类比暗示的是同时出现的群体目击而非间隔单独出现的物体，这给实际观察到的情况造成了模糊性。

001_1948-10-15_Fukuoka area, Japan_38_14.report_summary:
**Witness:** An F-61 pilot and radar observer operating out of the Fukuoka area conducted multiple intercept attempts of an unidentified aircraft on the night of 15 October 1948. The interception zone spanned the area between Shigamo Shima (33°40'N, 132°00'E) and Fukue Suima (32°45'N, 128°40'E). Sufficient moonlight permitted visual silhouette identification, though no details could be discerned.

**Sighting:** The crew encountered the object(s) six times over the course of the mission, continuing search operations until approximately 0130 hours. Possibly one or two unidentified aircraft were involved. Ground radar picked up only the F-61 periodically, as the interceptor flew in and out of permanent ground return areas. The object(s) were detected only by the F-61's airborne radar. Weather conditions showed unlimited ceiling, calm winds, 5-6 miles visibility with hazy cloud coverage scattered at 12,000-14,000 feet.

**Object:** Size could not be estimated, and it was impossible to determine whether the craft was jet or propeller driven. No exhaust flames or trails were observed. Speed was reported as much greater than the F-61, with a high rate of acceleration. The object demonstrated capability for nearly vertical ascent or descent beyond radar elevation limits.

**Tactics:** The object exhibited awareness of the F-61's location at all times, suggesting possible radar equipment aboard. Initial detection occurred at 10 miles (lost at 5,000 feet). The last three sightings occurred within a 10-minute period: each time the F-61 detected the object at approximately 9 miles ahead, slowly closed to within 12,000 feet, whereupon the object would suddenly accelerate, dive, and disappear from the airborne radarscope. The F-61 attempted normal pickup by diving after the object but was unsuccessful in all cases. After six encounters, the object was not detected again despite continued searching.

**Note:** The object's consistent evasive maneuvers and apparent awareness of the interceptor's position represent highly unusual characteristics.
001_1948-10-15_Fukuoka area, Japan_38_14.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 一名F-61飞行员和雷达观察员于1948年10月15日夜间从福冈(Fukuoka)地区起飞,对一架不明飞行器进行了多次拦截尝试。拦截区域横跨志贺茂岛(Shigamo Shima)(北纬33°40',东经132°00')和福江水岛(Fukue Suima)(北纬32°45',东经128°40')之间的区域。充足的月光允许进行视觉轮廓识别,但无法辨别细节。

**Sighting:** 机组人员在任务过程中六次遭遇该目标,搜索行动持续至大约0130时。可能涉及一架或两架不明飞行器。地面雷达仅周期性地捕捉到F-61,因为拦截机飞进飞出永久地面回波区域。该目标仅被F-61的机载雷达探测到。天气状况显示无云高限制,风力平静,能见度5-6英里,在12,000-14,000英尺高度有分散的雾状云层覆盖。

**Object:** 无法估计尺寸,也无法判断该飞行器是喷气式还是螺旋桨驱动。未观察到排气火焰或尾迹。报告速度远超F-61,具有高加速率。该目标展示了几乎垂直上升或下降超出雷达仰角限制的能力。

**Tactics:** 该目标始终表现出对F-61位置的感知,暗示可能装备有雷达设备。初次探测发生在10英里处(在5,000英尺高度时失去)。最后三次目击发生在10分钟内:每次F-61在大约9英里前方探测到目标,缓慢接近至12,000英尺以内,此时目标会突然加速、俯冲并从机载雷达屏幕上消失。F-61尝试通过俯冲追踪进行常规捕获,但所有情况下均未成功。经过六次遭遇后,尽管继续搜索,但未再次探测到该目标。

**Note:** 该目标持续的规避机动和对拦截机位置的明显感知代表了极不寻常的特征。

001_1948-10-20_Winona, Minnesota_38_1436.report_summary:
**Witness:** Dr. F. T. Benoit and Paul Zenk observed an unusual aerial phenomenon from the ground at Winona, Minnesota, at 6:00 AM on October 20, 1948. The witnesses' occupations and backgrounds are not specified. This incident was reported in the Minneapolis Morning Tribune on October 21, 1948, but the witnesses were not directly contacted by investigators from Wold Chamberlain Field in Minneapolis.

**Sighting:** The observers witnessed a single, slowly traveling object that ultimately broke up into numerous bright particles over the town. The time in sight and altitude were not specified, though the object was visible long enough for the witnesses to estimate its dimensions and observe its disintegration.

**Object:** The object was estimated to be approximately 25 feet long by 8 feet wide. It was described as appearing like "a bunch of sparks with a tail," exhibiting luminosity in the form of sparks with an accompanying tail or exhaust trail. The color, exact shape, and apparent construction were not detailed beyond this spark-like description.

**Tactics:** The object traveled at a slow speed before breaking up into numerous bright particles. This disintegration over the town was noted as one of the peculiarities of the sighting, along with the slow speed of travel.

**Note:** The witnesses were not interviewed directly by Air Force investigators. The report is based solely on the newspaper account published the day after the sighting. A cross-reference is made to Incident 185, which involves witnesses L. A. Hansen and Harold Oliver, suggesting possible related observations.
001_1948-10-20_Winona, Minnesota_38_1436.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** F. T. Benoit博士和Paul Zenk于1948年10月20日上午6:00在明尼苏达州威诺纳(Winona, Minnesota)从地面观察到一个不寻常的空中现象。目击者的职业和背景未予说明。该事件刊登于1948年10月21日的《明尼阿波利斯晨报》(Minneapolis Morning Tribune),但明尼阿波利斯沃尔德·张伯伦机场(Wold Chamberlain Field)的调查人员并未直接联系目击者。

**Sighting:** 观察者目击了一个缓慢移动的单一物体,该物体最终在城镇上空分解成无数明亮的微粒。目击时间和高度未予说明,尽管该物体在视野中停留的时间足以让目击者估计其尺寸并观察到其解体过程。

**Object:** 该物体估计长约25英尺、宽约8英尺。其外观被描述为"一束带尾巴的火花",呈现出火花形式的发光现象,并伴有尾迹或排气痕迹。除了这种火花状的描述外,其颜色、确切形状和明显构造均未详细说明。

**Tactics:** 该物体以缓慢速度移动,之后分解成无数明亮的微粒。这种在城镇上空的解体现象以及缓慢的移动速度被列为此次目击事件的特殊之处。

**Note:** 空军调查人员未直接访问目击者。该报告仅基于目击事件发生次日发布的报纸报道。报告交叉引用了第185号事件(Incident 185),该事件涉及目击者L. A. Hansen和Harold Oliver,暗示可能存在相关观测。

001_1948-10-29_Goose Bay, Labrador, Cana.report_summary:
**Witness:** A radar operator at AAF Goose Bay, Labrador, detected an unknown object on Ground Control Approach (GCA) radar on 29 October 1948. A second operator was called in to verify the findings.

**Sighting:** Three separate radar detections occurred at 0812Z, 0819Z, and 0916Z. The first sighting placed the object approximately 2 miles from the center of the field on a bearing of 170° (in the Hamilton River area). The object traveled about 2 miles before disappearing. The second sighting at 0819Z showed the object on a bearing of 090°, moving slowly in a wide arc to 270° over 6 minutes before disappearing (Lake Melville and Dock Area). The third sighting at 0916Z showed the object east of the field on a heading of 270°, approximately 2 miles distant in perfect alignment with runway 27.

**Object:** The radar return appeared to be the size of a normal aircraft, though altitude could not be determined—it could have been at extremely low or extremely high altitude. The object traveled at an estimated 25 to 30 MPH. The radar image was very clear on the GCA scope at all times. No visual confirmation was obtained.

**Tactics:** The object's behavior resembled that of an aircraft making an approach for landing, particularly during the third sighting when it was aligned with runway 27.

**Note:** The slow speed (25-30 MPH) is unusual for conventional aircraft, though consistent with a helicopter or very slow-moving aircraft. The multiple appearances and clear radar returns suggest a physical object rather than atmospheric anomaly.
001_1948-10-29_Goose Bay, Labrador, Cana.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 1948年10月29日，AAF古斯湾(Goose Bay)、拉布拉多的一名雷达操作员在地面控制进近(GCA)雷达上探测到一个不明物体。随后召集了第二名操作员来核实这一发现。

**Sighting:** 在0812Z、0819Z和0916Z时分别发生了三次雷达探测。第一次目击将物体定位在距离场地中心约2英里处，方位角170°(位于汉密尔顿河(Hamilton River)区域)。该物体在消失前移动了约2英里。0819Z的第二次目击显示物体位于方位角090°，在6分钟内缓慢以宽弧线移动至270°后消失(梅尔维尔湖(Lake Melville)和码头区)。0916Z的第三次目击显示物体位于场地东侧,航向270°，距离约2英里，与27号跑道完美对齐。

**Object:** 雷达回波显示的大小似乎与普通飞行器相当，但无法确定高度——可能处于极低或极高的高度。该物体以估计25至30英里/小时的速度移动。雷达图像在GCA显示屏上始终非常清晰。未获得目视确认。

**Tactics:** 该物体的行为类似于飞行器进行着陆进近，特别是在第三次目击时，当时它与27号跑道对齐。

**Note:** 缓慢的速度(25-30英里/小时)对于常规飞行器来说不同寻常，但与直升机或速度极慢的飞行器相符。多次出现和清晰的雷达回波表明这是一个实体物体，而非大气异常现象。

001_1948-09-22_Albany, Georgia_38_143685.report_summary:
**Witness:** Lt Martin G. Rubisch, Assistant Combat Operations Officer and co-pilot stationed at Eglin Auxiliary Field #2, Eglin AFB, Florida, observed an unidentified object while serving as co-pilot on a C-47 aircraft approaching Turner AF Base near Albany, Georgia, at approximately 1530 hours EST on 22 September 1948. He was the only crew member aboard the C-47 to observe the object.

**Sighting:** The C-47 was approaching Turner Field from the southwest at approximately 2,000 feet altitude under CAVU (clear air, visibility unlimited) conditions when Lt Rubisch noticed the object approaching at an angle of about 25°. The object was estimated to be 500 feet lower than the aircraft (between 1,500-2,000 feet altitude), approximately 1,500-2,000 feet away horizontally, and 500 feet laterally. The sighting lasted approximately 3 seconds.

**Object:** The object was described as metallic and shiny, approximately 5-10 feet in size (comparable to a radio-controlled model airplane). Shape could not be determined, but Lt Rubisch specifically noted the absence of visible wings or rudder. The object traveled in level flight at an estimated speed of 250 MPH on a heading of 335°. No exhaust trail, sound, or luminosity was observed. Construction appeared metallic.

**Tactics:** The object maintained level flight throughout the brief observation period.

**Note:** The investigating officer found Lt Rubisch's ability to determine color, speed, and size at distance to be excellent, and he closely corroborated information from his initial interrogation. However, the observer's credibility was significantly undermined when his Squadron Commander stated that Lt Rubisch "is inclined to exaggerate and is a person whose opinion is not highly regarded by associate officers." The interrogating officer concluded the observer was of normal intelligence and sound character, though also inclined to exaggeration.
001_1948-09-22_Albany, Georgia_38_143685.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 马丁·G·鲁比施中尉(Lt Martin G. Rubisch),驻扎在佛罗里达州埃格林空军基地(Eglin AFB)埃格林第2辅助机场的助理作战行动官和副驾驶员,于1948年9月22日东部标准时间约1530时,在担任一架C-47飞机副驾驶员接近佐治亚州奥尔巴尼附近的特纳空军基地(Turner AF Base)时,观察到一个不明物体。他是C-47上唯一观察到该物体的机组人员。

**Sighting:** 该C-47飞机在CAVU(晴空,能见度无限)条件下,以约2,000英尺高度从西南方向接近特纳机场时,鲁比施中尉注意到该物体以约25°角接近。据估计,该物体比飞机低500英尺(高度在1,500-2,000英尺之间),水平距离约1,500-2,000英尺,横向距离500英尺。目击持续时间约3秒。

**Object:** 该物体被描述为金属质地且闪亮,大小约5-10英尺(相当于一架无线电遥控模型飞机)。无法确定形状,但鲁比施中尉特别指出未见明显的机翼或方向舵。该物体以估计250英里/小时的速度沿335°航向做水平飞行。未观察到尾迹、声音或发光现象。构造看似金属质地。

**Tactics:** 在整个短暂观察期间,该物体保持水平飞行。

**Note:** 调查官认为鲁比施中尉在远距离判断颜色、速度和大小方面的能力极佳,且他详细证实了初次询问中的信息。然而,当其中队指挥官表示鲁比施中尉"倾向于夸大其词,是一个其意见不受同僚军官高度重视的人"时,该观察者的可信度受到严重削弱。询问官总结认为该观察者智力正常、品格良好,但也倾向于夸大其词。

001_1948-10-24_Moorhead, Minnesota_38_14.report_summary:
**Witness:** L. G. Sanders and his wife, residents of 9th Street, North Fargo, North Dakota. No occupation or hobbies listed. Both witnesses observed the object clearly.

**Sighting:** On October 24, 1948, around 5:45 P.M. during early evening, the witnesses were motoring northwest on U.S. Highway #52 near the outskirts of Moorhead, Minnesota en route to Fargo, North Dakota. Mr. Sanders first noticed the light to his right and pointed it out to his wife. Visibility was good at the time, with observers estimating they could have seen a conventional aircraft at the estimated distance of the object.

**Object:** A single light traveling in horizontal flight from east to west. No details provided on size, color, shape, luminosity, distance, time in sight, sound, or construction beyond characterizing it as a "light." Speed estimated at 2 to 3 times faster than a conventional airplane.

**Tactics:** The object maintained horizontal flight with a slight upward trajectory rather than descending.

**Note:** Both witnesses ruled out the meteor hypothesis, citing two factors: the extended duration of visibility and the fact that the flight path showed a slight rise rather than the typical descending trajectory of a meteor.
001_1948-10-24_Moorhead, Minnesota_38_14.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** L. G. Sanders及其妻子,居住在北达科他州北法戈市第9街。未列出职业或爱好。两位目击者都清楚地观察到了该物体。

**Sighting:** 1948年10月24日傍晚约下午5点45分,目击者驾车沿52号美国国道向西北行驶,位置在明尼苏达州穆尔黑德(Moorhead, Minnesota)郊区附近,前往北达科他州法戈市(Fargo, North Dakota)途中。Sanders先生首先注意到右侧的光源并指给妻子看。当时能见度良好,观察者估计在该物体所处的距离上他们本可以看清常规飞行器。

**Object:** 一个单一光源,以水平飞行方式从东向西移动。除了将其描述为"光源"外,未提供关于大小、颜色、形状、光度、距离、可见时长、声音或结构的详细信息。速度估计为常规飞机的2至3倍。

**Tactics:** 该物体保持水平飞行,带有轻微上升轨迹而非下降。

**Note:** 两位目击者排除了流星假设,理由有两点:可见时间较长,以及飞行路径呈现轻微上升而非流星典型的下降轨迹。

001_1948-10-15_Neubiberg, Bavaria, Germa.report_summary:
**Witness:** Multiple men stationed at Neubiberg Air Force Base observed the object from a housing project located 2 miles west of the base. Specific names and occupations were not provided.

**Sighting:** On an unspecified date in October 1948, between 1200 and 1430 hours, an unidentified flying object was observed for approximately 2 minutes. The sun was high at the time. Weather conditions were not specified. The object was positioned between the observers and the sun during the sighting.

**Object:** The object appeared black in color with a round visible circumference, though overall shape and size could not be determined. Altitude could not be estimated. The object's speed appeared faster than an F-47 type aircraft (likely referring to P-47 Thunderbolt fighter). No sound, luminosity, exhaust trail, or construction details were reported.

**Tactics:** The object pursued a southwest course. No other tactical maneuvers were noted or specified.

**Note:** Evaluation classified as B-2. The sighting involved multiple military witnesses from Neubiberg AFB, an American air base in occupied Germany. The lack of detailed observer information and many "N/S" (not stated) entries suggests an incomplete investigation or report.
001_1948-10-15_Neubiberg, Bavaria, Germa.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 多名驻扎在诺伊比贝格空军基地(Neubiberg Air Force Base)的人员从基地以西2英里的住宅区观察到该物体。未提供具体姓名和职业信息。

**Sighting:** 在1948年10月某日,时间介于1200至1430小时之间,观察到一个不明飞行物体约2分钟。当时太阳位置很高。天气状况未说明。目击期间该物体位于观察者与太阳之间。

**Object:** 该物体呈黑色,可见轮廓为圆形,但整体形状和尺寸无法确定。高度无法估计。该物体的速度似乎快于F-47型飞机(可能指P-47"雷电"战斗机)。未报告有声音、发光、尾迹或结构细节。

**Tactics:** 该物体沿西南方向移动。未记录或说明其他战术机动。

**Note:** 评估分类为B-2级。该目击事件涉及来自诺伊比贝格AFB(美国占领德国期间的一个美国空军基地)的多名军方目击者。缺乏详细的观察者信息以及许多"N/S"(未说明)条目表明调查或报告不完整。

001_1948-10-31_Goose Bay, Labrador, Cana.report_summary:
**Witness:** A Ground Controlled Approach (GCA) radar operator at Goose Bay, Labrador detected an unknown target on PPI Scope Number 1 at 1545Z on 31 October 1948. The sighting was verified by two senior officers present in the unit at the time: Base Commander Colonel C. T. Jones and Group Commander Captain Verner, both of Newfoundland Base Command, Fort Pepperell, Newfoundland. The professional credentials of the observers—military radar operators and commanding officers—lend significant weight to the report.

**Sighting:** The radar target appeared approximately 3 miles south of Goose Bay airfield and was tracked traveling on a southwest heading. The object moved at an estimated speed of approximately 25 miles per hour, unusually slow for any conventional aircraft of the period. The target eventually disappeared into ground clutter at a distance of 6 miles from the radar installation.

**Object:** No visual observation accompanied the radar detection. The object's size, shape, altitude, color, luminosity, construction, and other physical characteristics could not be determined from the radar return alone. Duration of the sighting was not specified, though the object was tracked across at least 3 miles of distance.

**Tactics:** No tactical maneuvers were noted. The object maintained a steady southwest course at constant slow speed until lost in ground clutter.

**Note:** The extremely slow speed of 25 MPH is inconsistent with aircraft operations but could suggest a weather balloon, though the southwest trajectory and verification by senior officers warranted formal documentation as an unexplained incident.
001_1948-10-31_Goose Bay, Labrador, Cana.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 1948年10月31日1545Z时，加拿大拉布拉多古斯湾(Goose Bay, Labrador)的一名地面控制进场(GCA)雷达操作员在1号平面位置显示器(PPI)上探测到一个未知目标。该目击事件得到当时在该单位的两名高级军官的证实:基地指挥官C. T. Jones上校和大队指挥官Verner上尉,两人均来自纽芬兰佩珀雷尔堡(Fort Pepperell, Newfoundland)纽芬兰基地司令部。观察者的专业资质——军用雷达操作员和指挥官——为该报告增添了重要的可信度。

**Sighting:** 雷达目标出现在古斯湾机场以南约3英里处,被追踪到向西南方向移动。该物体以估计约每小时25英里的速度移动,对于当时任何常规飞行器而言都异常缓慢。目标最终在距雷达装置6英里处消失于地面杂波中。

**Object:** 雷达探测未伴随任何目视观测。仅从雷达回波无法确定该物体的大小、形状、高度、颜色、光度、构造及其他物理特征。目击持续时间未具体说明,但该物体至少被追踪了3英里的距离。

**Tactics:** 未观察到战术机动。该物体保持稳定的西南航向和恒定的低速移动,直至消失于地面杂波中。

**Note:** 每小时25英里的极慢速度与飞行器操作不符,但可能暗示为气象气球,尽管如此,其西南飞行轨迹以及高级军官的证实使得此事件被正式记录为无法解释的事件。

001_1948-11-05_Richmond, Indiana_38_1436.report_summary:
**Witness:** Dale Stevens, sports editor for The Palladium-Item newspaper in Richmond, Indiana, observed a brilliant white light in the eastern sky. Stevens was alerted by two separate phone calls from citizens describing a light resembling a flare hanging from a parachute. His employer vouched for his honesty and sincerity, and Stevens was a member of the local Junior Chamber of Commerce.

**Sighting:** On 5 November 1948 at approximately 0435 hours, Stevens observed a stationary white light slightly south of east from The Palladium-Item building. The object remained in sight for 20 minutes (0435-0455). When first observed, the sky was clear with stars visible. Within the observation period, low clouds at approximately 1,000 feet moved in, causing the object to appear dimmer before obscuring it completely.

**Object:** The object appeared as a brilliant white, round light larger than a star (estimated 5 to 10 times the size of a normal star). It exhibited a flickering quality and luminosity resembling that of a brilliant star. The object remained completely stationary throughout the observation. Stevens lined it up with a building corner and detected no movement over several minutes. No sound or exhaust trail was observed.

**Tactics:** The object remained stationary in position throughout the 20-minute observation period. Stevens photographed it with time exposures from the building's upper roof.

**Note:** Professor David Telfair, astronomer at Earlham College, stated it could not have been a star. Military ordnance experts ruled out USAF parachute flares, which burn only 3-8 minutes maximum. Tow-type aerial flares were also dismissed as they are never dropped by parachute and consist of sequential 3-minute flares.
001_1948-11-05_Richmond, Indiana_38_1436.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 戴尔·史蒂文斯(Dale Stevens),印第安纳州里士满市(Richmond, Indiana)《帕拉第姆报》(The Palladium-Item)报社的体育编辑,在东方天空观察到一个明亮的白色光体。史蒂文斯是在接到两名市民分别打来的电话后被提醒注意的,这些市民描述该光体类似一枚挂在降落伞上的照明弹。他的雇主证实了他的诚实和真诚,史蒂文斯还是当地青年商会的成员。

**Sighting:** 1948年11月5日约0435时,史蒂文斯在《帕拉第姆报》大楼观察到一个静止的白色光体,位于正东方向稍偏南。该物体在视野中保持了20分钟(0435-0455)。首次观察时,天空晴朗,星星清晰可见。在观察期间,约1,000英尺高度的低云层移入,导致该物体显得更暗淡,最终完全遮蔽了它。

**Object:** 该物体呈现为明亮的白色圆形光体,比星星大(估计为正常星星大小的5到10倍)。它表现出闪烁特性,发光度类似于明亮的恒星。该物体在整个观察过程中完全静止不动。史蒂文斯将其与建筑物的一角对齐,在几分钟内未检测到任何移动。未观察到声音或尾迹。

**Tactics:** 该物体在整个20分钟观察期间保持位置静止。史蒂文斯在大楼顶层屋顶用长时间曝光对其进行了拍摄。

**Note:** 厄尔汉姆学院(Earlham College)的天文学家戴维·特尔费尔(David Telfair)教授表示,它不可能是一颗星星。军事军械专家排除了USAF降落伞照明弹的可能性,因为这种照明弹最多只能燃烧3-8分钟。拖曳式空中照明弹也被排除,因为它们从不通过降落伞投放,而是由连续的3分钟照明弹组成。

001_1948-10-31_Lajes Field, Azores, Port.report_summary:
**Witness:** Staff Sgt. Joseph J. Barnett (AF 13127245), U.S. Air Force, stationed at an Army Air Base in the Azores (APO 406, New York). Observer was on the ground at the time of sighting.

**Sighting:** On 31 October 1948 at approximately 0230Z (2:30 AM Zulu time), Barnett observed a single unidentified object overhead for 3 to 5 minutes. Weather conditions included 3 layers of strato-cumulus clouds at 2,500 feet, visibility of 15 miles, and southwest winds at 7-8 MPH.

**Object:** The object was described as flat and round in shape, pale yellow or light orange in color (specifically noted as "not blue-white"). No size estimate was provided. The object produced no sound and left no vapor trails. Its luminosity characteristics were not detailed.

**Tactics:** The object exhibited a distinctive "weaving" motion while maintaining an overall northerly course and constant altitude. Estimated speed was approximately 160 MPH. The object eventually disappeared behind cloud cover.

**Note:** The weaving flight pattern while maintaining course and altitude is a notable kinematic characteristic. The object's silent operation at relatively low speed (160 MPH) and lack of exhaust trails distinguish it from conventional aircraft of the era.
001_1948-10-31_Lajes Field, Azores, Port.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 美国空军上士约瑟夫·J·巴尼特(Joseph J. Barnett)(空军编号13127245),驻扎在亚速尔群岛(Azores)的陆军航空基地(APO 406, 纽约)。观察者在目击时位于地面。

**Sighting:** 1948年10月31日约0230Z时(祖鲁时间凌晨2:30),巴尼特在头顶上方观察到一个不明物体,持续3至5分钟。天气条件包括:2,500英尺高度有3层层积云,能见度15英里,西南风7-8英里/小时。

**Object:** 该物体被描述为扁平圆形,颜色为淡黄色或浅橙色(特别注明"不是蓝白色")。未提供尺寸估计。该物体无声响,无蒸汽尾迹。其发光特性未详细说明。

**Tactics:** 该物体表现出独特的"摇摆"运动,同时保持总体向北的航向和恒定高度。估计速度约为160英里/小时。该物体最终消失在云层后面。

**Note:** 在保持航向和高度的同时呈现摇摆飞行模式是一个值得注意的运动学特征。该物体以相对较低的速度(160英里/小时)静默运行且无排气尾迹,这使其区别于那个时代的常规飞行器。

001_1948-11-08_Newark, New Jersey_38_143.report_summary:
**Witness:** Edmund J. Cisek, a civilian dispatcher at Newark Air Force Base and former USAF Reserve Captain, observed the object from outside Hangar #7. He was a regular participant in Reserve flying activities and was described as "a very reliable employee, highly intelligent and of excellent character."

**Sighting:** At 1850 hours EST on 8 November 1948, during a clear, moonlit night, Cisek glanced toward the moon and perceived a pale luminous object race across the sky. The sighting lasted approximately one second or less before the object passed out of sight over another hangar. He observed approximately 75% of the object's flight path.

**Object:** The object appeared as a pale luminous disc, round with little or no depth (thickness), approximately the same relative diameter as the moon but only 1/3 its brightness. It maintained steady luminosity throughout its flight. The object produced no sound and left no exhaust trail. Its altitude was estimated at 5,000 to 6,000 feet.

**Tactics:** The object traveled from north-northwest in a comparatively horizontal arc toward the south-southeast. The peak of its arc was approximately 45° above the horizon to the west-southwest of the observer's position. Speed was estimated at 800 MPH, approximately 200 MPH faster than jet aircraft Cisek had observed making tactical approaches at 600 MPH.

**Note:** No commercial, private, or military aircraft were reported flying in the vicinity at the time. No reports were received regarding possible testing device releases in the area.
001_1948-11-08_Newark, New Jersey_38_143.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** Edmund J. Cisek，纽瓦克空军基地(Newark Air Force Base)的一名民间调度员，曾任美国空军预备役上尉(USAF Reserve Captain)，在7号机库(Hangar #7)外观察到该物体。他是预备役飞行活动的常规参与者，被描述为"一位非常可靠的员工，高度聪慧且品格优秀"。

**Sighting:** 1948年11月8日东部标准时间1850时，在一个晴朗、月光明亮的夜晚，Cisek瞥向月亮时察觉到一个苍白发光的物体掠过天空。目击持续时间约为一秒或更短，随后该物体飞越另一个机库后消失在视线之外。他观察到该物体飞行轨迹的约75%。

**Object:** 该物体呈现为苍白发光的圆盘状，圆形且几乎没有或完全没有厚度，相对直径与月亮大致相同，但亮度仅为月亮的1/3。在整个飞行过程中保持稳定的发光度。该物体没有产生声音，也没有留下尾迹。其高度估计为5,000至6,000英尺。

**Tactics:** 该物体从北-西北方向以相对水平的弧线飞向南-东南方向。其弧线的最高点位于观察者位置西-西南方向约45°仰角处。速度估计为800英里/小时，比Cisek曾观察到的以600英里/小时进行战术进场的喷气式飞机快约200英里/小时。

**Note:** 当时没有商业、私人或军用飞机报告在附近飞行。也未收到关于该区域可能进行测试装置释放的任何报告。

001_1948-11-06_Panama_38_143685_box7_inc.report_summary:
**Witness:** Weather observer Solera, Panama, during routine weather reporting duties at 1640 hours on 6 November 1948.

**Sighting:** At sunrise, Solera observed what appeared to be a comet in the southeast quadrant of the sky. The object remained visible to the naked eye for approximately 40 minutes until full sunrise obliterated it from view as sunlight dimmed the phenomenon's brilliance.

**Object:** Described as comet-like in appearance with a long cone of light terminating in a star-like point larger than the planet Venus. The tail exhibited approximately four grades of intensity. The luminosity was characterized as similar to that of a comet.

**Tactics:** No unusual maneuvers noted; object appeared stationary or moved consistently with celestial bodies.

**Note:** The report includes important corroborating astronomical data. On 6 November 1948 (5 November U.S. time), Dr. Harley Wood, astronomer in Sydney, Australia, recognized a new and extraordinary comet with a tail extending 15 million miles. Three days later, early risers in southern and western U.S. observed the same celestial body. The comet was moving at approximately 128,000 mph, close to but away from the sun, and was visible for brief periods before being obscured by sunlight. The investigating officer recommended submission to Dr. J. Allen Hynek to determine whether Solera's observation and the documented comet were the same object. This incident represents a likely astronomical explanation.
001_1948-11-06_Panama_38_143685_box7_inc.report_summary_zh:
**Witness:** 气象观测员索莱拉，巴拿马，1948年11月6日1640时执行常规天气报告任务期间。

**Sighting:** 日出时分，索莱拉在天空东南象限观测到一个类似彗星的物体。该物体在肉眼可见状态下持续了大约40分钟，直到日出完全遮蔽了它——阳光使这一现象的亮度变暗而无法观测。

**Object:** 描述为彗星状外观，带有一条长锥形光带，末端呈星状点，比金星更大。尾部呈现出大约四个等级的亮度。其光度特征类似于彗星。

**Tactics:** 未发现异常机动；物体呈现静止状态或与天体的运动一致。

**Note:** 该报告包含重要的佐证天文数据。1948年11月6日（美国时间11月5日），澳大利亚悉尼的天文学家哈雷·伍德博士发现了一颗新的非凡彗星，其尾部延伸达1500万英里。三天后，美国南部和西部的早起者观测到了同一天体。该彗星以大约每小时128,000英里的速度运动，靠近太阳但正在远离，在被阳光遮蔽前只能在短暂时间内可见。调查官员建议将此案提交给J·艾伦·海尼克博士，以确定索莱拉的观测与记录在案的彗星是否为同一物体。该事件很可能有天文学解释。

001_1947-07-04_Vancouver, Washington_38_.report_summary:
**Witness:** John Sullivan, Sheriff's Deputy, along with fellow deputies Clarence McKay and Fred Krives, observed from Vancouver, Washington (on the ground). Account noted as corroborated.

**Sighting:** On July 4, 1947 at 1:05 PM (1305), the deputies heard a Portland police radio broadcast and ran out of the Sheriff's office to look at the sky. The objects were located over Portland, approximately 3 to 5 miles away from their position.

**Object:** Between 20 to 30 objects observed in "V" shaped formation, described as "like a flight of geese." The objects produced a low humming sound. Time in sight, altitude, speed, direction of flight, size, and color were not specified in the report.

**Characteristics:** No exhaust trails, sketches, or photographs documented. Weather conditions and effects on clouds not specified.

**Disappearance:** Manner of disappearance not specified in the report.
001_1947-07-04_Vancouver, Washington_38_.report_summary_zh:
**目击者:** 约翰·沙利文(John Sullivan),警长副手,与同事克拉伦斯·麦凯(Clarence McKay)和弗雷德·克里夫斯(Fred Krives)一同在华盛顿州温哥华(地面)进行观察。记录注明为经证实的报告。

**目击经过:** 1947年7月4日下午1:05(1305时),副警长们听到波特兰警察广播后跑出警长办公室观察天空。物体位于波特兰上空,距离他们的位置约3至5英里。

**物体描述:** 观察到20至30个物体呈"V"字形编队,被描述为"像一群飞雁"。物体发出低沉的嗡嗡声。报告中未指明目视时间、高度、速度、飞行方向、大小和颜色。

**特征:** 未记录尾迹、草图或照片。未指明天气条件和对云层的影响。

**消失方式:** 报告中未指明消失方式。

001_1947-07-08_Muroc Army Air Field, Cal.report_summary:
**Witness:** Major Richard R. Shoop, employed in Office of Chief of Technical Engineering Division, stationed at Muroc Army Air Field, California. Observation brought to attention of Col. Gilkey.

**Sighting:** Occurred approximately noon on July 8, 1947, from ground position at Muroc Army Air Field. Object remained visible for eight (8) minutes at a distance of five (5) to eight (8) miles to the north.

**Object:** Single unconventional-shaped object, approximately the size of a pursuit airplane. Described as having an aluminum colored, apparently metallic surface that reflected sunlight. Object was at a fairly high altitude initially.

**Flight Characteristics:** Moved slowly northward with distinctive oscillating motion. Object descended from intermediate altitude in oscillating fashion, almost reaching the surface of the ground, then started climbing again.

**Disappearance:** Moved off slowly in the distance until no longer visible.

**Additional Details:** No sound reported. No exhaust trails mentioned. Weather conditions not stated. No sketches or photographs available.
001_1947-07-08_Muroc Army Air Field, Cal.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** Richard R. Shoop少校，技术工程部主任办公室雇员，驻扎在加利福尼亚州穆罗克陆军航空基地。观察结果已报告给Gilkey上校。

**目击经过：** 1947年7月8日约正午时分发生，目击者在穆罗克陆军航空基地地面位置观察。物体在北方5至8英里处可见，持续时间为8分钟。

**物体描述：** 单个非常规形状物体，大约相当于一架追击机的大小。描述为具有铝色、明显为金属表面，反射阳光。物体最初处于相当高的高度。

**飞行特征：** 缓慢向北移动，具有独特的振荡运动。物体以振荡方式从中等高度下降，几乎到达地面，然后再次开始爬升。

**消失方式：** 缓慢移动至远处直至不再可见。

**其他细节：** 未报告声音。未提及排气尾迹。未说明天气状况。无草图或照片。

001_1947-07-08_Rogers Dry Lake, Californ.report_summary:
**Witness:** Captain John Paul Strapp, Flight Test officer stationed at Muroc Army Air Field, California. Four of five people in the observation truck witnessed the object, including Mr. Lenz, a civilian from Wright Field, Dayton, Ohio.

**Sighting:** On July 8, 1947 at 11:50, Captain Strapp was sitting in an observation truck at Area #3, Rogers Dry Lake, watching a formation of two P-82s and an A-26 aircraft at 20,000 feet preparing for a seat ejection experiment. The object was in sight for approximately 90 seconds.

**Object:** The object initially resembled a parachute canopy, appearing white aluminum/silvery in color. As it descended and its lateral silhouette became visible, it presented a distinct ovular outline approximately 25-50 feet in size. Two projections on the upper surface, possibly thick fins or knobs, crossed each other at intervals suggesting rotation or oscillation of a slow type. The object appeared less dense than a parachute canopy and resembled aluminum painted fabric.

**Behavior:** The object was observed at an altitude lower than 20,000 feet, falling at three times the rate of a parachute that ejected 30 minutes later. It drifted slightly north of due west against the prevailing wind toward Mount Wilson. Horizontal speed appeared slower than maximum velocity of an F-80 aircraft. No smoke, flames, propeller arcs, engine noise, or other visible means of propulsion were noted.

**Disappearance:** The object dropped to a level where it came into the line of vision of the mountain tops and was lost from sight.

**Assessment:** Captain Strapp believed it was a man-made object based on its distinct outline and functional appearance. He thought its path suggested it might have been dropped from a great height. He specifically stated this was not a hallucination.
001_1947-07-08_Rogers Dry Lake, Californ.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 约翰·保罗·斯特拉普上尉（Captain John Paul Strapp），飞行测试官员，驻扎在加利福尼亚州穆罗克陆军航空基地。观察卡车内五人中有四人目击了该物体，包括来自俄亥俄州代顿莱特机场的平民伦茨先生（Mr. Lenz）。

**目击经过：** 1947年7月8日11:50，斯特拉普上尉坐在罗杰斯干湖3号区域的观察卡车内，正在观察两架P-82和一架A-26飞机在20,000英尺高度编队飞行，准备进行弹射座椅实验。该物体在视线中停留了约90秒。

**物体描述：** 物体最初类似降落伞伞盖，呈白色铝质/银色。当它下降并显现出侧面轮廓时，呈现出明显的椭圆形轮廓，大小约25-50英尺。上表面有两个突起物，可能是厚鳍或圆钮，它们周期性地交叉，表明物体在缓慢旋转或摆动。物体看起来比降落伞伞盖密度小，类似涂有铝漆的织物。

**行为特征：** 物体被观察到的高度低于20,000英尺，下降速度是30分钟后弹射降落伞速度的三倍。它逆着主导风向略微向正西偏北方向漂移，朝向威尔逊山。水平速度似乎慢于F-80飞机的最大速度。未观察到烟雾、火焰、螺旋桨弧光、发动机噪音或其他可见的推进装置。

**消失方式：** 物体下降到与山顶视线齐平的高度后从视野中消失。

**评估：** 斯特拉普上尉认为这是人造物体，基于其清晰的轮廓和功能性外观。他认为其飞行路径表明可能是从极高处投放的。他特别声明这不是幻觉。

001_1947-07-04_West Trenton, New Jersey_.report_summary:
**Witness:** Miss Marion Marshall, employed at WINJ Western Electric, Trenton, New Jersey. Occupation not stated.

**Sighting:** On July 4, 1947 at 11:45 p.m., the witness observed a flying object while standing on the southbound platform of the West Trenton station of the Reading railroad. The sighting occurred under bright moonlight conditions.

**Object:** A single luminous object described as a "flying saucer" traveling east over West Trenton at high altitude and fast speed. The object was self-luminous with no tail or halo visible. No exhaust trails were observed.

**Flight Characteristics:** The object traveled in an easterly direction over West Trenton at high altitude and fast speed. Distance from observer, time in sight, tactics, sound, size, apparent construction, and manner of disappearance were not stated.

**Additional Details:** Weather conditions were clear with bright moonlight. No sketches or photographs were obtained. No odor was detected and no effect on clouds was noted.
001_1947-07-04_West Trenton, New Jersey_.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** Marion Marshall小姐，受雇于新泽西州特伦顿WINJ西方电气公司。职业未说明。

**目击经过：** 1947年7月4日晚上11:45，目击者站在雷丁铁路西特伦顿站南行站台上时观察到一个飞行物体。目击时月光明亮。

**物体描述：** 单个发光物体，被描述为"飞碟"，向东飞越西特伦顿上空，高度很高，速度很快。物体自发光，没有尾迹或光晕。未观察到排气尾迹。

**飞行特征：** 物体向东方向飞越西特伦顿上空，高度很高，速度很快。与目击者的距离、视野停留时间、战术动作、声音、大小、明显构造和消失方式均未说明。

**其他细节：** 天气状况晴朗，月光明亮。未获得素描或照片。未检测到气味，未注意到对云层的影响。

001_1946-12-15_Northern Arizona, Route 6.report_summary:
**Witness:** K. D. Wood, Professor and Head of Aeronautical Engineering at University of Colorado, Boulder, Colorado.

**Sighting:** Observed early morning during a flight trip through the southwest along Route 66 in northern Arizona. Mid-December 1946.

**Object:** Did not observe the object itself. One vapor trail observed.

**Trail Characteristics:** White, heavy vapor trail described as resembling rocket or jet exhaust. Distinctly different from usual jet airplane trails.

**Flight Pattern:** Trail first appeared vertical, then proceeded west to east overhead. No maneuvers observed.

**Altitude and Speed:** Estimated between 20,000 feet to 50,000 feet altitude. Speed estimated at 600 mph, ± 200 mph.

**Sound:** None detected.

**Weather:** Clear conditions.

**Remarks:** Observer only saw the vapor trail and did not observe the object creating it. The professional background of the witness as an aeronautical engineering professor gives credibility to his assessment that the trail was unusual and unlike conventional jet aircraft exhaust.
001_1946-12-15_Northern Arizona, Route 6.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** K. D. Wood，科罗拉多大学博尔德分校航空工程系教授兼系主任。

**目击经过：** 1946年12月中旬清晨，在穿越西南部的飞行旅途中，沿亚利桑那州北部66号公路观察到。

**物体：** 未观察到物体本身。观察到一条蒸气尾迹。

**尾迹特征：** 白色、浓重的蒸气尾迹，被描述为类似火箭或喷气发动机排气。与通常的喷气式飞机尾迹明显不同。

**飞行模式：** 尾迹首先呈垂直方向出现，然后从西向东从头顶上方通过。未观察到机动动作。

**高度和速度：** 估计高度在20,000英尺至50,000英尺之间。速度估计为600英里/小时，误差±200英里/小时。

**声音：** 未检测到。

**天气：** 晴朗条件。

**备注：** 观察者仅看到蒸气尾迹，未观察到产生尾迹的物体。目击者作为航空工程教授的专业背景使其评估具有可信度，即该尾迹不寻常且不同于常规喷气式飞机的排气。

001_1947-07-07_Phoenix, Arizona_38_14368.report_summary:
**Witness:** William Albert Rhodes, residing at 4333 N. 14th St., Phoenix, Arizona. Occupation not stated.

**Sighting:** On July 7, 1947 at 1600 hours, Rhodes observed a single unidentified object from coordinates 33° 27' N, 112° 3' W in Phoenix, Arizona. The object remained in view for an unspecified duration. Weather conditions included cumulus clouds.

**Object:** The object appeared elliptical in shape with a diameter of 20-30 feet and grey in color, making it difficult to perceive against the clouds. The object had what appeared to be a cockpit canopy in the center extending toward the back and beneath, visible with the naked eye but not protruding from the surface. The tail had two points on the outside area. The craft demonstrated an excellent airfoil, tapered from wing tip to wing tip, with no discernible landing gears or propellers. The object did not revolve on its own axis.

**Flight Characteristics:** The object was first observed at approximately 5,000 feet traveling at 400-600 MPH from northeast to west. It spiraled down from 5,000 feet to 2,000 feet, making two left-to-right circles with an approximate radius of 1/4 to 1/2 miles, then ascended at a 45° angle.

**Sound:** A jet-like noise was heard prior to the object's appearance, but no audible sound was produced while it remained in view. Rhodes speculated that 10-15 MPH wind velocity causing rustling tree leaves might have made it impossible to hear any noise from the object.

**Documentation:** Rhodes successfully took two photographs - one at the object's lowest point (about 2,000 feet) and another as it turned out of its second spiral and started upward.

**Observer Notes:** Rhodes initially thought the object was the Navy's new "Flapjack Plane" but altered his opinion since the object had no landing gears or propellers, which the Navy ship possessed.
001_1947-07-07_Phoenix, Arizona_38_14368.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** William Albert Rhodes，居住在亚利桑那州凤凰城北14街4333号。职业未说明。

**目击经过：** 1947年7月7日16时，Rhodes在亚利桑那州凤凰城北纬33° 27'、西经112° 3'的位置观察到一个不明物体。物体在视野中停留的具体时长未说明。天气状况包括积云。

**物体特征：** 物体呈椭圆形，直径20-30英尺，灰色，使其在云层中难以察觉。物体中部有一个看似驾驶舱的舱盖，向后和底部延伸，肉眼可见但不从表面突出。尾部外侧区域有两个尖点。飞行器展现出优秀的翼型，从翼尖到翼尖逐渐变细，没有可辨认的起落架或螺旋桨。物体没有绕自身轴线旋转。

**飞行特征：** 物体首次被观察到时位于约5,000英尺高度，以400-600英里/小时的速度从东北向西飞行。它从5,000英尺盘旋下降到2,000英尺，进行了两次从左到右的圆周运动，半径约1/4到1/2英里，然后以45°角上升。

**声音：** 在物体出现之前听到类似喷气式飞机的噪音，但在物体保持在视野内时没有听到声音。Rhodes推测10-15英里/小时的风速导致树叶沙沙作响，可能使他无法听到物体发出的任何噪音。

**记录文档：** Rhodes成功拍摄了两张照片——一张在物体最低点（约2,000英尺）拍摄，另一张在它从第二次盘旋转出并开始上升时拍摄。

**目击者评论：** Rhodes最初认为该物体是海军的新型"煎饼飞机"，但后来改变了看法，因为该物体没有起落架或螺旋桨，而海军飞机具有这些装置。

001_1947-07-01_Oakland, California_38_14.report_summary:
**Incident:** #52

**Witness:** Capt Ryherd and Lt Ward Stewart observed two unidentified aerial objects. Note indicates Capt Ryherd showed extreme sincerity throughout the interview.

**Sighting:** The objects were traveling at approximately 8,000 to 10,000 ft altitude, above a P-80 aircraft. They were observed until they disappeared in flight, presumably over Oakland headed toward the ocean. Weather conditions were clear.

**Object:** The objects were estimated to be possibly 15 to 25 feet in diameter. They were circular in shape, described as "like a ball on the bottom but not completely round." The first object flew straight and level. The second object flew close behind the first at the same altitude, appearing to move from left to right and right to left, described as moving "more like a guard than a leading aircraft."

**Sound/Trail:** Due to the noise of the P-80, no sound could be heard from the objects. They did not leave any vapor, smoke, or visible trail.
001_1947-07-01_Oakland, California_38_14.report_summary_zh:
**事件编号：** #52

**目击者：** Ryherd上尉和Ward Stewart中尉观察到两个不明飞行物体。备注指出Ryherd上尉在整个访谈过程中表现出极度的真诚。

**目击经过：** 这些物体在大约8,000至10,000英尺高度飞行，位于一架P-80飞机上方。目击者一直观察它们直到消失，推测是在奥克兰上空朝海洋方向飞去。天气状况晴朗。

**物体特征：** 物体估计直径可能为15至25英尺。形状为圆形，描述为"底部像球但不完全圆"。第一个物体直线水平飞行。第二个物体紧跟在第一个后面，在相同高度飞行，表现出从左到右再从右到左的移动，被描述为"更像护卫而非领航飞行器"的运动方式。

**声音/尾迹：** 由于P-80的噪音，无法听到物体发出的任何声音。它们没有留下任何蒸汽、烟雾或可见尾迹。

001_1948-01-07_Wilmington, Ohio_38_14368.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Six U.S. Air Force personnel at Clinton County Air Base: Gale F. Walter, James Hudson, M/Sgt Irvin H. Lewis, S/Sgt John P. Haag, Sgt Harold E. Olvis, and T/Sgt LeRoy Ziegler. Observers included control tower operators and four members of the alert crew.

**Sighting:** Observed between 7:20 and 7:55 P.M. (35 minutes total) from the Clinton County Air Base Control Tower.

**Object:** Single red cone-shaped object with appearance of "fire" trailing a gaseous green mist. Size, distance, and altitude not specified.

**Behavior:** The object hung suspended in the air at intervals, then gained and lost altitude at seemingly terrific bursts of speed. General direction of flight was southwest. The intense brightness pierced through a heavy layer of clouds passing intermittently over the area and obscured other celestial phenomena. Object eventually disappeared over the horizon.

**Weather Conditions:** Heavy layer of clouds present.

**Related Incidents:** Project SIGN notes reference an unnamed comet expected in the northern hemisphere around January 1, 1948. The report cross-references multiple related incidents (48a-d, 33a-f, 30, 32). A corroborating report from Danville, Kentucky on January 9, 1948 described Mr. & Mrs. Markham observing a pencil-like object flying very high with a long trail that turned into a fireworks display of sparks.
001_1948-01-07_Wilmington, Ohio_38_14368.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 克林顿县空军基地的六名美国空军人员：Gale F. Walter、James Hudson、一级军士长Irvin H. Lewis、二级军士长John P. Haag、中士Harold E. Olvis和技术军士长LeRoy Ziegler。观察者包括控制塔操作员和四名警戒机组成员。

**目击经过：** 晚上7:20至7:55之间从克林顿县空军基地控制塔观察到（总计35分钟）。

**物体特征：** 单个红色锥形物体，外观似"火焰"，拖曳着气态绿色薄雾。尺寸、距离和高度未指明。

**行为表现：** 物体时而悬停在空中，然后以看似极快的速度爆发上升和下降高度。总体飞行方向为西南方。其强烈的亮度穿透了间歇性经过该地区的厚重云层，并遮蔽了其他天体现象。物体最终在地平线上消失。

**天气条件：** 存在厚重云层。

**相关事件：** 蓝皮书计划注释提到1948年1月1日左右预计在北半球出现的一颗未命名彗星。报告交叉引用了多个相关事件（48a-d、33a-f、30、32）。1948年1月9日来自肯塔基州丹维尔的佐证报告描述Markham夫妇观察到一个铅笔状物体在高空飞行，拖着长长的尾迹，随后变成烟火般的火花展示。

001_1947-10-20_Dayton, Ohio_38_143685_bo.report_summary:
**Witness:** S. C. Britton, resident of David Road, Dayton, Ohio. The witness was strolling in his orchard when his grandson called his attention to "the funny flying fishes in the sky." The witness was familiar with aircraft as they flew over his property daily.

**Sighting:** On October 20, 1947, at 1:20 PM, two strange-looking craft were observed from the ground at David Road, Dayton, Ohio. Weather conditions were CAVU (Ceiling And Visibility Unlimited) with cloudless skies. The sun was to the observer's right, causing the objects to reflect sunlight brilliantly.

**Objects:** Two cigar-shaped objects, longer than they were wide, with no visible wings. The objects reflected light brilliantly in the sunlight, making the exact shape difficult to discern clearly. Size was not specified.

**Flight Characteristics:** The objects flew very fast in a very straight course from west to east, slightly to the north. One object followed about a city block behind and to the right of the leading object. They maintained formation without dipping or veering. Altitude estimated between 1 to 5 miles high. No sound was heard.

**Exhaust:** An unusual trail was observed that seemed like a slight trace of steam attached to the objects, which disappeared immediately. It did not persist like vapor trails from ordinary planes or jet aircraft.

**Assessment:** Witness was positive the objects were not meteors, birds, or ordinary aircraft. Subsequent investigation by the Command indicated Mr. Britton's testimony should be considered reliable. Objects remained unidentified.
001_1947-10-20_Dayton, Ohio_38_143685_bo.report_summary_zh:
**目击者:** S. C. Britton，俄亥俄州代顿市大卫路居民。目击者在果园散步时，他的孙子提醒他注意"天空中有趣的飞鱼"。目击者熟悉飞机，因为飞机每天都会飞过他的房产。

**目击经过:** 1947年10月20日下午1点20分，在俄亥俄州代顿市大卫路地面观察到两个奇怪的飞行器。天气条件为CAVU（云高和能见度无限制），天空无云。太阳在观察者右侧，使物体反射阳光非常明亮。

**物体特征:** 两个雪茄形物体，长度大于宽度，没有可见的机翼。物体在阳光下反射明亮的光线，使精确形状难以清晰辨认。未说明尺寸。

**飞行特征:** 物体以非常快的速度沿从西向东、略向北的方向笔直飞行。一个物体在前导物体后方约一个街区距离，并位于其右侧。它们保持编队飞行，没有下沉或偏离。高度估计在1到5英里之间。没有听到声音。

**尾迹:** 观察到不寻常的尾迹，看起来像是附着在物体上的轻微蒸汽痕迹，立即消失。它不像普通飞机或喷气式飞机的蒸汽尾迹那样持续存在。

**评估:** 目击者确信这些物体不是流星、鸟类或普通飞机。该司令部随后的调查表明，Britton先生的证词应被视为可靠。物体仍未确认身份。

001_1947-07-20_Near Sidney, Newfoundland.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Messrs Maitland, Larkin, Douglas, and Hamilton, occupation and address listed as "with above-named concern" (details illegible).

**Sighting:** Observed on 20 July 1947 at 0015Z while traveling from Nova Scotia to Port aux Basques, Newfoundland, approximately one hour from Sidney, Newfoundland.

**Object:** The object itself was not seen. Witnesses observed 4 or 5 flashes, each approximately 1 second apart and equidistant from each other. Flashes were silvery to red in color. The phenomenon appeared at 30° off the horizon at an estimated 1/4 mile range.

**Flight Characteristics:** Moved in horizontal flight at high velocity, described as faster than a tracer bullet. Direction of travel was NNE (30° East of true North). No sound reported.

**Weather:** Clear and dark conditions.

**Remarks:** The report notes that what was observed was possibly itself a rocket charge. No sketches or photographs available. Size, shape, odor, exhaust trails, effect on clouds, and manner of disappearance not stated.
001_1947-07-20_Near Sidney, Newfoundland.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** Maitland、Larkin、Douglas和Hamilton先生，职业和地址列为"与上述机构"（详细信息不清楚）。

**目击经过：** 1947年7月20日0015Z时，在从新斯科舍省前往纽芬兰巴斯克港途中观察到，距离纽芬兰西德尼约一小时路程。

**物体：** 未看到物体本身。目击者观察到4或5次闪光，每次间隔约1秒且等距分布。闪光颜色为银色至红色。该现象出现在地平线上方30°，估计距离1/4英里。

**飞行特征：** 水平飞行，高速移动，被描述为比曳光弹更快。飞行方向为北东北（真北以东30°）。未报告声音。

**天气：** 晴朗黑暗的条件。

**备注：** 报告指出所观察到的可能本身就是火箭装药。无草图或照片。未说明大小、形状、气味、尾迹、对云的影响以及消失方式。

001_1947-07-13_Snake River Canyon near T.report_summary:
**Witness:** A. C. Urie (farmer) and his two sons, Kenneth and Billy (age 10), observed the object from Snake River Canyon near Twin Falls, Idaho.

**Sighting:** On July 13, 1947, at 0900 hours, Urie sent his sons to the river to retrieve tools from his boat. As they climbed back up the trail, Urie observed through a break in the trees a sky-blue object silhouetted against the steep canyon walls on the far side. The canyon was approximately 400 feet deep and 1200 feet across at that location. Billy saw it almost immediately after his father. The sighting was momentary, lasting only moments before the object disappeared behind a hill.

**Object:** The object was described as 20 feet in diameter and 10 feet thick, shaped like a broad-rimmed hat with a low crown or an inverted plate. It was sky-blue in color, which Urie stated would probably not be noticed against the sky. The object had a red tubular fiery glow (exhaust flame) at the rear and made a swishing sound.

**Flight Characteristics:** The object traveled from east to west at approximately 75 feet above the canyon floor (300 feet below the canyon rim and 300 feet from the observers). It followed the contours of the ground, passing up and down over hills and hollows of the canyon. Urie stated "it did not spin like a top." Notably, trees over which it passed almost directly did not bend with wind as if a plane had gone by, but instead spun around on top as if they were in a vacuum.

**Agent's Assessment:** Urie seemed completely sincere about the incident and the boys stated they had never before seen one of the discs. One sketch was provided.
001_1947-07-13_Snake River Canyon near T.report_summary_zh:
**目击者:** A. C. Urie(农民)和他的两个儿子Kenneth和Billy(10岁)在爱达荷州双瀑布附近的蛇河峡谷观察到该物体。

**目击经过:** 1947年7月13日上午9点,Urie派儿子们去河边从船上取工具。当他们爬回小路时,Urie透过树木的间隙观察到一个天蓝色物体,在对面陡峭的峡谷壁上形成剪影。峡谷在该位置约400英尺深,1200英尺宽。Billy在他父亲之后几乎立即看到了它。目击时间很短,仅持续片刻,物体就消失在山丘后面。

**物体特征:** 物体被描述为直径20英尺、厚10英尺,形状像宽边帽配低帽冠或倒置的盘子。颜色为天蓝色,Urie表示这种颜色在天空背景下可能不会被注意到。物体后部有红色管状火焰光芒(排气火焰),发出嗖嗖声。

**飞行特征:** 物体从东向西飞行,距峡谷底部约75英尺(距峡谷边缘下方300英尺,距观察者300英尺)。它沿着地面轮廓飞行,上下越过峡谷的山丘和凹地。Urie表示"它不像陀螺那样旋转"。值得注意的是,它几乎直接飞过的树木并未像飞机经过时那样随风弯曲,而是在顶部旋转,仿佛处于真空中。

**调查员评估:** Urie对该事件似乎完全真诚,孩子们表示他们以前从未见过飞碟。提供了一张草图。

001_1947-07-03_South Brooksville, Maine_.report_summary:
**Witness:** Mr. John F. Cole of South Brooksville, Maine observed the incident in the vicinity of Harborside, Maine.

**Sighting:** At 1930 hours (7:30 PM) on July 3, 1947, an unusually loud roar attracted the observer's attention. Upon looking up, he saw a group of very light-colored objects at an altitude of approximately 50° elevation angle, bunched rather closely with no regular formation. The sun was behind the observer at the time.

**Objects:** Approximately 10 objects were observed. The group covered an estimated angular diameter of 1-1/2° in the sky and appeared to be moving irregularly, like a swarm of bees. Individual objects were estimated to be 50 to 100 feet wide. The only concrete evidence of form appeared on the left tangent of the group—two dark shaped forms that could have been tail wings.

**Movement:** The group traveled through approximately 30° of arc in an estimated 10 to 15 seconds. Based on geometric calculations assuming various distances and sizes, the witness estimated speed at 900-1200 MPH. The objects proceeded with no regular formation.

**Sound:** A loud roar was heard, which suggested to the witness that the objects may have been much closer and rather small than initially estimated.

**Analysis:** The witness noted the unusual characteristics: irregular formation like a swarm of bees, yet only two objects showed evidence of wings. One plane towing multiple cones would have been easily recognized, ruling out that explanation.
001_1947-07-03_South Brooksville, Maine_.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 缅因州南布鲁克斯维尔的约翰·F·科尔先生在缅因州哈伯赛德附近观察到此事件。

**目击经过：** 1947年7月3日1930时（晚上7:30），一阵异常响亮的轰鸣声引起了观察者的注意。抬头望去，他看到一组浅色物体，仰角约50°，相当密集地聚在一起，没有规则的编队。当时太阳在观察者身后。

**物体描述：** 观察到大约10个物体。该群体在天空中覆盖的角直径估计为1-1/2°，似乎像一群蜜蜂一样不规则地移动。单个物体估计宽度为50至100英尺。唯一具体的形状证据出现在群体的左侧切线处——两个深色形状，可能是尾翼。

**运动特征：** 该群体在估计10至15秒内穿过约30°弧。根据假设不同距离和尺寸的几何计算，目击者估计速度为900-1200英里/小时。物体没有规则编队地前进。

**声音：** 听到响亮的轰鸣声，这使目击者认为物体可能比最初估计的更近且更小。

**分析：** 目击者注意到不寻常的特征：像蜂群一样的不规则编队，但只有两个物体显示出机翼的证据。一架飞机拖曳多个锥体很容易被识别，排除了这种解释。

001_1947-09-12_Necker Island, Pacific Oc.report_summary:
**Witness:** Captain Stanley S. Griffin (Pilot) and 2nd Officer Edward B. Polhemus, Pan American Airways (PAA), observed from eastbound aircraft flying from Midway Island to USA.

**Sighting:** At 0558 GCT (45 minutes after sunset), approximately 23 minutes after passing Necker Island (23° 34' N, 164° 40' W), an intense white light was observed 60° off the starboard bow. The sighting lasted six seconds total.

**Object:** Single object initially appeared as an extremely intense white light, similar to an approaching aircraft but far brighter. The light color resembled an incandescent lamp without appreciable blue or reddish tinge. The object was initially traveling on course approximately 350° true at an estimated distance of 5 miles, closing to approximately 1 mile off the starboard bow.

**Behavior:** When the PAA plane switched from automatic to manual control, the object abruptly veered to an approximate course of 109°. During the course change, the bright white light split into two parts and assumed a reddish hue. The twin reddish lights appeared about a wing-length apart but were less intense than the original white light. The object maintained horizontal flight at constant altitude of 9,500-10,000 feet throughout the observation, never rising above or dropping below this level. It far outraced the PAA plane (traveling at 205 knots) at an estimated speed of 1,000 knots (1,160 MPH).

**Disappearance:** The twin reddish lights appeared to burn out approximately 30 miles ahead of the PAA aircraft, still maintaining the same altitude.

**Weather:** Dark conditions with cumulus clouds at 3,000 feet with 0.4 density. The object gave off insufficient illumination to reflect on the cloud formation below.

**Analysis:** Both observers considered the possibility of a meteor but rejected this explanation due to the object's ability to maintain constant altitude throughout the observation. When questioned about optical illusion or the possibility the object dropped at an oblique angle, both observers firmly maintained the object appeared to change course horizontally and hold altitude. The PAA plane was at 9,000 feet on magnetic course 98° (approximately 110° true) flying on automatic pilot at the time of initial observation.
001_1947-09-12_Necker Island, Pacific Oc.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 泛美航空公司（PAA）机长Stanley S. Griffin和副驾驶Edward B. Polhemus，从中途岛飞往美国的东行航班上观察到。

**目击经过：** 格林尼治标准时间0558（日落后45分钟），在飞越内克尔岛（北纬23° 34'，西经164° 40'）约23分钟后，在右舷前方60°处观察到一个强烈的白光。整个目击过程持续了6秒钟。

**物体描述：** 单一物体最初表现为极其强烈的白光，类似于接近的飞机但亮度要强得多。光色类似白炽灯，没有明显的蓝色或红色色调。物体最初以大约350°真航向飞行，估计距离5英里，接近到右舷前方约1英里处。

**行为特征：** 当泛美飞机从自动驾驶切换到手动控制时，物体突然转向约109°航向。在转向过程中，明亮的白光分裂成两部分并呈现红色色调。两个红色光点看起来相距约一个翼展长度，但强度低于原来的白光。物体在整个观察过程中保持9,500-10,000英尺的恒定高度水平飞行，从未高于或低于这个高度。它远远超过了泛美飞机的速度（205节），估计速度为1,000节（1,160英里/小时）。

**消失方式：** 两个红色光点在泛美飞机前方约30英里处似乎熄灭，仍然保持相同的高度。

**天气状况：** 黑暗环境，3,000英尺高度有0.4密度的积云。物体发出的光照不足以在下方云层上产生反射。

**分析：** 两位观察者都考虑过流星的可能性，但由于物体在整个观察过程中保持恒定高度而排除了这一解释。当被问及光学错觉或物体以倾斜角度下降的可能性时，两位观察者坚定地认为物体似乎是水平改变航向并保持高度。观察时泛美飞机正以磁航向98°（约110°真航向）在9,000英尺高度自动驾驶飞行。

001_1947-07-07_Hickam Field, Hawaii_38_1.report_summary:
**Witness:** Mr. Daniel Saito, employed in the Air Communications Section at Hickam Field, Hawaii. Contactable at Hickam Field.

**Sighting:** On July 7, 1947, at 0900 hours, Mr. Saito's attention was attracted to a flashing object in the sky near Hickam Village #2. He observed the object for several minutes before losing sight of it among the clouds.

**Object:** The object appeared to be a large balloon with a silver disc (not a parachute) suspended from it. Although no cable connecting the two objects was visible, Saito assumed they were attached because they maintained the same distance apart and moved in unison. The object was spherical in shape with silver coloring.

**Behavior:** The object was at approximately 6,000 feet altitude and slowly ascending. It moved in a northwesterly direction toward the sea. The silver disc attachment flashed on and off, which Saito attributed to the rays of the sun striking it as it revolved.

**Disappearance:** After watching for a few minutes, Saito discontinued observation. When he attempted to locate the object again, he could not do so owing to cloudy weather conditions.

**Assessment:** The description suggests a weather balloon or similar atmospheric device with attached equipment.
001_1947-07-07_Hickam Field, Hawaii_38_1.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** Daniel Saito先生，夏威夷希卡姆机场航空通信部门雇员。可在希卡姆机场联系。

**目击经过：** 1947年7月7日上午0900时，Saito先生的注意力被希卡姆村2号附近天空中一个闪光物体吸引。他观察该物体数分钟后在云层中失去视线。

**物体描述：** 该物体看起来像一个大型气球，悬挂着一个银色圆盘（不是降落伞）。虽然看不见连接两个物体的缆绳，但Saito认为它们是连接在一起的，因为它们保持相同距离并似乎同步移动。物体呈球形，银色。

**行为特征：** 物体位于约6,000英尺高度，缓慢上升。向西北方向朝海面移动。银色圆盘附件闪烁明灭，Saito将此归因于旋转时阳光照射。

**消失方式：** 观察数分钟后，Saito停止观察。当他试图再次定位该物体时，由于多云天气条件无法找到。

**评估：** 描述表明可能是气象气球或类似的大气装置及附带设备。

001_1947-05-19_Oklahoma City, Oklahoma_3.report_summary:
**Witness:** Byron B. Savage, Sales Engineer for Radio Corporation of America, residing at 1416 N.W. 29th St., Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. Observation made from his residence.

**Date & Time:** Between May 17-21, 1947, just after dusk (approximately 2030-2100 hours).

**Sighting:** Savage observed a single unidentified flying object for 15-20 seconds. The object maintained straight flight on a trajectory from 160° south to 350° north.

**Object Description:** Round but disc-like shape with no protrusions. Frosty white in color. Size described as having the width of six B-29 bombers.

**Performance:** Altitude estimated at 10,000-18,000 feet. Speed approximately three times that of a jet aircraft. A loud swishing sound was heard after the object had passed.

**Additional Details:** No exhaust trails were observed. No odor detected. The object flew out of sight as its manner of disappearance. No sketches or photographs were provided. Weather conditions and effect on clouds not specified.
001_1947-05-19_Oklahoma City, Oklahoma_3.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** Byron B. Savage,美国无线电公司销售工程师,居住在俄克拉荷马城西北29街1416号。从其住所进行观察。

**日期和时间：** 1947年5月17日至21日之间,黄昏后(大约2030-2100时)。

**目击经过：** Savage观察到一个不明飞行物体,持续15-20秒。物体保持直线飞行,航迹从160°南方向到350°北方向。

**物体描述：** 圆形但呈碟状,无突出物。颜色为霜白色。大小描述为相当于六架B-29轰炸机的宽度。

**性能表现：** 高度估计在10,000-18,000英尺。速度约为喷气式飞机的三倍。物体通过后听到响亮的呼啸声。

**其他细节：** 未观察到尾迹。未检测到气味。物体飞出视线作为其消失方式。未提供草图或照片。天气条件和对云层的影响未说明。

001_1947-07-01_Tauberbischofsheim, Germa.report_summary:
**Witness:** Robert J. Sroka, address listed as S. Washington Ave., Waukesha, Wisconsin. Occupation not stated.

**Sighting:** Observed in Germany, approximately 20 miles southwest of Tauberbischofsheim, during evening hours. Date not specified. Two objects were visible for an undetermined duration.

**Objects:** Two vapor-trailed objects initially appeared at approximately 5,000 feet altitude and at a distance of 3 to 10 miles to the front, closing to approximately 1 mile. Objects traveled at slow speed.

**Behavior:** Observer initially thought the objects might be regular aircraft but then noticed unusual maneuvers. At about one mile distance, one object made a sudden horizontal motion while continuing to descend slowly. The motion changed from a descending parachute-like movement to a spinning motion, then suddenly dropped in a spiral motion. The objects appeared dark in form.

**Notable Details:** The first impression was that the object was a cloud, but it was observed traveling at right angles to the wind direction, which ruled out a meteorological explanation. The vapor trails and unusual descent patterns distinguished these objects from conventional aircraft.
001_1947-07-01_Tauberbischofsheim, Germa.report_summary_zh:
**目击者:** Robert J. Sroka，地址为威斯康星州沃基肖市华盛顿大道南段。职业未说明。

**目击经过:** 在德国陶伯比绍夫斯海姆西南约20英里处，于傍晚时分观察到。日期未具体说明。两个物体可见，持续时间不详。

**物体特征:** 两个带有蒸汽尾迹的物体，最初出现在约5,000英尺高度，距离前方3至10英里处，后接近至约1英里。物体以缓慢速度移动。

**行为表现:** 目击者最初认为这些物体可能是常规飞机，但随后注意到异常机动。在约1英里距离处，一个物体做出突然的水平运动，同时继续缓慢下降。运动方式从类似降落伞的下降变为旋转运动，然后突然以螺旋方式坠落。物体呈暗色形态。

**值得注意的细节:** 第一印象是物体为云层，但观察到它以与风向成直角的方向移动，这排除了气象学解释。蒸汽尾迹和异常下降模式使这些物体区别于常规飞机。

001_1947-07-06_Hollywood, California_38_.report_summary:
**Witness:** M. Lenore Corey, address 2636 Magnolia Ave., Los Angeles, California. Occupation not stated.

**Sighting:** Observed from a bus terminal in Hollywood, California on July 6, 1947. Time not specified. Weather conditions noted as sunlight.

**Object:** Several saucer-shaped objects observed. Size, color, and specific distance from observer not stated. Objects traveled at great speed in a northward direction, parallel to Ventura Boulevard. The objects "rolled" during flight. No sound, odor, exhaust trails, or effect on clouds reported.

**Unusual Phenomena:** Observer reported accompanying ray phenomena with the saucers. Witness perceived what appeared to be white rays in the sunlight which seemed to cause a curious phenomenon. The rays did not appear as reflected light - they were not evenly spaced and they "criss-crossed." There appeared to be a vortex with a radius of about 18 inches as observed from witness's position. Objects described as "planing objects" that were not flying as if magnetized.

**Disappearance:** Manner of disappearance not stated. Observer looked away and when looking back, the objects and secondary ray phenomena occurred again, but by this time the saucers were out of sight.

**Remarks:** Observer seemed to be speculating on warfare applications but did not think the experience could be turned to use for a directed light. No sketches or photographs obtained.
001_1947-07-06_Hollywood, California_38_.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** M. Lenore Corey，地址为加利福尼亚州洛杉矶市木兰大道2636号。职业未说明。

**目击经过：** 1947年7月6日在加利福尼亚州好莱坞的一个公共汽车站观察到。时间未具体说明。天气条件记录为阳光明媚。

**物体特征：** 观察到数个碟形物体。物体的大小、颜色和与目击者的具体距离均未说明。物体以极快速度向北方向移动，平行于文图拉大道。物体在飞行过程中"翻滚"。未报告声音、气味、尾迹或对云层的影响。

**异常现象：** 目击者报告碟形物体伴随有光线现象。目击者在阳光中看到似乎是白色光线的东西，似乎引起了一种奇特现象。这些光线看起来不像反射光——它们间距不均匀且"交叉"。从目击者所在位置观察，似乎存在一个半径约18英寸的漩涡。物体被描述为某种"滑翔物体"，飞行方式不像被磁化。

**消失方式：** 消失方式未说明。目击者看向别处后再次观望，物体和次级光线现象再次出现，但此时碟形物体已经消失在视野之外。

**备注：** 目击者似乎在推测战争应用，但认为这次经历不能被用于定向光武器。未获得草图或照片。

001_1947-05-19_Manitou Springs, Colorado.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. D. A. Mauser, Mr. F. J. Smith, and Mr. L. D. Jenison, employees of Pikes Peak Railway, Manitou Springs, Colorado.

**Sighting:** During their lunch period (1215-1315 hours) on 19 May 1947, a member of a train crew called attention to a silver object in the sky approaching from the northeast. The sighting lasted for several minutes.

**Object:** The object appeared extremely small and silver in color. No definite shape could be determined even with the aid of power binoculars. The witnesses were certain it was not a conventional aircraft since it did not have any of the physical characteristics. The object appeared to be traveling at great speed and at an altitude over 1,000 feet (higher than the top of Manitou Mountain, which is some 1,000 feet higher than the city).

**Maneuvers:** Upon reaching the area just north of Manitou, the object remained in the area for several minutes executing maneuvers such as climbing, diving, and reversal of flight direction. These maneuvers happened every few seconds. At times it seemed to hover and then would start on another flight path. The distance and location between views prompted two of the men to think there may have been more than one object in the sky.

**Disappearance:** When last seen, the silver object was climbing very fast towards the west, almost directly into the wind.

**Weather:** CAVU (Ceiling And Visibility Unlimited), no ground wind, no clouds.

**Evaluation:** Source rated "E"; Information rated "C".
001_1947-05-19_Manitou Springs, Colorado.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** D. A. Mauser先生、F. J. Smith先生和L. D. Jenison先生，科罗拉多州马尼托斯普林斯派克峰铁路公司的雇员。

**目击经过：** 1947年5月19日午餐时间（1215-1315时），一名列车乘务员注意到天空中有一个银色物体从东北方向接近。目击持续了数分钟。

**物体描述：** 该物体看起来极小，呈银色。即使借助高倍望远镜也无法确定明确的形状。目击者确信这不是常规飞行器，因为它没有任何常规飞行器的物理特征。该物体似乎以极快的速度飞行，高度超过1000英尺（高于马尼托山顶，而马尼托山顶比城市高出约1000英尺）。

**机动动作：** 到达马尼托以北地区后，该物体在该区域停留了数分钟，期间执行了爬升、俯冲和反向飞行等机动动作。这些动作每隔几秒钟就会发生。有时它似乎悬停，然后又开始另一条飞行路径。由于观察距离和位置的变化，其中两名目击者认为天空中可能有不止一个物体。

**消失方式：** 最后一次看到时，该银色物体正以极快的速度向西爬升，几乎直接逆风飞行。

**天气状况：** CAVU（无限制的云高和能见度），无地面风，无云。

**评估：** 来源评级"E"；信息评级"C"。

001_1947-12-30_Pyramid Lake, Nevada_38_1.report_summary:

**Location:** Pyramid Lake area, Nevada

**Witness:** Name and occupation not stated. Address illegible.

**Report:** The Fairfield control tower obtained a report at approximately 2300 EST on 30 December 1947 from a witness who observed aerial activity over the Pyramid Lake area of Nevada.

**Object/Activity:** The aerial activity was observed at approximately 12 to 15 hundred feet (1,200-1,500 feet) above the ground. The objects or phenomena performed unusual maneuvers.

**Analysis:** Many details on the check-list form are illegible or not stated, including the number of objects, distance from observer, and time in sight. The remarks note that this observation appears to be connected with Incidents 48, 94, 95, and 97, suggesting a possible pattern or series of related sightings in the area during this timeframe.
001_1947-12-30_Pyramid Lake, Nevada_38_1.report_summary_zh:
**事件：** #96

**日期：** 1947年12月30日

**时间：** 大约东部标准时间2300时

**地点：** 内华达州金字塔湖地区
