**Document:** Single-page typewritten letter dated **Portland, Oregon, August 20, 1947**, preserved in FBI file **62-HQ-83894, Section 3** and stamped **CONFIDENTIAL**. It is addressed to **Lt. Col. Donald L. Springer, Assistant Staff**. The page bears a later **A TRUE COPY** endorsement signed by Springer, indicating this is a retained file copy rather than the original outgoing letter.

**Witness:** The author identifies himself as **F. M. Johnson**, a **prospector** living at **106 No. West 1st Ave, Portland, Oregon**. He says he was in the **Mt. Adams district** on **June 24, 1947**, the same day Kenneth Arnold reported his now-famous sighting near the Cascade range.

**Sighting:** Johnson states he saw “the same flying objects” at about the same time Arnold did. He says he used a **telescope** and is certain the objects were real. He reports they passed **very high** overhead, probably around **1,000 feet** above him, making no sound like an airplane. He describes them as **round**, about **30 feet in diameter**, tapering sharply to a point, with an **oval shape** and a **bright top surface**. The rear or tail end allegedly looked like “a big hand of a clock shifting from side to side like a big magnet.” He says their speed seemed greater than anything he had ever seen and that the last view showed them “standing on edge” while **banking in a cloud**.

**Assessment:** This is a contemporaneous eyewitness letter tying the observation to the **Kenneth Arnold** wave of 1947 reports. The account is detailed but subjective, with no supporting witnesses or measurements beyond the observer’s estimate. The page appears to be the complete report for this incident; no later page in the provided sequence indicates a different event.

He added that the objects were not Navy "flapjacks".

**Investigation:** The report is an intelligence-style interview summary rather than a full technical analysis. **Witness:** The primary witness was Bruce Armstrong, identified as an electronics technician at the Boeing Aircraft plant. The report also names M. A. Nichols of Seattle as a second sighting witness, with additional corroboration from Ray Stanley, George and Mrs. Krogstad, and Boeing Field personnel.

**Sighting:** Armstrong stated that about 2:20 p.m. on August 12, 1947, while standing in front of Section D of the Boeing Aircraft Plant with about ten other research engineers, he saw a small black object about 200 feet high moving south over the Boeing Field runway. Later, report text notes another sighting by Nichols at about 4 p.m., who said he saw an object over his home moving southwest at a much higher altitude, with observers describing it as a white, cylindrical object reflecting sunlight with a purplish tinge.

**Investigation:** The Seattle office interviewed control-tower operator Ken Grant and Boeing Field weather-bureau personnel. Grant suggested the low object may have been a piece of burnt paper blown across the field; weather personnel noted that balloons were released every six hours from Boeing Field, were white in color, and could reflect sunlight at altitude. The report concludes that the observed object was probably a balloon or other debris and states that no further investigation would be conducted.

The page is part of FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4, and carries later file stamps (including 162-83894-149 and a Jan. 4, 1949 routing mark). It records a telephone report from SAC Willis in Houston and subsequent instructions from FBI Headquarters.

**Witness:** The primary eyewitness is Lonnie Noack of the Humboldt Oil Company, Houston, Texas. According to the memo, Noack was flying as a passenger with a friend in a private aircraft from California to Houston when the incident occurred. A Houston businessman, Fuller Blackwell, had furnished photographs reportedly taken by Noack.

**Sighting:** About 30 miles east of Lone Pine, California, Noack and the pilot saw an object on the ground that produced a very strong bright reflection. They landed to inspect it. The object was described as roughly 8 feet in diameter, with wings about 4 feet long, about 1 foot thick, and something in the center that “appears to be some type of gyroscope.” The wings were said to have some kind of jet propulsion arrangement. No identifying marks were found, and photographs were taken.

**Investigation:** SAC Willis said he had already informed Lt. Robert Fleming of the Army Air Forces at Ellington Field and Capt. Bush, the Army representative in Houston. Noack was to be interviewed the next morning with Lt. Fleming present, and an Army Air Forces examination of the object was anticipated. Fletcher instructed Willis to send full details and a copy of the photograph by air mail special delivery and to ensure a Bureau agent was present when the object was examined in California. The memo reflects active FBI coordination with the Army Air Forces rather than a completed technical conclusion.

Fleming and Christopher R. Bradley (Office of Special Investigation, Ellington Field) and FBI Special Agents Graham W. Kitchall and Galen N. Willis. The pages shown are consecutive pages 1–2 of the same statement in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4.

**Witness:** Noack says he was traveling with R.C. Person, Nathan Smith, C.A. Toce, Robert Broussard, and one other unidentified man. He describes the information as partly firsthand and partly relayed by Person and Smith. The statement reads like an interview/affidavit rather than an independent field report, but it includes Noack’s own observation of the object and the photos/film taken at the scene.

**Sighting:** On Dec. 6, 1948, the group dined at the Old Virginia Inn in Los Angeles and then returned to Smith’s electrical manufacturing company. Person reportedly described a flying disc and arranged for the group to leave the next day with cameras. Because Person was delayed at a private airfield, they did not depart until about 2 P.M. on Dec. 7. They then drove to the reported location, which Noack describes as flat, desert, and desolate, roughly 150 miles from Pasadena and east/northeast of the city.

**Object:** At the site they found a “disc, or flying wing” on the ground in a semi-vertical position at about a 45-degree angle, with the left wing imbedded in the ground. Noack says it had apparently struck with considerable force and slid 300–400 feet. He estimates the diameter at about seven feet, with wings about four feet by twenty inches and three inches thick, mounted on an axle through the disc and on ball bearings. The object was dented but generally intact.

**Investigation:** Nathan Smith shot about 10 feet of 16 mm film; Person took five or six Speed Graphic stills, though Noack notes the first three may have been underexposed. The report contains no formal FBI conclusion, but the physical description strongly suggests a man-made flying wing or experimental device rather than an unexplained aerial object.

**Witness:** The initial account was relayed from Logan, Utah, based on what an unnamed guard at the Army General Supply Depot in Ogden said he saw at about 9:00 AM. Additional contemporaneous observers included Lt. Ron Hatfield of the Logan Police Department, Utah Highway Patrolman L. N. Jeppson at Mantua, and several residents at Trenton. Because the report is a teletype summary rather than a signed field interview, the first-hand chain is somewhat indirect, but the sightings were reportedly corroborated by multiple local witnesses.

**Sighting:** Witnesses described a silver-colored object, a flash of light/fire, and what looked like an airborne explosion followed by a falling object west of Ogden/Logan, near Taylor, Sardine Canyon, and west of Trenton. One report mentions two puffs of smoke high in the air; another says the object appeared to explode as it neared the mountain. The timing clustered around 9:00-9:20 AM on 5 Apr 1949.

**Investigation:** The report says the information was immediately furnished to OSI at Hill Field, Utah. Hill Field then advised that the phenomena were probably caused by two B-29s from Wendover Field practice-bombing in the desert west of Logan at extremely high altitude, producing vapor trails that could have been misread as aerial explosions or a falling disc. The document therefore records a UFO-style sighting but ends with a conventional military explanation rather than a confirmed unknown."

001_1949-04-01_Los Angeles, California,.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 一页FBI备忘录，印在局方信笺纸上，由局长J. Edgar Hoover致空军部特别调查处处长（Pentagon），日期为1949年5月2日。其上标注“RE: FLYING DISCS”，盖有“CONFIDENTIAL BY SPECIAL MESSENGER”印章，并带有FBI案卷标记，包括“62-HQ-83894-167”和“RECORDED - 128”注记。页面还显示1949年5月3日的通信科印章以及流转/批准首字母，表明这属于FBI内部处理，而非外勤调查。

**Witness:** 备忘录并未指明实际目击者。文中称，一名可靠的机密来源告诉FBI，位于California, Hollywood, Los Feliz的4312号的C. A. Atkins先生报告了这一情况。Atkins随后表示，Los Angeles市公园娱乐部门的三名雇员看见天空中有物体，看起来像飞碟。由于目击者未具名，且报告为转述，其证词可信度仅限于这条机密来源链。

**Sighting:** 这次目击发生在1949年4月上旬，地点为Los Angeles, California。文中未提供精确时间、方向、持续时间、飞行高度、物体数量、颜色、形状、速度或机动细节。唯一的描述是，天空中的这些物体“appeared to be flying discs”。

**Investigation:** FBI明确表示，相关信息正提供给空军，由其酌情采取行动，而局方“no investigation is being conducted”。从分析角度看，这只是一份简短的转交，而非实质性案件报告：它保留了一条早期民间UFO式线索，但页面上没有佐证、没有技术描述，也没有后续结论。

001_1949-03-31_Killeen Base / Camp Hood.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64), from the SAC, San Antonio, to the Director, FBI, dated April 4, 1949, marked "Air Mail / Special Delivery" and filed under Bureau file 65-48300 (with local notation 100-7545). The memo references an earlier San Antonio letter to the Bureau dated March 22, 1949 concerning "unconventional aircraft" and records a follow-up inquiry from G-2, 4th Army on April 4, 1949 asking whether the FBI had information to substantiate or discredit Walter Winchell’s remarks about "flying discs."

**Witness:** The principal observer was 1st Lt. Frederick W. Davis, who was in charge of a platoon in Company C, 12th Armored Infantry Battalion, part of the alert force ("Force Abel") assigned from Camp Hood to protect Killeen Base. The report presents him as a trained military officer on duty near the installation, which gives the account some operational credibility, though the narrative remains secondhand within the FBI memo.

**Sighting:** At about 11:50 P.M. on March 31, 1949, Lt. Davis reportedly saw a lighted object about the size of a basketball, reddish-white in color and trailing fire, southwest of Killeen Base adjacent to Camp Hood, Texas. He estimated it at about 6,000 feet altitude. The object traveled parallel to the ground, passed directly over him at rapid speed, remained visible for 10 to 15 seconds, and then suddenly disappeared high in the sky without descending. He reported no sound or odor, and the night was clear with good visibility. The object passed almost directly over the air strip at Killeen Base.

**Investigation:** Immediately after the sighting, Lt. Davis tried to telephone headquarters but heard static or electrical interference on the line, which he considered possibly radio interference. The memo further notes that G-2 reported other unidentified lights on March 6, 7, 8, and 17, 1949, seen by military personnel about 1,000 yards east of the fence surrounding Killeen Base, but states the March 31 object was different in nature from those earlier lights. No FBI analytic conclusion is recorded on this page; the document functions as a relay of military observations and a request for Bureau input amid public discussion of "flying discs."
001_1949-03-31_Killeen Base / Camp Hood.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** FBI办公室备忘录（标准表格第64号），由圣安东尼奥（San Antonio）SAC致FBI局长，日期为1949年4月4日，标注“Air Mail / Special Delivery”，并归档于局档案65-48300（本地编号100-7545）。该备忘录提及此前圣安东尼奥于1949年3月22日致局里的一封信，内容涉及“非常规飞行器”，并记录了4月4日来自G-2，第四军（4th Army）的后续询问，询问FBI是否掌握能够证实或驳斥Walter Winchell关于“飞碟（flying discs）”言论的信息。

**Witness:** 主要目击者是Frederick W. Davis中尉（1st Lt.），他当时负责C连（Company C）第12装甲步兵营（12th Armored Infantry Battalion）的一支排，该营属于从胡德营（Camp Hood）派往保护基林基地（Killeen Base）的警戒部队（“Force Abel”）的一部分。报告将他描述为一名在该设施附近执勤的受过训练的军官，这为叙述提供了一定的作战可信度，尽管在FBI备忘录中，这一叙述仍属于转述。

**Sighting:** 据称，1949年3月31日晚上约11:50，Davis中尉看到一个发光物体，大小约如篮球，呈红白色，尾部拖着火焰，位于得克萨斯州（Texas）胡德营旁的基林基地西南方。他估计其高度约为6,000英尺。该物体平行于地面飞行，以极快速度直接从他头顶掠过，持续可见10到15秒，随后在空中高处突然消失，没有下降。他报告称没有听到声音或闻到气味，且当晚天空晴朗、能见度良好。该物体几乎直接从基林基地的跑道上方飞过。

**Investigation:** 目击发生后，Davis中尉立即试图拨打电话联系总部，但听到线路上有静电或电气干扰，他认为这可能是无线电干扰。备忘录进一步指出，G-2报告称在1949年3月6日、7日、8日和17日，军方人员还在基林基地围栏以东约1,000码处看见过其他不明灯光，但声明3月31日的物体在性质上与那些早先的灯光不同。本页未记录FBI的分析结论；该文件的作用是在公众讨论“飞碟”之际，转述军事观察并请求局方提供意见。

001_1949-05-18_New Orleans, Louisiana_65.report_summary:
**Document:** One-page FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) from SAC, New Orleans to the Director, FBI, dated June 2, 1949, subject line “FLYING DISCS.” The memo references SAC Letter 38 of March 25, 1949 and carries Bureau routing/receipt stamps. It is an internal FBI intelligence note, not a field interview, and states that all three incidents had been investigated by Army Intelligence.

**Witness:** The underlying sightings were reported through the Office of Naval Intelligence, New Orleans, and involved two unnamed witnesses for at least one observation. The memo notes that the witnesses were outdoors and did not wear glasses. No personal names, occupations, or ranks are provided on this page.

**Sighting:** The Bureau was advised that three flying-disc sightings occurred in the City of New Orleans within the previous ten days, on May 18, 19, and 23, 1949. The objects were described as single discs in straight flight, generally northbound in the late afternoon, about the size of an observation plane but shaped like a saucer. The Navy further reported that two witnesses said the object appeared to be traveling end over end.

**Investigation:** Weather was reportedly good at the times of the sightings. Naval Intelligence considered the possibility that the objects were weather balloons, but noted that weather balloons were launched from only one airport, typically an hour before sighting times, and would usually be out of view within minutes. The memo does not reach a definitive conclusion, but it preserves the Navy’s tentative balloon explanation and the fact that Army Intelligence had already looked into the three cases. The event is therefore best catalogued as a New Orleans multi-sighting UFO/flying-disc report rather than a confirmed aircraft or astronomical identification.

**Witness:** 相关目击报告是通过新奥尔良海军情报办公室（Office of Naval Intelligence, New Orleans）上报的，其中至少有一次观测涉及两名未具名证人。备忘录指出，证人在室外，且未戴眼镜。本页未提供任何个人姓名、职业或军衔。

**Sighting:** 据告知，过去十天内，新奥尔良市（City of New Orleans）发生了三起飞碟目击事件，分别在 1949年5月18日、19日和23日。所见物体被描述为单个圆盘，呈直线飞行，通常在傍晚时分向北飞行，大小约如一架观察机（observation plane），但外形像飞碟。海军进一步报告称，两名证人表示该物体看起来像是在首尾翻转地移动。

001_1949-04-04_Merced, California (about.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) from the SAC, Los Angeles, to the Director, FBI, dated May 13, 1949, in case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4. The memo summarizes a "flying disk" report tied to Merced, California, and carries file marks including 100-2442 plus Recorded/Indexed 110.

**Witness:** The principal witness is William H. Parrott of 12-A Langdon Villa, Merced. He is described as being in the Air Corps Reserve. His account reached the FBI indirectly: Mel Hodell, a Sun-Star reporter in Merced, spoke with FBI Special Agent Marlin W. Johnson, and George Bremer of Castle Air Force Base later produced a letter from Lt. Col. Stanley F. Jacobs, USAF, containing Parrott's statement.

**Sighting:** Parrott said that on April 4, 1949, at about 2220, while outside his home about one mile west of Merced, he heard a strong clicking noise. After about ten seconds he looked toward the source and saw one object in the sky, about 40 degrees above the horizon to the east, moving in a west or northwesterly direction and apparently blanking out stars. He described it as a solid mass, roughly 4 to 5 feet in diameter, at an estimated altitude of less than 1,000 feet. Color was only visible by reflection of ground lights on two occasions.

**Investigation:** The memo also notes that Castle Air Force Base personnel had been asked about local "flying disk" reports, and that Bremer heard an intelligence report had been made at the base. The page is an intelligence-style relay of secondhand information rather than a direct witness interview, and it ends mid-sentence with no final identification or conclusion.

001_1944-01-01_Texas–Mexico border regio.report_summary:
**Document:** Single handwritten page in FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4, part of the bureau’s 1947 flying-disc correspondence. The page is signed "Mrs. Frank Gardner" and addressed "Respectfully yours" to "Mr. Hoover," indicating a direct letter to J. Edgar Hoover rather than a formal field report. No continuation or "page 2" marker appears on the rendered page.

**Witness:** Mrs. Frank Gardner says the information did not come from a direct sighting by her. She writes that the story was "told me in 1944 or 43," and that she wrote it down at the time, then forgot about it until the flying-saucer discussion revived her memory. In a postscript she adds that she lived a few miles from the Mexican border in Texas when she heard it.

**Sighting / claim:** The page does not describe a firsthand UFO observation. Instead, it reports a remembered account that "there were thousands of them" and that "they were supposed to be the rocket type." The wording suggests a wartime rumor or second-hand report of rocket-like objects, later reconsidered by the writer as possibly relevant to flying saucers. No color, shape, flight behavior, speed, sound, or duration is provided.

**Assessment:** Because the page is hearsay rather than a direct observation, it is best treated as a correspondence lead, not a substantiated sighting. The document’s value lies in showing how civilians near the Texas-Mexico border interpreted earlier rocket rumors through the 1947 flying-saucer lens. The page offers no corroboration, no investigative findings, and no technical analysis beyond the writer’s belief that such "flying saucers could be more dangerous than we think."

001_1948-07-24_near Montgomery, Alabama.report_summary:
**Document:** Single-page newspaper clipping pasted into FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 4. Source is the *Atlanta Journal* (Sunday, 7/25/48), article by William Key, headlined “‘Sky Devil-Ship’ Scares Pilots; Air Chief Wishes He Had One.” No FBI interview memorandum or official witness statement appears on this page; it is press coverage preserved in the file.

**Witness:** The report centers on Capt. C. S. Chiles of Atlanta and Co-Pilot John B. Whitted of Hapeville, identified as Eastern Air Lines pilots on the Houston–Atlanta–Boston run. The article says they told their story after arriving at Atlanta Municipal Airport. Chiles is the named pilot in the headline photo caption, with Whitted as the second witness.

**Sighting:** The pilots said they saw an unusual object near Montgomery, Alabama, during the “spooky hours” Saturday morning, 24 July 1948. The article characterizes it as a “gigantic plane without wings,” black against the night sky and “streaking through the heavens” at about 5,000 feet.

**Object:** Described as having a fiery comet-like tail 25 to 50 feet long, an estimated 100-foot fuselage, and two rows of brightly lit square windows. The article says no crew was seen aboard. It compares the object to a “Flying Dutchman of the Skies” and notes that airplane makers and the Army Strategic Air Command were skeptical but curious.

**Investigation:** This page is a newspaper account rather than a formal investigative report, so it provides no corroboration, radar data, or chain-of-custody evidence. In the FBI file it serves as press documentation of the famous Alabama/Eastern Air Lines “wingless aircraft” event, with the sighting date clearly preceding the newspaper date by one day.

001_1947-07-01_Los Angeles, California (.report_summary:
**Document:** This is page 2 of an FBI Los Angeles file item marked "LA 100-2442" in Section 4 of the 62-HQ-83894 UFO file. The page is a continuation of a typed report/letter and closes with "The above is being furnished for the information of the Bureau," indicating a field-office transmission rather than a standalone public statement.

**Witness:** The principal witness is identified only as Mr. Parrott, a major in the Active USAF Reserve. The report says he qualified as a pilot in August 1941 and had approximately 2,200 hours of flying time, with substantial night-flying experience during World War II. Those details were included to support his credibility as an experienced observer.

**Sighting:** Parrott stated that he first heard the object about 10 seconds before seeing it and then watched it for about 35 seconds from his home area. He described a dull-surfaced, light-colored metal object moving very slowly west or northwest, then passing beyond the house and making an estimated 90-degree left turn before heading south or southwest. He said the object came to appear directly overhead before disappearing.

**Object:** The witness reported a continuous clicking sound, likened to the beaters of an improperly meshed home mixer. He denied any whistle, roar, flame, exhaust trail, or steady lights, though he saw brief reflections twice. He believed the underside may have been curved because of the streetlights behind him about half a block away. His dog also reacted to the object’s path, which he noted as a possible indicator of sound frequencies not obvious to him.

**Investigation:** The report says no other witnesses were located through the local newspaper or area inquiry. Mr. Bremer indicated he would clear the matter with headquarters and likely conduct an investigation. No final explanation is offered on this page, but the report preserves a seemingly credible, short-duration observation of a metallic, noisy object with unusual maneuvering and no visible propulsion.

001_1952-07-27_Jackson, Minnesota (uncle.report_summary:

**Sighting:** The event appears to have occurred on Sunday morning, 27 Jul 1952, at a pasture near Jackson, Minnesota. A neighbor’s wife reportedly got up to get water and saw a “steady white Light circling their farm,” though she did not initially consider it important. Later that same morning, Hoffmeyer’s uncle went to get the cows and found an unidentified substance in the pasture.

001_1952-08-26_West Palm Beach, Florida.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64), dated 29 Aug. 1952, from D. J. Parsons to Mr. Harbo, subject “Unidentified Flying Object allegedly cited by Mr. D. S. Desvergers, West Palm Beach, Florida.” The memo says the Air Force, by letter of 26 Aug. 1952, asked the FBI to examine Desvergers’ cap for possible residues and to provide an oral report the same night. Internal routing initials and file stamps show it was handled at FBI Headquarters / Laboratory level.

**Witness:** Mr. D. S. Desvergers, identified here as a scoutmaster in West Palm Beach, claimed he was in a desolate area when he observed an unidentified flying object. He reported that the object was about 30 feet in diameter, hovered over his head, and shot a “red blob” that caused him to lose consciousness. He also said the hair on his arms was singed and his cap was burned.

**Investigation:** FBI examination of the cap found no residue that would identify the material responsible for the burns. The memo notes one small burned area that was likely caused by a small hot ember rather than deliberate ignition, and says the singeing was not uniform as would be expected from a single flash of flame. The front edge of the bill was more severely singed than other portions, a pattern the lab said would not be expected if the source were directly overhead. The memo further observes that the fold in the blue cloth showed no singeing underneath, suggesting the cap may not have been worn when the burning occurred. Recommendation: orally advise the Air Force/Colonel Free of these findings rather than attributing the damage to an identified aerial substance.

**Document:** This page is a secondary-source newspaper/magazine clipping preserved in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7. No FBI memo header, classification stamp, or signer is visible on the page itself; the material is a narrative excerpt about the Washington, D.C. radar UFO incidents, with unrelated advertisements in the left column.

**Witness:** The principal named witness in the excerpt is Barnes, described in context as the radar/controller source for the Washington air-traffic facility. He is quoted at length describing what he saw on the radarscope and rejecting ordinary explanations. Other witnesses mentioned include a commercial pilot, additional nearby pilots, and Air Force interceptor pilots.

**Sighting:** Barnes reports that for six hours on the morning of 20 July 1952 there were at least ten unidentifiable objects moving above Washington. The text then shifts to a related follow-up on 26 July 1952 at 9:08 P.M., when the Air Route Traffic Control Center and Andrews AFB radar again showed unidentified targets over the capital. Two jet interceptors were sent from New Castle, Delaware, toward the objects; one pilot later reported four lights roughly ten miles ahead and slightly above his aircraft, and another saw a steady white light before it vanished.

**Object:** The objects are described as radar pips and lights, not ordinary aircraft. Barnes says they were not aircraft and that he could not attribute them to natural phenomena, shooting stars, electrical disturbances, or clouds. Visual descriptions are sparse but include multiple lights, horizontal motion, and abrupt disappearance.

**Investigation:** The excerpt states that Air Force spokesmen denied evidence that the objects were flying saucers, while also admitting they had no evidence they were not. The incidents triggered intense public reaction, with the Air Force receiving large numbers of letters, calls, and telegrams and airlines being asked to photograph any saucers encountered. The overall analytic takeaway on the page is that the Washington radar cases remained unexplained in the source narrative, even as official caution persisted.
001_1952-07-20_Washington, D.C. (Washing.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 这一页是保存在 FBI 档案 62-HQ-83894 第7节中的二手来源报纸/杂志剪报。页面本身看不到 FBI 备忘录页眉、机密印章或签署人；该材料是一段关于华盛顿特区雷达 UFO 事件的叙述性摘录，左栏还夹有无关广告。

**Witness:** 摘录中提到的主要具名证人是 Barnes，他在上下文中被描述为华盛顿空中交通设施的雷达/管制员消息来源。他被大段引用，描述自己在雷达屏幕上看到的情况，并否定了普通解释。文中还提到其他证人，包括一名商业飞行员、其他附近飞行员以及空军拦截机飞行员。

**Sighting:** Barnes 报告称，在 1952 年 7 月 20 日上午长达六个小时的时间里，华盛顿上空至少有十个无法识别的物体移动。随后，文本转到 1952 年 7 月 26 日晚 9:08 的一个相关后续事件，当时 Air Route Traffic Control Center 和 Andrews AFB 雷达再次在首都上空显示出不明目标。两架喷气式拦截机从 Delaware 的 New Castle 起飞，前往接近这些目标；其中一名飞行员后来报告称，在其飞机前方约十英里处、略高的位置看到了四个灯光，另一名飞行员则看到一个稳定的白光，随后它便消失了。

**Object:** 这些物体被描述为雷达上的光点和灯光，而非普通飞机。Barnes 说它们不是飞机，并且他无法将其归因于自然现象、流星、电气扰动或云层。视觉描述较少，但包括多个灯光、水平移动以及突然消失。

**Investigation:** 摘录称，空军发言人否认这些物体是飞碟的证据，但同时也承认他们没有证据证明它们不是飞碟。这些事件引发了强烈的公众反应，空军收到大量信件、电话和电报，并要求航空公司对遇到的任何飞碟进行拍照。页面上的总体分析结论是，尽管官方保持谨慎态度，华盛顿雷达案例在来源叙述中仍然没有得到解释。

001_1952-07-28_Franklin, Indiana, USA_65.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is from *SPACE REVIEW*, page 10, under the heading “SAUCER SIGHTINGS BY IFSB MEMBERS,” with the subhead “Exclusive! From Franklin, Indiana and Surrounding Towns.” The primary incident on the page is “Sighting No. 4,” compiled from a police report turned in by Capt. Lee Sloan, Patrolman Jack W. Moore, and Patrolman Kenneth Rund of the Franklin, Indiana Police Department. The page states that the objects were also witnessed by civilian authorities and members of the U.S. Army, and that after authorities were notified no definite action was taken by the Army or otherwise.

**Witness:** The reporting witnesses were Franklin police officers—Capt. Lee Sloan, Patrolman Jack W. Moore, and Patrolman Kenneth Rund. Because the account is framed as a police report and references multiple corroborating observers, it reads as a multi-witness civilian/official observation rather than a lone sighting. However, the page is a later UFO-periodical summary, not the original police incident report itself.

**Sighting:** On the morning of July 28, 1952, at about 6:00 a.m., three strange objects were seen in the skies southeast of and at times directly over Franklin, Indiana. One object was larger and brighter than the other two; it cast a white-yellow light and appeared to follow the smaller craft. The two smaller objects had their own lights, one orange and one reddish. The report says they flew in a “dog fight” pattern, making barrel rolls, loops, spins, 90-degree and 45-degree turns, and even appearing to move up and down like a giant yo-yo.

**Object:** The observers estimated the objects at about 15,000 feet altitude and varying from 1,500 to 10,000 mph. Even with binoculars, the witnesses could not determine an exact shape beyond “round and flat as a saucer.” The objects were reportedly visible for 4 hours and 15 minutes, with daylight not changing their appearance. At 5:11 a.m. the smaller objects disappeared above the larger one, first the orange and then the red; the larger object then moved west and vanished. The report emphasizes the apparent coordinated maneuvers, but the speed and altitude estimates are likely subjective and should be treated cautiously.

001_1952-09-12_Flatwoods (near Sutton),.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a *Space Review* clipping, page 3, carrying an article titled “Sutton, West Virginia Monster May Be ‘Collier’s’ Rocket!” by Rev. S. L. Daw, Washington, D.C., listed as a Representative of the IFSB. The page is a composite newsletter page; the lower half begins a separate item about New Zealand saucer contacts and is not part of this event.

**Witness:** The article does not name individual observers. It refers generically to “the West Virginia people” who claimed to have seen the object at Sutton, and it cites secondary testimony about a police officer burned by a similar object in Wheeling, with Daw’s cousin described as the treating doctor.

**Sighting:** The Sutton incident is described as a “monster” or object seen in the Sutton/Flatwoods area of Braxton County, West Virginia. Daw summarizes the reported appearance as a large object “in the shape of a man,” estimated at about 10 feet tall and four feet wide at the bottom, with two flashing lights, a sound like gas escaping, and a sharp, sickening odor.

**Object / interpretation:** Daw argues the reported creature may have been a rocket or test article rather than a biological being. He connects the event to a *Collier’s* magazine piece describing a future moon rocket: a sphere-headed, wide-bottomed, tank-bellied craft that would emit burning hydrazine and nitric acid and could, in reflection, be mistaken for a small person or “monster.”

**Investigation / conclusion:** This is not a field report from law enforcement or the military; it is a speculative popular-press interpretation reprinted in a civilian UFO newsletter. The author concludes that the United States may be experimenting with secret rocket technology and that the public is being kept uninformed, suggesting the age of rocket ships is near.

**Witness:** 文章并未点名任何具体目击者。它笼统地提到“Sutton 的西弗吉尼亚人”声称在 Sutton 看到过该物体，并引述了有关一名警官被类似物体在 Wheeling 烧伤的间接证词，而 Daw 的表兄被描述为当时的主治医生。

**Sighting:** Sutton 事件被描述为在 West Virginia 的 Braxton County 的 Sutton/Flatwoods 地区看到的一个“怪物”或物体。Daw 概述称其外观像一个“人的形状”的大型物体，估计高约 10 feet，底部宽约 four feet，伴有两道闪光，发出类似气体逸出的声音，并散发出刺鼻、令人作呕的气味。

001_1951-07-06_Lynchburg College adminis.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a clipped article from *Space Review* titled “Excerpts from a Summary of a Five-Year Flying Saucer Investigation,” by George D. Fawcett (International Council, IFSB). It appears in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7, but it is not an FBI-originated investigative memo. No classification marking is visible on the page.

**Witness:** Fawcett presents himself as a private flying-saucer researcher who had spent a little over five years collecting reports, interviewing astronomers, scientists, pilots, guided-missile experts, and other eyewitnesses. He says he also wrote a pamphlet and lectured on the subject. His own sighting is described as the event that most increased his interest.

**Sighting:** Fawcett states that his first personal encounter was an “orange disk like globe” that hovered for about four minutes over the Lynchburg College administration building in Lynchburg, Virginia, on the morning of 6 July 1951. He does not provide an exact time, weather conditions, or corroborating witnesses on this page.

**Object:** The object is described only as orange, disk-like, and globe-shaped, with a brief hover. No sound, lighting behavior, size estimate, maneuver details, or physical evidence are reported here.

**Investigation:** The rest of the page is a general summary of his five-year UFO research and speculation. Fawcett argues that the accumulated reports suggest the phenomenon may involve grouped sightings, long-duration observations, and possibly controlled or satellite-like activity. He further suggests the U.S. government may know more than it says, but offers no concrete evidence in this excerpt. The page ends with an editorial note and unrelated club notice.

001_1953-03-09_Bowie, Prince George's Co.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum, United States Government, dated March 10, 1953. It was addressed to A. H. Belmont and signed by L. H. Martin. Subject line: “FLYING SAUCERS / JOHN BAILEY, INFORMANT.” The file context and routing show this was an internal FBI HQ memo, not a standalone field interview report.

**Witness:** John Bailey, identified only as an informant. The memo says he called from Bowie, Maryland, at 9:05 P.M. on 3/9/53. He was not cooperative: he was vague about where he was calling from and about his residence, and he did not provide identifying details.

**Sighting:** Bailey stated that he had “just seen a flying saucer near that city,” meaning near Bowie, Maryland. No description of the object’s shape, size, color, motion, altitude, duration, sound, or direction of travel was recorded. The memo does not confirm whether the object was observed directly, photographed, or independently verified.

**Investigation:** When asked where he planned to stay that night so the Air Force could interview him if advisable, Bailey replied that “the writer wanted to know too much” and disconnected. The memo concludes that because no specific information was furnished and the call may have been a prank, the Air Force was not advised. It also notes that no identifying information was obtained and no attempt was made to check Bureau records. Overall, this is best characterized as an unsubstantiated, low-detail UFO claim rather than a corroborated sighting report.

**Investigation:** The letter provides no follow-up identification or official analysis. Based on the limited description, the event remains an unclassified brief luminous-object sighting reported by a student witness, with a second student said to have observed it as well.

001_1953-04-08_Fort Buchanan (San Juan a.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Office Memorandum (Standard Form No. 64) from the SAC, San Juan (65-330) to the Director, FBI, dated 4/28/53. The subject line reads "UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECT OBSERVED 11:30 AM, APRIL 8, 1953, FORT BUCHANAN, PUERTO RICO; MISCELLANEOUS." The page bears handwritten office markings and a blue pencil note reading "flying saucers." The memo states it was prepared after a report was received on 4/27/53 from Major Bradford P. Shuman, Wing Intelligence Officer, Ramey Air Force Base, Puerto Rico.

**Witness:** Five persons at Fort Buchanan reportedly observed the object, including three captains and a sergeant of the U.S. Army, plus one civilian. Their statements were summarized by the Air Force intelligence office; the memo does not identify the individuals by name. The sighting was therefore secondhand to the FBI, coming through military intelligence channels.

**Sighting:** The event occurred at 11:30 AM on 4/8/53 at Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico. The witnesses described the object only generally, as either a "bright star" or a "bright ball of fire" at a great height, moving rapidly while observed. No size, shape, maneuvering details, sound, or duration are provided.

**Investigation:** The memorandum notes that all witnesses also observed one RB-36 aircraft in the area at the time. The Wing Intelligence Officer reported two RB-36 aircraft were operating nearby, at 12,000 and 21,000 feet respectively. None of the witnesses could accurately describe the object beyond the brief comparison above. The memo says the matter was being reported to the Bureau for information purposes and is marked "CLOSED." The file code at the bottom reads FDO 'B:MD, and the page is stamped/recorded in FBI indexing traces. No official FBI findings are included on the page, and the best reading is that this is an unsolicited civilian letter recounting a local UFO rumor rather than a formal investigative report.

001_1953-03-04_Valparaíso, Chile (letter.report_summary:
**Document:** Single typed Spanish letter dated Valparaíso, Chile, 4 Mar 1953, addressed to the Director of the FBI in Washington and included in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 7. The page is headed as a reference to a person with possible involvement in "Discos Voladores". No sender name is visible on the page.

**Witness:** The author appears to be an unnamed correspondent in Valparaíso rather than a firsthand UFO witness. The page compiles reported newspaper material and draws inferences from it.

**Sighting:** The letter does not describe one direct observation by the writer. Instead, it cites three published anecdotes: (1) the 1950 London detention/escape of Dr. Julius Linke, during which police allegedly encountered a sudden blackout, stopped elevators, dead telephones, and failed flashlights; (2) a Berlin incident shortly before the fall of the city in which car and truck engines allegedly stopped for about an hour before restarting; and (3) a local newspaper/AP account from roughly three months earlier in which an officer and companion pursued a flying disc that performed maneuvers, rose to great height, hovered over their airplane, and allegedly stalled the aircraft’s engines.

**Object:** The object is described as a "disco volador" (flying disc) with unusual maneuverability and the apparent ability to interfere with electrical or mechanical systems.

**Investigation:** The writer’s central theory is speculative: if the London/Kent incidents involved a person’s "interference" with electrical systems, then Dr. Linke might also explain the Berlin engine stoppage and the aircraft encounter. The page reads as analytical correspondence, not as an official FBI field investigation or a verified sighting report.

001_1954-09-05_Rockford, Illinois (moon.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a mixed newsletter-style case-file page preserved in FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 8. It includes an unrelated write-up on the Cincinnati paint incident and, under **CASE FILE REVIEW**, a separate Rockford, Illinois observation coded “C-22, Rockford, Ill.. 9/5/54).” The page is numbered “-7-” and cites a prior article by Edward S. Schultz in B.S.R.A.’s *Round Robin*; the editorial note is signed by Meade Layne.

**Witness:** Amateur astronomers Peter Bartkus and Theodore McColm were watching the Moon through a telescope. Bartkus is the principal narrator in the quoted report.

**Sighting:** Between 10:35 and 11:15 P.M. on 5 September 1954, Bartkus reported observing “the most unusual phenomena” he had ever witnessed. The Moon was in first quarter, with an apparent diameter of 29 feet 30 inches. Using a 6-inch casigranian reflector telescope with secondary mirror, over 100 inches focal length, and 150x and 200x eyepieces, the pair saw a spherical object rising from the northern section of Mare Humboldtianum.

**Object:** The object was described as not glowing or brilliant, but more like a dull reflected light from a planet. Its estimated apparent size was about that of the craters Pitiscus or Vlaco. By the time it disappeared at 11:15 P.M. it had traversed more than the Moon’s apparent diameter in roughly 40 minutes.

**Investigation / conclusion:** The witnesses checked for atmospheric diffraction and optical artifacts by moving the telescope and changing eyepieces, but found no explanation. Bartkus concluded the object was a powered body because the Moon was descending at about 1,081 mph while the object appeared to rise and did not follow a true orbit. His final assessment was that it was “definitely in space” and in the same field as, or near, the Moon. The page records no formal FBI analysis beyond preserving the report in the case file.

**Witness:** The primary witness was Senator Richard B. Russell, traveling by rail with three companions, including Colonel Hathaway and Mr. Green (a fourth participant is referenced later in the text but the name is partly unclear on this page). 001_1944-01-01_Gut Alt Golssen (near Gol.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Detroit 31, Michigan memorandum dated November 7, 1957, in file 62-83894-384, under the heading "UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS." The page bears an unclassified stamp and red handwritten routing/approval notations. These two pages are a single continuous report; page 2 is explicitly marked "-2-" and continues the same interview narrative.

**Witness:** Wladyslav Krasuski, a Polish displaced person and former prisoner of war living in Detroit, was interviewed at the request of the federal government after writing to Robert Cutler, special assistant to President Dwight D. Eisenhower, saying he might know something about "the rocket in Texas." At the time of the interview he was employed at Gobel Brewery in Detroit.

**Sighting:** Krasuski said that in 1944, while walking to work near Gut Alt Golssen, about 30 miles east of Berlin, he experienced a tractor-engine stall in a swampy road area. He later observed an alleged circular vehicle in an otherwise deserted zone guarded by German SS personnel. He placed the vehicle at roughly 500 feet, describing it as circular, 75-100 yards across, about 14 feet high, with dark gray top and bottom sections and a three-foot middle section that appeared as a rapidly moving blurred band around the circumference. He also described a whine or generator-like noise.

**Investigation:** The account says an SS guard spoke with the tractor driver, waited several minutes, and the noise stopped, after which the tractor restarted normally. On a later visit, Krasuski said he saw a circular enclosure screened by a ~50-foot tarpaulin wall, a vertical rise of the object, and uninsulated metal cables running underground between the enclosure and a small concrete column-like structure. He reported that the cables were removed after the war and the area later flooded. The memo also notes he had not been in contact since 1945 with other POW laborers who had discussed the incident, except for remembering one man, Francizek Grabowski. The report is a retrospective wartime recollection, not a contemporaneous airborne sighting, and the source is a single civilian witness with no corroboration in the file excerpt.
001_1944-01-01_Gut Alt Golssen (near Gol.report_summary_zh:

**Sighting:** Perry reported that at about 1:00 a.m. on February 21, 1960, while photographing the moon through a home-made telescope, he took a set of moon photographs. After developing them and viewing the images, he said that one photograph showed what appeared to be a flying object somewhere between the end of the telescope and the surface of the moon.

**Object:** Perry described the object as flat on the bottom when enlarged, oval-shaped, with a fluorescent glow around the entire object and a vapor trail behind it. He believed it was actually moving. He said he had taken over 1,000 moon pictures and had never seen anything resembling it. Based on his photographic experience, he stated he was sure the image was not a camera malfunction, not a blur from the telescope, and not an artifact of film development.

**Investigation:** Perry said he took about twenty moon pictures that night, found most underexposed, cut out the two that appeared properly exposed, destroyed the rest, and furnished both selected pictures to the FBI. The page contains Perry’s statement only and does not record any final Bureau conclusion about the image.

**Document:** FBI Detroit memorandum dated **May 20, 1960** (file **62-HQ-83894**, Section 9), subject **“Unidentified Flying Object; Joseph Perry, Grand Blanc, Michigan – Complainant.”** The page is marked with later archival stamps including **“ALL INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN IS UNCLASSIFIED”** and **“COPIES DESTROYED.”** It is an FBI report containing no recommendation or conclusion.

**Witness:** The principal named individual is **Joseph Perry of Grand Blanc, Michigan**. The report also cites **Jerry Chiappetta** of the *Detroit Times* and **Dave Downey**, identified as District Director of the **Aerial Phenomenon Investigation Society**. Downey is described as the source of the account relayed to the newspaper and then to the FBI.

**Sighting:** Downey said Perry had received a slide from **Selfridge Air Force Base, Mt. Clemens, Michigan, on May 3, 1960**. Perry reportedly claimed the slide showed a photograph of the Moon and that it also showed what appeared to be a flying object near the Moon. The incident is therefore a photographic UFO claim rather than a direct visual sighting, and the exact time of the original exposure is not given on this page.

**Object:** The alleged object is described only as a **flying object** or **UFO** appearing in the vicinity of the Moon on the slide. No size, shape, motion, color, or altitude is provided. The report notes that the Air Force returned the photograph with a letter explaining that the apparent object was **actually part of the negative that was not properly developed**.

**Investigation:** Downey reportedly did **not** accept the Air Force explanation, saying he knew Perry was careful in developing pictures and that the slide likely did contain a real flying object. He intended to obtain the slide and forward it to **Eastman Kodak Company** for further analysis. The FBI memo itself records these competing views without resolving them. This page appears to be the only page in the event scope shown here.

**Witness:** 主要提及的个人是 **Joseph Perry of Grand Blanc, Michigan**。报告还提到了《*Detroit Times*》的 **Jerry Chiappetta**，以及被认定为 **Aerial Phenomenon Investigation Society** 地区主任的 **Dave Downey**。Downey被描述为该说法的来源，此说法先转述给报纸，随后又传到FBI。

001_1960-04-17_Philips Auditorium, City.report_summary:
**Document:** FBI Denver memorandum on letterhead of the U.S. Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigation, dated April 26, 1960. The page is marked “Property of FBI” and is part of FBI file 62-HQ-83894, Section 9. No separate continuation page is present, so the report scope is limited to this single page.

**Witness/Event:** On April 17, 1960, George W. Van Tassel gave a public lecture at Philips Auditorium in City Park, Denver, Colorado. The event was advertised as a lecture, movie film, and discussion of unidentified flying objects and was sponsored by Denver-area unidentified flying objects investigative societies.

**Sighting/Program:** The audience was described as mostly older and mostly female, with few young people apart from some family groups. The program included a 45-minute film with shots said to be flying saucers and interviews with people recounting UFO sightings. After the film, Van Tassel delivered a talk that the writer characterized as more religious-economic than specifically about UFOs.

**Object/Claims:** Van Tassel stated that he had been in the “flying saucer” field for over 30 years and operated a privately owned Civil Aeronautics Authority-approved airfield in California. He claimed personal observation of many sightings, conversations with hundreds of witnesses, and contact with beings from outer space. He presented his work as a crusade to bring these claims to the American public.

**Investigation/Assessment:** The memorandum is descriptive and does not document an independent FBI observation of a UFO. Its value is primarily as a record of a public contactee-style UFO lecture and the speaker’s self-reported background and beliefs, rather than as evidence of a specific aerial incident.

**Event:** Stringfield said he appeared on the television program *Impact News* on WCPO-TV, Cincinnati, on Sunday, September 10, 1961. The caller said he had very important information to relate to Stringfield about unidentified flying objects and asked for Stringfield by name.

**Investigation:** This page is an FBI record of Stringfield’s account, not a UFO observation report with object characteristics. The extant text ends mid-narrative, and no corroboration, analysis, or conclusion appears on this page. The report mainly documents Stringfield’s background, his media appearance, and the anonymous UFO-related contact he received.

001_1961-10-15_Cincinnati, Ohio (Mr. Str.report_summary:
**Document:** Declassified FBI case file 62-HQ-83894, Section 9, typed continuation page marked “-2-” (page 0189). This page contains the second half of an FBI memorandum/report; no signature or report date is visible on the page shown, but it is clearly part of an FBI file concerning UFO-related correspondence and calls.

**Witness:** Leonard H. Stringfield, identified here as a public UFO researcher and adviser to the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena (NICAP). He also stated that he was authorized to report unidentified-object sightings to Air Defense Command headquarters in Columbus, Ohio, which the report uses to explain why he may receive such calls.

**Sighting/Claim:** Stringfield described a telephone call from an unidentified male who refused to identify himself but, according to Stringfield, spoke intelligently and did not sound like a prankster. The caller told him to expect “the biggest flurry of unidentified flying objects sightings” as a result of Russian nuclear explosions “in the one hundred megaton range.” He advised that confusion would begin with these sightings and said, “Mark these dates, October 15 to October 19,” adding that this would be the greatest UFO incident “over the years.” The caller reportedly said he would remain in touch and call back after the nineteenth.

**Assessment:** Stringfield told the FBI he was concerned because the caller seemed serious and because, if true, such a claim could cause public panic. He emphasized that anonymous UFO-related calls were not unusual for him due to his public role. The page records no confirmed visual observation, only an anonymous prediction/warning; the available text does not support any verified UFO event and reads more like an unverified tip or hoax warning than a substantiated sighting.

**Sighting:** Orlando reportedly saw a blue-white flame that appeared to come from “port holes” on a stationary, silent object. He watched for about one minute until the flame went out. He then went into the house, told his father, and returned the next morning to find a smoldering area at the site.

**Object / Ground Effects:** Captain Vigil said he checked the site at about 7:30 PM on April 26. He noted a scorched circular area roughly 30–40 feet in diameter, one rectangular/V-shaped indentation in the ground about 8 by 12 inches and 3–4 inches deep, and three more similar indentations reported by another officer. He also saw several smooth circular prints on the ground about 3.5 inches across.

**Investigation:** The excerpt names no other witnesses and provides no identification of the object. The physical traces make the report more substantial than a simple visual sighting, but the file fragment does not establish a cause. The event remains unresolved in this excerpt; possibilities could include a landing or burn event, but no firm conclusion is documented here.

001_1957-11-03_Levelland, Hockley County.report_summary:
**Document:** Two consecutive Washington City News Service clippings pasted into FBI case file 62-HQ-83894 Sub A (pages p.0014-0015). Both carry the same Levelland, Texas UFO story, with wire codes and a 11/3/57 timestamp, indicating they are continuations of one event report rather than separate incidents.

**Witnesses:** The clipping says Pedro Saucedo, a Levelland motorist, was the first to report the object. Other named witnesses include James Long of Waco and Sheriff Clem, who also observed it with a deputy. A Kermit, Texas motorist is mentioned as a further corroborating witness.

**Sighting:** Around the night of Nov. 2-3, 1957, witnesses reported an egg-shaped object over/near Levelland, described as looking like a "blazing-red sunset" and later as a large intermittently glowing body "like a blinking neon light." It was said to be about 200 feet long, to rise silently, and to disappear in a flash of light. The sheriff reported one sighting at about 11:30 a.m. while looking for earlier reports.

**Effects/Investigation:** Several motorists said the object killed their engines and headlights when they approached it, then left their vehicles functioning normally once it departed. James Long said he drove up to it on the road about 200 feet away; Saucedo reported an explosive thunder-like sound and a loss of engine/headlight power. Authorities reportedly found no burn marks or other evidence at the alleged landing spot, and Air Force Base personnel at Lubbock checked for a possible plane crash but found nothing. The clipping offers no firm identification, but it preserves one of the classic Levelland UFO accounts involving repeated vehicle interference and multiple independent witnesses.

**Witness:** The article centers on Harry Feinaeur, 43, of Birdsboro, identified as the person who submitted the report. Long said he saw an object about 30 feet in front of his automobile near the Allentown Pike and thought it was a saucer. **Object:** The object(s) were ultimately described as a B-36 intercontinental bomber and a jet aircraft flying at roughly 40,000 to 45,000 feet, leaving vapor trails that looked like discs. 001_1947-07-12_Twin Falls, Twin Falls Co.report_summary:
**Document:** Consecutive FBI case-file pages in 62-HQ-83894 Sub A contain two pasted newspaper clippings dated July 12, 1947: an Associated Press item from the *Washington Star* and a United Press item from *Washington News*. Both pages are stamped/recorded by the FBI on July 18, 1947 and routed on a standard HQ cover sheet listing staff names (Tolson, Tamm, Clegg, Glavin, Ladd, Nichols, Rosen, Tracy, Carson, Egan, Gurnea, Harbo, Hendon, Jones, Pennington, Quinn Tamm, Nease, Gandy). The clipping set is clearly part of the same incident file; page 0110 is not a new event, but a second account of the same Twin Falls story.

**Witness:** The apparent complainant is an unnamed Twin Falls, Idaho housewife whose yard received the object. The reporting also references four unnamed teenage boys; because they were juveniles, their names were withheld and they were not prosecuted. No direct FBI interview is shown on these pages, so credibility rests on contemporaneous press reporting and the later Army/FBI assessment.

**Sighting:** The object was said to have fallen “with a thud” in the yard of the housewife in Twin Falls. It was initially treated as a flying-disc/flying-saucer object that drew the attention of local police, FBI, Army intelligence, and civilian military personnel. The incident is dated July 12, 1947 in the clippings, with the object described as having been created over two days.

**Object:** Both clippings conclude the “disc” was a hoax manufactured by four boys from parts of an old phonograph, burned-out radio tubes, discarded electrical/electrical-like parts, plexiglass dome, chromium-plated edges, burned wire, and decorative gold/silver sides. One article says it had no meaningful function beyond ornament and causing investigative expense.

**Investigation:** Army/FBI personnel reportedly examined the gadget after an FBI agent passed it to Army officers at Twin Falls and it was rushed to Ft. Douglas for expert review. The analytical conclusion on these pages is explicit: this was not an authentic aerial phenomenon but a fabricated prank/hoax that had momentarily fooled multiple agencies.

001_1947-07-06_St. Joseph's Church yard,.report_summary:
**Document:** Newspaper clipping preserved in FBI file 62-HQ-83894 Sub A and stamped by the Bureau as received/recorded on 18 Jul 1947. The page is a Washington Post clipping (stamped "THE WASHINGTON POST" with handwritten page/date notation) and carries FBI routing marks, initials, and file notation "Ex-74." No later page in the provided sequence appears to continue this incident.

**Witness:** Rev. Joseph Brasky of St. Joseph's Church in Grafton, Wisconsin, a Catholic priest living about 45 miles north of Milwaukee. He is described as the finder of the object and the person who notified the FBI.

Investigating, he found a warm sheet-metal disc about 18 inches in diameter, about 1/8 inch thick, weighing roughly 4-5 pounds. The article says it resembled a circular saw blade.

**Object:** The disc reportedly had a central hole about one inch across, and in the opening were "gadgets and some wires." Brasky said he did not know whether the object was important or a practical joke, but he held it for the FBI. The article frames it as potentially connected to the then-current "flying saucer" reports.

**Investigation:** The Milwaukee FBI office said it had not yet heard of the disc, though an official report might be at the office. The article also notes the broader national wave of saucer reports and an Army search effort, but offers no confirmation that the Grafton object was an actual aerial craft. Based on the clipping alone, the event is best characterized as a reported ground find of a strange metal object, not a verified flying-disc sighting.

**Witness:** The named civilian witness is Russell Long, identified as a construction engineer. Long described the object as having been "belching smoke" from two exhaust pipes and emitting a blue-white glare before he went outside. The FBI office said an agent had looked at the device and that it would be turned over to military authorities; FBI chief Richard B. Hood declined further comment. On the face of the clipping, this appears more like a recovered homemade/mechanical device or prank than a conventional airborne UFO sighting, though it was filed because of its saucer-like appearance and July 1947 flying-disc context.

001_1994-01-28_Near Coulommiers, Seine-e.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a narrative case-study excerpt headed “1.3 Air France Flight AF 3532 (January 28, 1994)” and continues into the next chapter heading. It is not an original FBI field report form; rather, it summarizes an aviation/UFO incident using operational details from French air-navigation and air-defense sources. The page includes no handwritten annotations, file number, or signer on this page.

**Witness:** Captain Jean-Charles Duboc (P) was flying Air France AF 3532 from Nice to London on January 28, 1994, assisted by Copilot Valérie Chauffour (CP). A chief steward was also present in the cockpit and independently pointed out the phenomenon. The account is strengthened by multiple trained observers who initially disagreed about what they were seeing but quickly converged that it was unlike any known aircraft.

**Sighting:** At 1314 hours, while cruising at 11,900 m near Coulommiers in Seine-et-Marne under excellent meteorological conditions, the crew observed an object at about 10,500 m altitude and roughly 50 km distance. It first seemed like a weather balloon, then like an aircraft banking at 45°, but then changed shape from a brown bell into a chestnut-brown lens before vanishing almost instantaneously off the left side of the aircraft.

**Object:** The crew judged the object to be large based on its apparent diameter, with an estimated length later placed at about 250 m. The report emphasizes the sudden disappearance and the unusual morphology rather than any conventional flight behavior.

**Investigation:** Duboc notified the Reims Air Navigation Control Center, which initially had no corresponding mobile air traffic on radar. Following procedure, Reims alerted the Taverny Air Defense Operations Center (CODA). CODA later recorded a radar track initiated by the Cing-Mars-la-Pile control center that matched the time and location of the sighting, crossed AF 3532’s trajectory, lasted about 50 seconds, and did not match any filed flight plan. CODA concluded the weather-balloon hypothesis was ruled out. The CRNA note says only three similar cases were investigated over seven years, including this one.
001_1994-01-28_Near Coulommiers, Seine-e.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 这页是一段叙事性案例研究摘录，标题为“1.3 Air France Flight AF 3532 (January 28, 1994)”，并延续到下一章标题。它并非原始的 FBI 现场报告表格；相反，它结合法国空中航行和防空来源的作业细节，对一起航空/UFO事件进行了概述。该页不包含手写注释、档案编号或签署人。

**Witness:** Jean-Charles Duboc 船长 (P) 于 1994 年 1 月 28 日驾驶 Air France AF 3532 从 Nice 飞往 London，由副驾驶 Valérie Chauffour (CP) 协助。驾驶舱内还有一名主任乘务员在场，并独立指出了这一现象。该叙述因有多名受过训练的目击者而更具说服力；他们起初对所见之物意见不一，但很快一致认为，这与任何已知飞机都不同。

**Sighting:** 在 1314 hours，飞机以 11,900 m 巡航，于 Seine-et-Marne 的 Coulommiers 附近，在极佳的气象条件下，机组看到一个位于约 10,500 m 高度、距离约 50 km 的物体。它起初看起来像一个气象气球，随后像一架以 45° 倾斜飞行的飞机，但接着又从棕色钟形变成栗褐色透镜状，随后几乎瞬间从飞机左侧消失。

**Object:** 机组根据其表观直径判断该物体很大，后来估计其长度约为 250 m。报告强调的是其突然消失以及异常形态，而不是任何常规飞行行为。

**Investigation:** Duboc 向 Reims 空中航行管制中心报告了此事，该中心最初在雷达上没有发现对应的机动空中交通。按照程序，Reims 通知了 Taverny 防空作战中心 (CODA)。CODA 随后记录到一条由 Cing-Mars-la-Pile 管制中心启动的雷达航迹，该航迹与目击时间和位置相符，穿越了 AF 3532 的飞行轨迹，持续约 50 seconds，且与任何已申报的飞行计划都不一致。CODA 结论认为，气象气球假说已被排除。CRNA 记录指出，在七年间仅调查过三起类似案例，其中包括这一件。

001_1957-07-17_Dallas, Texas area (RB-47.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a narrative account of the well-known RB-47 incident, not a stand-alone signed incident report. The scan has no visible FBI header, file number, classification stamp, or signature block on the page itself; instead it summarizes testimony later discussed by MacDonald in 1969 and compares it with Klass’s analysis.

**Witness:** The main witness named in the text is Commander Chase, the aircraft commander/pilot, with corroborating observations from Captain MacCoyd (copilot), Captain Provenzano, and electronic/radar observer MacClure. The page says six officers were interviewed and that three additional officers in the cockpit could also see outside the aircraft, strengthening the credibility of the account.

**Sighting:** The encounter unfolded during the RB-47’s northbound return from the Gulf of Mexico toward the Mississippi coast and then across Louisiana and Texas. Around 0930Z over Mississippi, MacClure saw a radar blip behind and to the right of the aircraft that passed it, arced around, and reappeared on the left; the pulse characteristics matched ground radar except for shorter 2-microsecond pulses. Around 1010Z in Louisiana, Chase and MacCoyd saw an intense bluish-white light that moved from left to right and vanished. At 1030Z a similar signal reappeared from about 2 o’clock and was confirmed by another detector. Near Dallas, Utah radar tracked both the aircraft and an object holding a constant 18 km separation. At 1039Z Chase saw a large red light apparently below the aircraft, and at 1042Z the object turned toward Dallas; by about 1050Z west of Dallas it stopped and disappeared from both radar and visual contact.

**Object:** The object was reported as airborne, fast-moving, and apparently responsive to the aircraft, with radar returns suggesting a microwave source and visual appearances ranging from bluish-white to red. The author notes that some sightings could have involved meteors or optical effects, but the radar/visual correlation and persistent tracking made a simple explanation difficult.

**Investigation:** The page emphasizes that the crew initially suspected an electronics malfunction, then later reported the contacts to Utah radar. The narrative concludes that, while some details remain debatable, the episode presented multiple independent radar and visual observations over a long flight path, and it remains one of the stronger historical military UFO cases.
001_1957-07-17_Dallas, Texas area (RB-47.report_summary_zh:

**Witness:** 文中提到的主要证人是 Chase 指挥官，亦即飞机指挥官/飞行员，另有 McCoyd 舰长（副驾驶）、Provenzano 舰长以及电子/雷达观察员 MacClure 的佐证。该页称共有六名军官接受了采访，并且驾驶舱内另外三名军官也能看到机外情况，这进一步增强了该叙述的可信度。

**Sighting:** 这次遭遇发生在 RB-47 从墨西哥湾向北返回、飞越 Mississippi 海岸，随后经过 Louisiana 和 Texas 的途中。约在 0930Z，位于 Mississippi 上空时，MacClure 看到飞机后方右侧有一个雷达回波点，随后该目标超越飞机，绕弧形机动后又出现在左侧；其脉冲特征与地面雷达相符，但脉冲宽度较短，为 2 微秒。约在 1010Z、位于 Louisiana 上空时，Chase 和 McCoyd 看见一道强烈的蓝白色光点从左向右移动并消失。到 1030Z 时，同样的信号又从大约 2 点钟方向出现，并被另一台探测器证实。在接近 Dallas 时，Utah 雷达同时跟踪到了飞机和一个始终保持 18 km 间距的目标。1039Z，Chase 看到一团巨大的红色光点，似乎位于飞机下方；1042Z 时，该目标转向 Dallas；到大约 1050Z，在 Dallas 西侧，它停止并从雷达与目视中同时消失。

001_1956-08-13_RAF Lakenheath / RAF Bent.report_summary:
**Document:** This page is a secondary-source case writeup, section 2.1, titled "Lakenheath (United Kingdom) (August 13-14, 1956)." It is not an original FBI memo on the page shown; instead it summarizes a military UFO case and cites later analyses, including the 1969 Condon Commission report, a 1971 study by Thayer in *Astronautics and Aeronautics*, and a 1976 critique by Philippe Klass. No FBI file number, classification marking, signer, or originating office is visible on this page.

**Witness:** The incident was reported by multiple independent observers: Bentwaters base radar/control personnel, a Bentwaters control-tower observer, a military transport pilot flying over Bentwaters, and later Lakenheath radar operators and the shift supervisor. The narrative emphasizes concurrence between radar and visual observations, which is presented as strengthening credibility.

**Sighting:** On the night of 13-14 August 1956, around 2255 hours, radar at Bentwaters detected an unidentified object moving east to west over the base at an estimated 2,000-4,000 mph (3,200-6,400 km/h), with no sonic boom reported. At the same time, control-tower personnel saw a bright light traveling east to west at "an incredible speed" at roughly 1,200 m altitude, and a military transport pilot said a bright light passed beneath his aircraft in the same direction and at similar speed.

**Object:** The page also describes a second radar contact near Lakenheath: a stationary object about 40 km southwest of the base, on the projected track of the earlier object, which later accelerated from apparent immobility to 600-950 km/h. The object is described only as an unidentified aerial object/bright light; no shape, size, color detail, or sound signature beyond the absence of a sonic boom is given.

**Investigation:** Bentwaters radar personnel reported the sightings to Lakenheath air traffic control, which confirmed a related radar target and alerted the base commander. The text states that the Condon Commission later judged the case "unidentified," while subsequent authors disputed or tried to conventionalize parts of the event. On this page alone, the case remains unresolved and is treated as a significant concurrent radar/visual UFO incident over eastern England.

**Witness:** The main witness is the **pilot of Aerolíneas Argentinas flight AR 674** (Boeing 727), with corroboration from the rest of the crew, passengers, the crew of another aircraft on standby, airport controllers, and some local inhabitants.

**Sighting:** On final approach to land at San Carlos de Bariloche, the town lost power and the airport lights went out. It had **three lights**, including **one red light in the middle**. When airport lighting failed again, the runway and approach lights also extinguished. The same phenomenon was observed from the second aircraft on standby.

**Object:** The object later became luminous, moved behind the airplane, stopped, climbed vertically, stopped again, then moved back in front of the airplane before disappearing toward the **Andes Cordillera**. The account emphasizes unusual maneuverability and sustained visibility over several minutes.

**Assessment:** The report highlights the case as noteworthy because it was independently observed in flight and on the ground, lasted several minutes, involved multiple apparent trajectories, and coincided with an electromagnetic effect (widespread light failure) that the report treats as directly associated with the object. 001_1965-07-01_Valensole (lavender field.report_summary:

The bottom of the page begins a new, separate incident (“4.2 Cussac, Cantal”), which is not part of this event.

**Witness:** Maurice Masse left home at about 5:00 a.m. for his lavender fields near Valensole and began work around 6:00 a.m. He is described as the sole eyewitness. The report says he was later questioned by local gendarmes, and that investigators found no indication of mythomania or a staged hoax.

**Sighting:** While lighting a cigarette, Masse heard a hissing sound and saw an object about 90 meters away behind a pile of stones. He approached to roughly 10 meters, thinking it might be thieves. He then observed two small beings; one reportedly pointed a tube at him from a bag on its left side. Masse said he became immobilized, numb, and paralyzed but remained fully aware. After the beings reentered the craft, he watched from behind a dome-like structure as a heavy sound accompanied takeoff.

**Object:** He described the craft as reminiscent of a “Dauphine” automobile on six legs with a central pivot. The tube under the object touched the ground and rotated; the six legs retracted beneath the machine. The object rose vertically, tilted diagonally, and departed faster than a jet.

**Investigation:** Gendarmerie and Digne investigators reportedly found a ground depression with soaked soil, a smooth-walled cylindrical hole about 18 cm across and 40 cm deep, and three bent holes about 6 cm across. Lavender along the flight path was dried out over roughly 100 meters, and replanting failed for years. The report concludes that the physical traces and witness reaction made the account plausible despite some contradictions.

001_1976-09-18_Tehran, Iran (above the S.report_summary:

**Witness:** The first-hand observer named here is Hossain Perouzi, the Tehran airport night-shift controller. Additional observations are attributed to General Youssefi of the Imperial Iranian Air Force and to two F-4 crews.

**Sighting:** Around 11:00 p.m. on 18 Sep 1976, the Tehran airport control tower received multiple calls about a stationary luminous object over the Shemiran residential district in northern Tehran. Perouzi viewed it with binoculars and described a rectangle, probably a cylindrical object, with bluish-white pulsing lights at both ends and a small red light in the center tracing a circle. Youssefi also saw an object like a star but much larger and brighter, and he ordered an F-4 intercept.

**Object/Effects:** When the first F-4 closed to about 45 km, its flight instruments and communications reportedly stopped working; the pilot aborted the interception and returned to base, after which the crew regained use of the systems. A second F-4 tracked a radar echo similar to a Boeing 707. As it approached at roughly 280 km/h relative speed, the target accelerated and maintained a constant 45 km separation. The page presents the case as a multi-witness visual-and-radar incident with alleged electromagnetic interference, but it offers no final explanation.

Their accounts were broadly consistent and included visual, auditory, and environmental effects.

**Sighting:** On the night of March 10–11, 1979, the first witness described a bluish, purplish luminous mass, slightly oval and about 15 meters long. He said the village square was lit as bright as daylight and the automatic public lighting shut off. Two motorists said the luminous mass moved about 2 meters in front of their car, and that the light went out suddenly after orange-colored lights appeared on both sides of the glow. The fish farmer said he woke to a dull noise, saw a bright bluish glow, and later found fish dead in one tank.

That electrical event was judged sufficient to explain the bluish glow, the noise, and the failure of the village lighting; the glow was also bright enough to trigger a nearby photoelectric cell. The fish deaths were attributed to aluminum droplets falling into the tank, supporting an electrical-origin explanation rather than a true UFO event.

**Witness:** The principal witness was an **auto mechanic driving on the Paris–Lille freeway**. He was accompanied by his family, who were also treated as part of the follow-up response after the sighting. **Sighting:** On 1988-09-29, the driver saw an **enormous red ball** cross the road a few dozen meters in front of him and roll down below the roadway, emitting reflections and appearing enveloped in dense smoke. The event caused alarm; highway gendarmes sealed off the freeway and a multi-kilometer zone around the object. Civilian and military security personnel arrived with **Geiger counters**, and the witness and family underwent hospital examinations. At the time, officials briefly considered a possible link to the Soviet satellite **Cosmos 1900**.

**Object / Conclusion:** When CNES was consulted, it was quickly confirmed that Cosmos 1900 was not involved. The object was later identified as a **decorative sphere for a Jean-Michel Jarre concert** that had fallen from the truck transporting it to London. The sphere’s mirrored surface and intact appearance explained the light reflections; no smoke or radioactivity was found near it. The page’s analytical point is that a dramatic “UFO” report can arise from an ordinary transported object, even after an extensive official response.

AUS-UFO-WOOMERA-MARALINGA-1960.report_summary:
**Document:** National Archives of Australia record from **Series A6456** (Control Symbol **R029/284**), part of Department of Supply / Weapons Research Establishment material on unexplained aerial sightings linked to the **Woomera–Maralinga** test range.

**Background:** Woomera and Maralinga were sensitive defence and weapons-testing sites, so unusual lights or aircraft-like observations were often treated as both a security issue and a reportable incident. These files sit within the broader Australian government response to UFO/UAS reports in the Cold War era.

AUS-UFO-RAAF-AFIS-PUBLIC-ENQUIRY-1982-19.report_summary_zh:
**Document:**  
澳大利亚国家档案馆（National Archives of Australia）保存的 RAAF 空军情报与安全部门面向公众及民间的 UFO 查询档案（Series A9755, control symbol 22）。该档案跨越 **1982–1994**，保存了与澳大利亚公众对 UFO / 未知空中目击的兴趣相关的官方往来函件和案件处理记录。

**Background:**  
到 1980 年代和 1990 年代初，UFO 报告通常作为公众咨询来处理，而不再是 RAAF 的常设调查项目。此类档案记录了 RAAF 如何接收、登记并回应平民报告，往往是在公众好奇、当地媒体关注以及要求官方发表评论的背景下进行的。

**Event / Contents:**  
该档案可能包含平民来信、目击者陈述、咨询回复以及 RAAF 内部处理备忘。凡有报告提交，其中可能包括基本的目击细节，例如时间、地点、移动方向、亮度、形状、持续时间，以及任何辅助观察，如雷达记录或其他目击者的证词。档案中也可能提及将事项转交其他机构，或就报告渠道向咨询者提供建议。

**Notable witnesses or sources:**  
这是一份记录档案，而非某一单一著名事件档案，因此元数据中未标明具体目击者。其主要来源是公众来函者、民间观察者以及 RAAF 行政往来文件。

**Significance:**  
该档案显示，尽管这一议题逐渐从正式调查转向行政回应与档案保存，澳大利亚国防部门在 20 世纪后期仍持续管理公众对 UFO 的关注。

**Where this fits:**  
适合研究者追踪 1970 年代后澳大利亚 UAS 报告史、公众向 RAAF 提出的咨询，以及官方对无法解释的空中目击所作回应的更广泛档案线索。

003_nzdf_air39_v1_2010-09-01_1955-12-17_.report_summary:
**Witness:** A mother sitting in a car in Park Avenue, Takapuna, with her baby, and the woman driving the car.

**Sighting:** They reported a light in the sky, first noticed while the car was being driven up a rise in Park Avenue.

**Object:** The light was described as very brilliant, green, bigger and different in shape from a normal light, and not a star, beacon, or navigation light.

**Tactics:** It appeared to travel in a northerly direction, lasted about 4–5 seconds, and was seen at a fairly low elevation before moving off at tremendous speed.

**Note:** The message states the beacon was not operating at the time and the witness emphasized the light was not a star.
003_nzdf_air39_v1_2010-09-01_1955-12-17_.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一位坐在Takapuna Park Avenue 车内的母亲，怀中抱着婴儿，以及开车的另一名女子。

**目击经过：** 她们报告说在天空中看到一道光，最初是在汽车沿 Park Avenue 上坡行驶时注意到的。

**物体：** 该光被描述为非常明亮、呈绿色、比普通灯光更大，形状也不同，不是星星、灯塔或航行灯。

**行动特征：** 它似乎向北飞去，持续约4至5秒，在较低高度可见，然后以极快速度离开。

**备注：** 电报指出当时旋转灯塔未在运行，目击者也强调这不是一颗星。

003_nzdf_air39_v1_2010-09-01_1955-11-04_.report_summary:
**Witness:** Mr D. W. Paul of Herndon Avenue, Avondale, and an Auckland taxi-driver.

**Sighting:** Early yesterday morning, while driving in Avondale, they saw a bright object in the sky moving silently at great speed from left to right.

**Object:** It was described as lighted, long, with three or four lighted windows much bigger than normal aircraft windows, and making no noise.

**Tactics:** The object was visible for about four minutes, then vanished into a cloud bank; shortly after, an RNZAF Sunderland aircraft was seen landing with its lights blinking.

**Note:** The newspaper account says the object was “completely different” from the later aircraft sighting.
003_nzdf_air39_v1_2010-09-01_1955-11-04_.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** Avondale 的 Herndon Avenue 居民 D. W. Paul 先生，以及一名奥克兰出租车司机。

**目击经过：** 昨日清晨，两人在 Avondale 驾车时，看见空中有一发光物体，以极快速度无声地从左向右移动。

**物体：** 据描述它带有灯光，外形较长，似有三四个亮着的窗户，窗户比普通飞机窗大得多，而且没有任何噪音。

**轨迹：** 该物体持续可见约四分钟，随后消失在云层中；不久后又看见一架 RNZAF Sunderland 飞机开着灯着陆。

**备注：** 报纸称这次所见物体与随后看到的那架飞机“完全不同”。

003_nzdf_air39_v1_2010-09-01_1954-11-01_.report_summary:
**Witness:** Captain R. S. Cohen of an N.A.C. airliner, with passengers aboard, observed the light on a Monday night flight.

**Sighting:** The aircraft was flying north from New Plymouth when a bright, mysterious light was seen and later discussed in newspaper reports the next day.

**Object:** Described as a strange flying light; one report says it was definitely not Venus, and another notes it appeared to change colour.

**Tactics:** The pilot and others watched it from the aircraft and compared it against possible explanations, but no conventional source was identified.

**Note:** This is a press-clipped account of a concrete sighting event, not a cover sheet or editorial.
003_nzdf_air39_v1_2010-09-01_1954-11-01_.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** N.A.C. 航空公司飞行员 R. S. Cohen 船长，以及机上乘客，都看到了这道光。

**目击经过：** 飞机在一个星期一晚上从新普利茅斯向北飞行时，看到了一道明亮而神秘的光，次日在报纸中被继续报道。

**物体：** 被描述为奇怪的飞行光；一则报道称它“绝不是金星”，另一则说它似乎会变色。

**行为：** 飞行员和其他人从机上持续观察，并尝试比对各种解释，但未找到常规来源。

**说明：** 这是一则关于具体目击事件的报纸剪报，不是封面页或社论。

003_nzdf_air39_v1_2010-09-01_1955-11-24_.report_summary:
**Witness:** The newspaper clipping quotes Napier locals, including Mr. W. Magee, who had seen the light on more than one occasion.

**Sighting:** On 24 Nov 1955, people in Napier reported a bright light/object over the town and harbour area, seen moving across the sky and then altering its appearance.

**Object:** It was described as a compact brilliant white light that became a larger blurred orange glow, later seeming to fade or change shape.

**Tactics:** The object was seen moving steadily and then changing colour/size, drawing renewed attention because it had been observed before.

**Note:** This is a press report about a concrete local sighting, not a contactee account.
003_nzdf_air39_v1_2010-09-01_1955-11-24_.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 这则报纸剪报提到内皮尔（Napier）当地居民，包括 W. Magee 先生在内，他们并非第一次看到该光点。

**目击：** 1955年11月24日，内皮尔居民报告称在城镇与港口上空看见一个明亮的物体/光点，在天空中移动并改变外观。

**物体：** 其被描述为一个紧凑、极亮的白色光点，随后变成较大的模糊橙色光团，之后似乎又减弱或变形。

**行为：** 该物体以平稳方式移动，并发生颜色与大小变化，因此再次引起注意。

**备注：** 这是一则关于具体本地目击事件的新闻报道，不是接触者叙述。

003_nzdf_air39_v1_2010-09-01_1955-11-26_.report_summary:
