**Witnesses:** Paul Cernick, Cindy Hyatt, and Bradley Hyatt.

**Sighting:** On August 11, 1980, at 11:05Z, four separate sightings occurred at Shaw Park in Yorkton, Saskatchewan. The weather was reported as cloudy. Each sighting lasted approximately 20 seconds, with 15 minutes between each event. The objects were observed moving in a westerly direction, with two sets passing directly overhead, one set to the north, and one set to the south of the observers.

**Object:** The objects were described as circular and orange in color, positioned below the cloud cover. They moved slowly from east to west. There were nine objects in each sighting. No noise was associated with the sightings, and they were not considered meteorites due to the lack of tails.

**Aftermath:** The report was filed by CFS Yorkton to the NRC/Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics.

**Witnesses:** Mark Robert Mose, Shirley Murphy, Norman Allan Perry, and Dr. Linda Ann Witham.

**Sighting:** On November 25, 1980, four individuals reported seeing an unidentified flying object in the vicinity of Elnora, Alberta. Mark Robert Mose reported a sighting north of Elnora at approximately 8:40 p.m. Shirley Murphy reported a sighting just east of Elnora at 6:20 p.m. Norman Allan Perry reported a sighting southeast of Elnora. Dr. Linda Ann Witham also reported an observation on the same date.

**Object:** The reports describe an unidentified flying object. The witness accounts roughly coincide regarding the description and direction of the object.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP officer, Cst. H.W. Trupish, noted that the witnesses had no contact with each other prior to providing their statements and appeared sincere. While Canadian Forces Base at Penhold confirmed a meteor shower occurred at 6:00 p.m. on the same date, all four witnesses maintained that what they observed was not a meteor.

**Additional pages:** This incident is also documented on 3 other pages of the FOIA release.

**物体：** 报告描述了一个不明飞行物。目击者的陈述在物体的描述和方向上大致吻合。

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警警官 H.W. Trupish 指出，目击者在提供陈述前彼此并无接触，且表现诚恳。尽管加拿大武装部队彭霍尔德基地证实当天晚上6:00有流星雨，但所有四名目击者均坚持认为他们所见并非流星。

**Witnesses:** Gordon Allan, Margaret Allan, and Mr. Allan are named in the account. The writer says they were asked whether they had seen anything after the light appeared about as far away as the farm of their friends.

**Aftermath:** Mr. Allan suggested phoning Flight Service Station, Transport Canada, at the Peace River Airport. The final visible line begins, “The man who answered the phone,” but the rest of that sentence is cut off on this page.

**Witnesses:** A civilian driver.

**Sighting:** At approximately 10:00 p.m. E.S.T. on April 6, 1981, the witness observed a circular object while driving. The sky was clear and stars were visible. The witness was approximately 8 miles west of Myrnam at the initial point of the sighting. As the witness approached Myrnam, reaching a point 1 to 1.5 miles west of the town, the object appeared to get larger and much closer.

**Object:** The object was described as greyish-white with a dull red color on the bottom. It appeared to be at an altitude of approximately 1 to 1.5 miles. The witness stopped their car for about 30 seconds to observe the object, during which time it appeared to remain stationary. As the witness drove into Myrnam, they lost sight of the object due to buildings.

**Aftermath:** The witness noted that while posting signs in Myrnam, they kept their eye level with the roof of a garage to see if there was any further movement.

**Additional pages:** This incident is also documented on 1 other page of the FOIA release.

**Witnesses:** Mr. Reid Sears and Mike Lucano.

**Sighting:** On April 8, 1981, between 0800 and 0830Z, in partially cloudy conditions, two sightings were reported near Burks Falls, Ontario, specifically at Renard Lake Road.

**Object:** The object was described as oval-shaped, blue/green in color, and encircled by a white haze. It appeared to be approximately 300-500 feet away. The first sighting involved the object moving up and down in a vertical motion. The second sighting involved the object moving horizontally across the lake.

**Aftermath:** The sightings were reported to the NRC for the Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics. The report notes that there was no sound associated with the sightings, which were separated by 15 and 20 seconds.

**Witnesses:** William James Schnare (pharmaceutical representative) and Peter Gregory King (truck driver).

**Sighting:** On April 13, 1981, between 1930 and 2035 hours AST, witnesses observed an object while traveling on Highway 103 from Halifax to East Chester. Schnare observed the object for 40 minutes, while King observed it for approximately five minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as cigar-shaped with a small white light on the front and rear, a white light on each side halfway back, and a red light in the center. **见证者：** 该页面描述了一位个人在威斯康星州斯坦格尔维尔以北1英里、以东3/4英里的农场使用观测镜所做的记录。

**目击：** 1981年11月28日至30日期间，基沃尼县记录了多次目击事件。观测内容包括各种光点、闪光单元在不同方向（北、南、北北西）移动。11月29日，观察到一个物体在进行不规则移动。11月30日凌晨4点55分，在富兰克林镇附近，一个物体被确认为圆盘状。目击者报告称，该圆盘在观测镜下翻转，并进行了180度翻转。

**Witnesses:** The document refers to the "Michalak file," identifying the primary witness as Michalak. The name P. M. Millman is also typed on the page, likely representing the researcher or official at the Meteor Centre.

**Sighting:** This page contains a detailed hand-drawn sketch of a saucer-shaped craft. The drawing includes specific measurements and technical annotations describing the physical characteristics of the object observed.

Features include a "3 x 3 fast closing exit" and the emission of "red, green, and violet light." An arrow indicates the craft exhibited "anticlockwise rotation."

**Aftermath:** The sketch is identified as a copy of an 8x10 photo from File No. 200 at the Meteor Centre, UAR/REED/NRC. It is officially categorized as a "Non-Meteoric Sighting."

**目击：** 在 1100z，约 20 个奇怪的灯光被目视到，方向是从北向南，飞越 DLP。它们似乎沿着一条路径朝天空中一个极其明亮、静止不动的物体移动。随后，其中 3 个奇怪物体改变方向，在该静止物体左侧形成了一个三角形。记录写明这些物体以一致速度快速移动。

**物体：** 本页将其描述为“奇怪的灯光”和“极其明亮的静止物体”，但除上述行为外，没有给出大小、颜色、高度或其他识别细节。

**后续：** 较早的条目写有 0310z “COMSEC destruct complete...agc”，以及 0410z “All radar checks complete for Voodoo Flt...kgg”。页面上还有其他带时间的行，但文字被遮挡或删去。本页未见明确的公历日期。

**其它相关页面：** 本 DLP 报告覆盖 CIRVIS Canada 2010-2019 档案的第 166 – 169 页（第 167 页为目击主页面；第 166、168、169 页为报告表、汇总表与后续通讯）。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A 36-year-old civilian (the same individual is the primary witness across both pages).

**Date / Time:** January 3, 1969, at approximately 9:30 PM.

**Location:** Port Arthur/Lakehead, Ontario (specifically Highway 11 between Port Arthur and Sunshine, the junction of Highway 11 and 17, and the area near the Fort William airport).

**Sighting:** On the evening of January 3, 1969, the witness was driving west on Highway 11 between Port Arthur and Sunshine when they observed a bright light hovering above the treetops. The object initially rose and moved behind a hill. Later, near the junction of Highway 11 and 17, the witness observed the object again, hovering over the treetops. The witness watched the object for nearly an hour from a laneway. Upon entering Fort William near the airport, the object appeared again, heading toward the airport, swooping down, and then the light went out. 

The witness reported that this light had been seen continuously over the Lakehead area, typically first sighted about an hour before dusk. During observations, the witness utilized eyeglasses and binoculars to track the object. The witness noted that the object would move forward with a burst of speed, stop and hang in the air, then revolve around and around. At times, it would shoot off in a slightly different direction, stop, and remain above the treetops. The witness also observed a jet plane in the vicinity at the same time, noting that the object appeared larger than the jet. The witness returned to the same location the following night with binoculars and observed the object again.

**Object:** The object was described as a very bright light of immense size. It featured red flashing lights around its center. While hovering over the treetops, small pinpoints of light were observed shooting to and from the larger lights. The object exhibited erratic movement, including bursts of speed, hovering, revolving, and sudden directional changes. It made no reported sound.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The witness expressed strong skepticism regarding official reports circulating at the time, which claimed the object was a weather balloon released from the United States. The witness explicitly disputed this explanation, maintaining that the object was something else entirely. The witness concluded their account by urging that the matter be investigated further and that official findings be published so that the public could be informed about the activity occurring in the skies above them.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 一名36岁的平民（该名人士为两页记录中的主要目击者）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年1月3日，晚上约9:30。

**地点：** 安大略省亚瑟港（Port Arthur）/ 湖首（Lakehead）地区（具体地点包括亚瑟港至阳光镇（Sunshine）之间的11号公路、11号与17号公路交汇处，以及威廉堡（Fort William）机场附近区域）。

**目击经过：** 1969年1月3日晚，目击者正驾车沿11号公路向西行驶，在亚瑟港至阳光镇之间，观察到一个明亮的光体悬浮在树梢上方。该物体起初上升并移动到一座小山后方。随后，在11号与17号公路的交汇处附近，目击者再次观察到该物体悬浮在树梢上。目击者从一条小路旁观察了该物体近一个小时。当进入威廉堡机场附近时，该物体再次出现，向机场方向飞去，俯冲而下，随后光芒熄灭。

目击者报告称，该光体在湖首地区被持续观察到，通常在黄昏前约一小时首次出现。在观察过程中，目击者使用了眼镜和双筒望远镜来追踪该物体。目击者指出，该物体会以极快的速度向前冲刺，随后停住并悬停在空中，接着不断旋转。有时，它会突然转向另一个方向，停下并保持在树梢上方。目击者同时观察到附近有一架喷气式飞机，并指出该物体的外观比飞机更大。次日晚上，目击者带着双筒望远镜回到同一地点，再次观察到了该物体。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个体积极其巨大的明亮光体。其中心周围有红色的闪烁灯光。当悬浮在树梢上方时，可以看到微小的光点在较大的灯光之间来回穿梭。该物体表现出不规则的运动轨迹，包括加速冲刺、悬停、旋转以及突然改变方向。据报告，该物体未发出任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 目击者对当时流传的官方报告表示强烈怀疑，该报告声称该物体是美国释放的气象气球。目击者明确反驳了这一解释，坚持认为该物体完全是其他东西。目击者在陈述结尾处敦促对此事进行进一步调查，并要求公布官方调查结果，以便公众了解在他们头顶的天空中究竟发生了什么。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** John Rae, Walter Lautrup, Van Jacobson, and Edward Rae (Superintendent of Kootenay National Park).

**Date / Time:** March 11, 1969, at 7:30 PM MST.

**Location:** Approximately 30 miles west of Radium Hot Springs, BC, specifically situated between Mt. Abbott and Mt. Stockdale.

**Sighting:** On the evening of March 11, 1969, four witnesses—John Rae, Walter Lautrup, Van Jacobson, and Edward Rae—observed an event they collectively interpreted as an aircraft crash. The weather conditions at the time were reported as clear. The witnesses observed a distinct vertical smoke trail that reached an altitude of approximately 10,000 feet. Following the descent of the object, a large amount of dark smoke was seen billowing from the ground at the impact site. This smoke remained visible for approximately 15 minutes. The witnesses, particularly John Rae, were noted by the RCMP as being highly reliable individuals, and their consensus was that they had witnessed a plane going down.

**Object:** The object was perceived by all witnesses as an aircraft. Its primary physical characteristics included a vertical descent path and the creation of a significant, dark smoke trail that extended to 10,000 feet. Upon reaching the ground, the object produced a large, billowing volume of smoke that persisted for 15 minutes. No sound or specific shape details beyond the smoke trail and the assumption of an aircraft were recorded.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the reports, the RCMP conducted an inquiry with the Department of Transport (D.O.T.) to determine if any aircraft were overdue or missing; the D.O.T. confirmed that no aircraft were reported missing in the sub-division. On March 13, 1969, Mr. Duncan McIntosh (also referred to as MacIntosh) volunteered to conduct an aerial scan of the area in his private plane, accompanied by the NCO in charge of the Radium Detachment. Additionally, on March 12, 1969, an official Albatross aircraft was deployed to search the area. Both the private and official searches yielded negative results, with nothing sighted at the location. The information regarding the sighting and the subsequent search efforts was formally passed to the Rescue Co-ordination Centre to determine if further search operations were required. The RCMP maintained their assessment that the witnesses were very reliable, despite the lack of physical evidence found during the aerial sweeps.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 约翰·雷 (John Rae)、沃尔特·劳特鲁普 (Walter Lautrup)、范·雅各布森 (Van Jacobson) 以及爱德华·雷 (Edward Rae，库特尼国家公园负责人)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年3月11日，山区标准时间 (MST) 晚上7:30。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省镭温泉镇 (Radium Hot Springs) 以西约30英里处，具体位于阿博特山 (Mt. Abbott) 和斯托克代尔山 (Mt. Stockdale) 之间。

**目击经过：** 1969年3月11日晚，四名目击者——约翰·雷、沃尔特·劳特鲁普、范·雅各布森和爱德华·雷——共同目击了一起他们认为的飞机坠毁事件。据报告，当时天气晴朗。目击者观察到一条明显的垂直烟迹，高度达到约10,000英尺。物体坠落后，撞击地点冒出大量浓烟。这些烟雾持续可见约15分钟。加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 指出，目击者（尤其是约翰·雷）是非常可靠的人，他们一致认为自己目睹了一架飞机坠毁。

**物体描述：** 所有目击者都认为该物体是一架飞机。其主要物理特征包括垂直的下降轨迹，以及产生了一条延伸至10,000英尺高的显著浓烟轨迹。物体落地后，产生了大量持续15分钟的滚滚浓烟。除了烟迹和对飞机身份的推测外，没有记录到任何声音或具体的形状细节。

**调查/后续：** 报告发出后，加拿大皇家骑警向交通部 (D.O.T.) 进行了查询，以确定是否有飞机逾期未归或失踪；交通部确认该分区没有飞机失踪的报告。1969年3月13日，邓肯·麦金托什先生 (Mr. Duncan McIntosh) 自愿驾驶其私人飞机，在镭温泉镇分遣队负责警官的陪同下对该区域进行了空中扫描。此外，1969年3月12日，一架官方的信天翁 (Albatross) 飞机也被部署到该区域进行搜索。私人搜索和官方搜索均未发现任何结果，在现场一无所获。有关此次目击事件及后续搜索工作的信息已正式移交给救援协调中心，以确定是否需要进一步的搜索行动。尽管在空中搜寻中未发现任何实物证据，加拿大皇家骑警仍坚持认为目击者非常可靠。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Yves Parré (also referred to as Yves Lasse), an unnamed friend.

**Date / Time:** March 15, 1969, at approximately 20:45 hours.

**Location:** Fabreville / St-Laurent, Quebec.

**Sighting:** On the evening of March 15, 1969, at 20:45, two witnesses—Yves Parré and an unnamed friend—were driving in the Fabreville area when they observed a luminous, bright red object in the northeast sky. At the time of the sighting, the sky was completely overcast, rendering stars invisible. The witnesses observed the object remaining stationary for several seconds before it suddenly disappeared in a northeasterly direction. Based on the object's speed, its distinct red color, and the fact that it did not twinkle or flash, the witnesses concluded that the object was not a conventional airplane. Troubled by the encounter and driven by personal curiosity, the witnesses contacted the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) to inquire about the nature of the light.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright, luminous red light. It appeared stationary for a few seconds before moving away. The witnesses noted that the light did not flash or twinkle, and its speed and movement patterns were inconsistent with those of an aircraft.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was reported to the National Research Council of Canada. On March 28, 1969, Peter M. Millman, the Head of Upper Atmosphere Research, provided a formal response to M. Yves Parré. Millman stated that, due to the limited amount of specific detail provided in the report, he was unable to definitively identify the origin of the light. Taking into account the overcast weather conditions reported at the time, Millman suggested that the object was likely either an unconventional type of aircraft light or a reflection of a terrestrial light source.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_03_-_Pages_60.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 伊夫·帕雷（Yves Parré，也被称为伊夫·拉塞 Yves Lasse），以及一位未具名的朋友。

**日期 / 时间：** 1969年3月15日，约20:45。

**地点：** 魁北克省法布尔维尔（Fabreville）/ 圣洛朗（St-Laurent）。

**目击经过：** 1969年3月15日晚20:45，两名目击者——伊夫·帕雷和一位未具名的朋友——在法布尔维尔地区驾车时，观察到东北方向的天空中出现了一个明亮的红色发光物体。目击当时天空完全被云层覆盖，无法看到星星。目击者观察到该物体静止了数秒，随后突然向东北方向消失。基于该物体的速度、独特的红色，以及它既不闪烁也不发光的特点，目击者断定该物体并非传统飞机。由于这次遭遇令他们感到困惑，出于个人好奇，目击者联系了加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）以询问该光源的性质。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一团明亮的红色光团。它在移动前静止了几秒钟。目击者指出，该光团没有闪烁，其速度和运动模式与飞机不符。

**调查/后续：** 此目击事件被报告给了加拿大国家研究委员会。1969年3月28日，高层大气研究负责人彼得·M·米尔曼（Peter M. Millman）向伊夫·帕雷先生作出了正式回复。米尔曼表示，由于报告中提供的具体细节有限，他无法明确确定该光源的来源。考虑到当时报告的阴天天气状况，米尔曼推测该物体很可能是一种非常规的飞机灯光，或者是地面光源的反射。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_16_-_Pages_45.report_summary:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A family residing on Deepdale Road and an investigating RCMP officer.

**Sighting:** On July 20, 1968, at approximately 11:30 PM, the RCMP received a call regarding a bright light in the sky. The family reported observing a luminous object at an altitude of approximately 10,000 feet. Upon the family's arrival at their home, the object moved in a northerly direction at a high rate of speed before stopping and remaining stationary for one hour. A second object was also noted at the same altitude to the east of the farm, which lit up the nearby barn.

**Object:** The objects appeared to be round and emitted brilliant layers of red, green, and white light. The objects made no noise when moving. The exact shape was difficult to determine due to the intensity of the light.

**Aftermath:** An RCMP officer patrolled the scene and observed a bright object in the sky for ten minutes with no change in position. Further inquiries at other farms in the area yielded negative results, and no other reports were received.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Deepdale路的一户家庭以及一名进行调查的加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）警官。

**目击：** 1968年7月20日晚上约11:30，加拿大皇家骑警接到关于天空中出现亮光的报告。该家庭报告称观察到一个位于约10,000英尺高度的发光物体。当该家庭抵达家中时，该物体以极高的速度向北移动，随后停止并保持静止状态长达一小时。在农场东侧的同一高度还发现了第二个物体，其光线照亮了附近的谷仓。

**物体：** 这些物体看起来呈圆形，并发出红、绿、白色的绚丽光芒。物体移动时没有发出任何声音。由于光线强度过大，无法确定其确切形状。

**后续：** 一名加拿大皇家骑警警官前往现场巡逻，并观察到天空中有一个亮光，持续了十分钟，其位置没有变化。对该地区其他农场的进一步调查结果均为负面，且未收到其他相关报告。

**Witnesses:** An unnamed person who reported the event to the YUL ACC Shift Manager.

**Sighting:** On April 20, between 1745Z and 1755Z, a report was received regarding an event sighted in the sky over Baie-Comeau.

**Object:** The YUL ACC suspects the object was a Space-X satellite.

**Aftermath:** The report was passed to CADS for awareness, and the YUL ACC indicated they would report the incident via official channels on their end.

**见证者：** 一名向 YUL ACC 值班经理报告此事件的匿名人士。

**目击：** 4 月 20 日 1745Z 至 1755Z 之间，收到一份关于 Baie-Comeau 上空出现不明飞行事件的报告。

**Sighting:** On July 19, 1952, at 10:45 PM, the observer witnessed an object while located behind the R. Council and in front of their home.

**Object:** The object was described as a ball of yellow light, appearing slightly larger than a bright star.

**Aftermath:** The observer noted they had not seen any "flying objects" before this incident.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_20_-_Pages_57.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** An unnamed witness says they are a last-year grade twelve student and eighteen years old. They mention that they never told anyone about their latest sightings because people around there would ridicule the idea.

**Sighting:** The witness describes one sighting lasting about ten minutes. The sky was overcast, and the time was 12:12 a.m. Another sighting occurred about four weeks earlier at 11:16 p.m., also under overcast skies. In that earlier case, the object was first seen in the southwest about one inch and a half above the horizon from the witness’s perspective.

**Object:** The object is described as a steady solid light. It moved steadily across the sky, then down and up above a radar station about six miles away. When it ended its run north and south, or when it turned or stopped, the light changed from white to red; when it moved, the light was white. The earlier sighting was said to be about the size of Jupiter.

**Aftermath:** No official investigation or identification appears on this page. The witness simply records the observations and notes social pressure not to discuss them.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_20_-_Pages_57.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 一名未署名的目击者自述自己是十八岁、即将升入十二年级的学生，并说自己从未向任何人谈起最近的目击，因为当地人会嘲笑这种说法。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Lawrence Allan Larocque, Ernest M. Fabien, Margaret Rose Mandeville, Mathew Tommy Unka, Gene Murie Norn (also referred to as Jean Murray Norn), Alice Hodges, Yvonne (Mrs. John) Boston, Francis (Mrs. George) Filiatrault, and Molly (Mrs. Merton) Mohr.

**Date / Time:** July 16, 1968, between midnight and 1:00 AM.

**Location:** Fort Resolution and Fort Smith, Northwest Territories, Canada.

**Sighting:** On the night of July 16, 1968, multiple witnesses in Fort Resolution and Fort Smith reported a high-speed aerial object. Gene Murie Norn, a forestry employee, first reported the object to nurse Alice Hodges after observing it while walking home in Fort Resolution between midnight and 12:30 AM. Norn described the object traveling northeast at high speed. Shortly thereafter, between 12:30 AM and 1:00 AM, other residents—Margaret Rose Mandeville, Ernest Michael Fabien, Lawrence Allan Larocque, and Mathew Tommy Unka—observed the same or a similar phenomenon. While some witnesses reported total silence, Mandeville and the group including Fabien, Larocque, and Unka reported hearing two distinct "shots" or backfire-like sounds as the object moved into the clouds. Simultaneously, in Fort Smith, Yvonne Boston, Francis Filiatrault, and Molly Mohr observed a luminous object moving south to north in a rising arc for 4–5 seconds.

**Object:** Descriptions varied but consistently highlighted a high-speed, luminous aerial phenomenon. The object was described as "jelly bean" shaped, long and pointed, oval, or round. It was intensely bright—brighter than stars—with a bluish-white, luminous appearance. Witnesses noted a "dark" front end and a rear that emitted multi-colored sparks (red, green, purple, white) and smoke/vapour trails extending 1/4 to 1/2 mile behind it. The object lacked wings, tail fins, or visible propulsion, and was described as "breathing" or flaring. It moved at speeds exceeding that of a jet, at altitudes estimated between 7,000 and 10,000 feet. Duration of the sightings ranged from 5 seconds to one minute.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP (Cst. J.W. Quinn, Resolution Detachment) conducted interviews and concluded that all witnesses were reliable, sober, and not prone to fabrication. Several witnesses provided hand-drawn sketches of the object. Official weather data for the time indicated a ceiling of 1,200 feet with scattered cumulus and alto-stratus clouds. The Department of Transport (D.O.T.) Aeradio confirmed that a Pacific Western Airlines Convair (Flight 182) had passed over at 9:10 PM, hours before the sighting, ruling it out as a cause. The RCMP noted the witnesses' expertise in aircraft spotting and their observation that the object’s lack of noise was inconsistent with conventional aircraft at that altitude. The case was filed under the National Research Council of Canada (RG 77, Vol. 306).
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 劳伦斯·艾伦·拉罗克 (Lawrence Allan Larocque)、欧内斯特·M·法比安 (Ernest M. Fabien)、玛格丽特·罗斯·曼德维尔 (Margaret Rose Mandeville)、马修·汤米·昂卡 (Mathew Tommy Unka)、吉恩·穆里·诺恩 (Gene Murie Norn，亦称 Jean Murray Norn)、爱丽丝·霍奇斯 (Alice Hodges)、伊冯·波士顿 (Yvonne Boston，约翰·波士顿夫人)、弗朗西斯·菲利亚特罗 (Francis Filiatrault，乔治·菲利亚特罗夫人) 以及莫莉·莫尔 (Molly Mohr，默顿·莫尔夫人)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月16日，午夜至凌晨1:00之间。

**地点：** 加拿大西北地区，雷索卢申堡 (Fort Resolution) 和史密斯堡 (Fort Smith)。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月16日晚，雷索卢申堡和史密斯堡的多名目击者报告称看到一个高速飞行的空中物体。林业局员工吉恩·穆里·诺恩在午夜至凌晨12:30之间步行回家时首次观察到该物体，并向护士爱丽丝·霍奇斯进行了报告。诺恩描述该物体正以极高速度向东北方向飞行。此后不久，即凌晨12:30至1:00之间，其他居民——玛格丽特·罗斯·曼德维尔、欧内斯特·迈克尔·法比安、劳伦斯·艾伦·拉罗克和马修·汤米·昂卡——也观察到了相同或类似的现象。虽然一些目击者称现场完全寂静，但曼德维尔以及包括法比安、拉罗克和昂卡在内的小组报告称，当物体进入云层时，听到了两声清晰的“枪响”或类似汽车回火的声音。与此同时，在史密斯堡，伊冯·波士顿、弗朗西斯·菲利亚特罗和莫莉·莫尔观察到一个发光物体以升起的弧线从南向北移动，持续了4至5秒。

**物体描述：** 描述虽有差异，但都一致强调这是一个高速发光的空中现象。该物体被描述为“软糖”状、长而尖、椭圆形或圆形。它极其明亮——比星星更亮——呈现出蓝白色的光芒。目击者注意到其前端呈“暗色”，尾部喷射出多种颜色的火花（红色、绿色、紫色、白色），并拖着长达1/4至1/2英里的烟雾/蒸汽尾迹。该物体没有机翼、尾翼或可见的推进装置，被描述为在“呼吸”或闪烁。它的飞行速度超过了喷气式飞机，估计高度在7,000至10,000英尺之间。目击持续时间从5秒到1分钟不等。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（雷索卢申分局的 J.W. Quinn 警官）进行了访谈，结论是所有目击者均可靠、清醒，且没有编造事实的倾向。几位目击者提供了该物体的手绘草图。当时的官方气象数据显示，云底高度为1,200英尺，有零散的积云和高层云。交通部 (D.O.T.) 航空无线电部门证实，太平洋西部航空公司的一架康维尔飞机（182号航班）曾在目击事件发生前数小时的晚上9:10飞过，排除了其作为成因的可能性。加拿大皇家骑警指出，目击者具备识别飞机的专业知识，他们观察到该物体缺乏噪音，这与该高度下的常规飞机不符。此案被归档在加拿大国家研究委员会（RG 77, Vol. 306）名下。

*   **Size:** Not explicitly quantified, but described as a "large star."
*   **Color:** The smaller detached object was described as a "ball of fire."
*   **Sound:** No sound was reported.
*   **Movement:** The main object moved in an up-and-down fashion with an oscillating side-to-side motion.
*   **Duration:** The duration was not explicitly stated, though the event involved a sequence of detachment, combustion, and disappearance.
*   **Additional Details:** A smaller object fell from the main object; the fireball trailed black smoke.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented and processed through military and governmental channels. The report was transmitted by the 41st NORAD Division Headquarters located in North Bay. The information was subsequently forwarded to CANFORCEHED (Canadian Forces Headquarters) and the National Research Council for Radio and Electrical Engineering Division for further review and analysis.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 克里斯蒂安·里弗林小姐 (Miss Christien Riverin)、库隆夫人 (Mrs. Coulomb)、伯特伦·杜福尔先生 (Mr. Bertram Dufor) 及伯特伦·杜福尔夫人 (Mrs. Bertram Dufor)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月17日，17:35Z（注：第80页存在印刷错误，误写为1958年；正确日期应为1968年）。

**地点：** 魁北克省阿尔维达（具体为圣马修教区附近）。

**目击经过：** 1968年8月17日17:35Z，四名目击者——克里斯蒂安·里弗林小姐、库隆夫人以及伯特伦·杜福尔夫妇——在阿尔维达同时报告了两次目击事件。当时的各种大气条件被描述为阴天，伴有烟雾和霾。目击者观察到圣马修教区上空出现了一个类似于大星星的物体。该主体呈现出独特的飞行模式，呈上下起伏运动，并伴有左右摇摆。在观察过程中，目击者看到一个较小的物体从主体上分离或坠落。这个小物体随后爆裂成一个火球，随即消失在视野中。库隆夫人提供了具体细节，称形成的火球在下降并消失时拖着黑烟。

**物体描述：**
*   **形状：** 主体类似于一颗大星星。
*   **大小：** 未明确量化，但被描述为“一颗大星星”。
*   **颜色：** 分离出来的小物体被描述为“火球”。
*   **声音：** 未报告有任何声音。
*   **运动：** 主体呈上下起伏运动，并伴有左右摇摆。
*   **持续时间：** 未明确说明，但事件包含了分离、燃烧和消失的过程。
*   **其他细节：** 一个较小的物体从主体上坠落；火球拖着黑烟。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已通过军事和政府渠道正式记录并处理。报告由位于北湾的北美防空司令部（NORAD）第41师总部发送。随后，相关信息被转发至加拿大武装部队总部（CANFORCEHED）以及国家研究委员会无线电与电气工程部，以进行进一步的审查和分析。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** R. Grandy Irwin, Mrs. Irwin, and one unnamed observer.

**Date / Time:** August 12, 1968 (9:45 P.M. / 12/00.45Z) and August 15, 1968 (nightfall).

**Location:** The veranda/steps of a residence at the corner of Water Street and St. Patricks Lane, Shelburne, N.S.

**Sighting:** 
The documentation details two distinct sighting events. The first occurred on August 12 at 9:45 P.M. (12/00.45Z). R. Grandy Irwin, observing from his home on Water Street, noted a light appearing between the "Evening Star" and a lesser star, positioned at an azimuth of 080 degrees and 35–40 degrees above the horizon. The object moved at an "enormous speed" in a south-westerly direction, executing six instantaneous, sharp 45-degree turns to the left and right without losing velocity. The sighting lasted approximately ten seconds before the object vanished to the southwest, either by traveling out of sight or being extinguished. Mr. Irwin attempted to alert his wife, but she was occupied watching television and did not witness this event.

The second event occurred on August 15, 1968, at nightfall. Mr. and Mrs. Irwin, along with an unnamed observer, watched the sky from their home. They observed the Evening Star in the West (approx. 40 degrees above the horizon) and a lesser star. A bright, slightly orange light appeared between them. The object moved steadily in a south-westerly direction at a speed comparable to a slow-moving plane. After approximately ten minutes, the object became motionless. It remained stationary in that position for two hours before observations were discontinued. Mr. Irwin noted that the object appeared to be at least twenty miles away, in the direction of Harper’s Lake.

**Object:** 
The object was described as a star-like, bright light with a slight orange hue. It possessed an intensity comparable to the Evening Star. During the August 12 sighting, it displayed high-speed, erratic, angular movement. During the August 15 sighting, it exhibited steady, slow-moving flight followed by a prolonged stationary period. There was no sound, no vapor trail, and no residue reported. Observations were conducted with the naked eye and 7x35 binoculars.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
Mr. Irwin contacted the duty officer at the Air Force Station in Baccaro to report the sightings. He suggested that authorities conduct a daylight observation of the Harper’s Lake area, speculating that the object might be seeking sanctuary in that uninhabited vicinity during the day. An unnamed observer submitted a detailed written report to the unit via mail, requesting instructions for further forwarding. Official records note that the sky was clear during both nights of observation.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** R. 格兰迪·欧文 (R. Grandy Irwin)、欧文夫人 (Mrs. Irwin) 以及一名未具名的观察者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年8月12日（晚上9:45 / 12日00:45Z）及1968年8月15日（夜幕降临时）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省谢尔本 (Shelburne, N.S.)，沃特街 (Water Street) 与圣帕特里克巷 (St. Patricks Lane) 交汇处的一处住宅阳台/台阶。

**目击经过：**
相关记录详细描述了两次独立的目击事件。第一次发生在8月12日晚上9:45（12日00:45Z）。R. 格兰迪·欧文在沃特街的家中观察时，注意到在“长庚星”（Evening Star）与一颗较小的恒星之间出现了一道光，其方位角为080度，位于地平线上方35至40度处。该物体以“极高的速度”向西南方向移动，在不减速的情况下完成了六次瞬间的、锐利的45度左右转向。目击过程持续了约十秒，随后物体向西南方向消失，可能是飞出了视野，也可能是熄灭了。欧文先生曾试图提醒妻子，但她当时正在看电视，未能目击到这一事件。

第二次事件发生在1968年8月15日夜幕降临时。欧文夫妇与一名未具名的观察者在自家住宅观察天空。他们观察到西边（地平线上方约40度）的长庚星及一颗较小的恒星。一道明亮、略带橙色的光出现在它们之间。该物体以类似于慢速飞机的速度平稳地向西南方向移动。约十分钟后，物体停止了移动。它在那个位置保持静止长达两个小时，随后观察结束。欧文先生指出，该物体似乎位于至少二十英里外，即哈珀湖 (Harper’s Lake) 的方向。

**物体描述：**
该物体被描述为一颗类似恒星的明亮光点，带有轻微的橙色色调。其亮度与长庚星相当。在8月12日的目击中，它表现出高速、无规律的角运动。在8月15日的目击中，它表现出平稳、缓慢的飞行，随后进入了长时间的静止状态。据报告，该物体没有声音，没有尾迹，也没有留下任何残留物。观察是通过肉眼和7x35双筒望远镜进行的。

**调查/后续：**
欧文先生联系了巴卡罗 (Baccaro) 空军基地的值班军官报告了这些目击事件。他建议当局对哈珀湖地区进行日间观察，推测该物体可能在白天躲藏在该无人居住的区域。一名未具名的观察者通过邮件向该单位提交了一份详细的书面报告，并询问后续转交的指示。官方记录显示，两次观察期间天空均晴朗无云。

**Witnesses:** Unnamed persons at various residences.

**Sighting:** Witnesses reported an object in the western sky, slightly to the north. The object was described as falling from sight.

**Object:** John Findlay, Assistant Chief Technician of the Calgary Planetarium, identified the object as the star Venus. He noted that Venus has a magnitude of minus 3.8 and moves at approximately 15 degrees per hour. Atmospheric conditions can cause the star to appear to change color and move slightly.

**Aftermath:** The investigating officer, Cst. R.M. Lequesne of the Calgary Detachment, concluded that the object was Venus. All witnesses were contacted, and they agreed that the object they observed was the star Venus and not a U.F.O.

**物体：** 卡尔加里天文馆助理总技师约翰·芬德利（John Findlay）将该物体鉴定为金星。他指出金星的星等为负3.8，移动速度约为每小时15度。大气条件可能导致该星体出现颜色变化和轻微移动。

**后续：** 卡尔加里分局的警官R.M. 勒奎斯（R.M. Lequesne）得出结论，该物体即为金星。所有目击者均已联系，他们一致认为所观察到的物体是金星，而非不明飞行物。

**Witnesses:** A civilian resident of 11111 Braxton Road S.W., Calgary, and others.

**Sighting:** On March 11, 1972, at approximately 10:10 PM, witnesses observed a flying object in the sky to the west of their residence. The object remained visible until approximately 10:45 PM.

The movement was slow and wandering, except at the time of departure, which was very rapid. The object proceeded northwest and fell below the horizon. **Aftermath:** The witness contacted the McCall Field Control Tower, which reported that radar within a 30-mile range showed nothing. Contact with commercial air traffic also yielded negative results, and no aircraft were reported in the area. Checks with the Calgary Armed Forces Base confirmed no military exercises were being conducted in the area at the time. The RCMP interviewed all persons mentioned in the report and deemed them extremely reliable.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 作者本人、其岳父以及一位邻居。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two civilian drivers, both alone in their vehicles.

**Sighting:** On January 14, 1977, two separate sightings occurred. The first was at 7:30 PM (PST) near Stewart Crossing, and the second was at 8:40 PM (PST) near Elsa, Yukon. Both observers reported seeing the same object while driving in clear, dark, and hazy conditions.

**Object:** The object was described as round or oblong, projecting a bright clear white light and flames of the same color and sparks. One observer noted the object grew larger and smaller, and appeared to be at an altitude of approximately 4000 feet, moving in valleys about 10 miles away. The object moved very fast, up, down, across, and straight. One observer noted the object made an "M" shape when first noticed. Both observers stopped their vehicles and reported no noise whatsoever. The object disappeared at 9:55 PM (PST).

**Aftermath:** The Mayo Detachment requested an analysis from the National Research Council. The report notes that the Ministry of Transport reported no air traffic in the vicinity at the time. The temperature was -20°C with a wind from the NE at 14 knots.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:

**物体：** 该物体被描述为圆形或长方形，投射出明亮的纯白光芒，并伴有同色的火焰和火花。一名观察者指出该物体时大时小，高度约为4000英尺，在约10英里外的山谷中移动。物体移动速度极快，轨迹包括上下、横向及直线运动。一名观察者提到物体在最初被发现时呈现“M”形。两名观察者均停车观察，并报告称没有任何声音。该物体于晚上9:55消失。

**后续：** 梅奥（Mayo）分遣队请求加拿大国家研究委员会进行分析。报告指出，交通部报告称当时该地区没有空中交通。当时气温为零下20摄氏度，东北风14节。

**Witnesses:** Two tractor trailer operators and other subjects in Whitehorse.

**Sighting:** At approximately 4:20 AM Y.C. on November 16, 1975, two tractor trailer operators were driving south on the Whitehorse-Carmacks Highway. At Mile 21 near Fox Lake, they observed an object much larger than their truck descend like a helicopter over the rear of the trailer. The object then proceeded in the same direction as the vehicle at a slightly greater speed than the truck, which was traveling at 55 mph.

**Object:** The object moved at a "fantastic speed" and moved north over some hills in an arc. It was described as very bright, hurting the eyes, with a very white center and bluish edges. The entire area for about a mile in all directions was lit up like daytime. The witnesses observed the object for a total of no more than 35 seconds. Several other subjects in the Whitehorse area also saw a brightness in the sky for a few seconds but did not actually see the object.

**Aftermath:** The report was transmitted via telecommunications to the National Research Council Meteor Centre in Ottawa by the Whitehorse RCMP detachment.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_29_-_Pages_84.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 两名拖拉机挂车司机，以及怀特霍斯地区的其他目击者。

**目击：** 1975年11月16日凌晨4:20左右（育空时间），两名拖拉机挂车司机正沿怀特霍斯-卡马克斯公路向南行驶。在福克斯湖（Fox Lake）21英里处，他们观察到一个比卡车大得多的物体像直升机一样降落在拖车后方。随后，该物体以略高于卡车（时速55英里）的速度向同一方向移动。

**物体：** 该物体以“惊人的速度”移动，并呈弧形向北越过一些山丘。据描述，该物体非常明亮，刺眼，中心呈白色，边缘呈蓝色。周围约一英里范围内的所有方向都被照亮得如同白昼。目击者观察该物体的时间总计不超过35秒。怀特霍斯地区的其他几个人也看到天空中出现了亮光，持续了几秒钟，但并未实际看到该物体。

**后续：** 该报告由怀特霍斯皇家骑警（RCMP）分局通过电信发送至渥太华的国家研究委员会流星中心。

The object hovered for a minute, departed at extremely high speed eastward towards Highway 17, then returned for another minute before leaving again in the same direction.

**Aftermath:** The total duration of the sighting was approximately two minutes. Mr. Bett phoned the information to the OPP while driving home from work, and the OPP relayed the report to CFS Falconbridge.

**Sighting:** On April 5, 1981, at approximately 8:15 PM, a UFO was observed near Rimbey, Alberta. The witness, Bill Muncaster, reported the object was hovering 200 feet above trees, about a quarter-mile from his residence. The object moved slowly in a northerly direction for about 20 minutes before disappearing.

A white beam of light was observed emanating from the middle of the object, hitting the ground like a spotlight. Other witnesses generally reported seeing two flashing red lights, though they could not confirm the shape due to darkness.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP investigated the report and contacted the Number 43 Radar Squadron in Red Deer on April 7, 1981, to inquire if the object could have been a weather balloon, but the squadron could not provide any information.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary_zh:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Tom Moberg and Eric Poulsen of Rimbey, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On April 14, 1981, Moberg reported seeing two flashing red lights. He contacted the Penhold tracking station, who identified the lights as two aircraft flying in formation.

**Object:** The objects were identified as two aircraft flying in formation. The pilots were experiencing strong head winds, reducing their ground speed to almost nil. The side lights were extinguished, leaving only the flashing red tail lights visible. The movement and tipping of the objects were attributed to the pilots attempting to find a less resistant slip-stream.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP contacted Bill Wright for assistance. Transport Canada later confirmed to the Rimbey Detachment that two helicopters were in the area at the time of the sighting. The report was copied to the Planetary Sciences Section of the National Research Council.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_18_-_Pages_51.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 位于阿尔伯塔省林比的 Tom Moberg 和 Eric Poulsen。

**目击：** 1981年4月14日，Moberg 报告看到两盏闪烁的红灯。他联系了 Penhold 跟踪站，对方确认这些灯光是两架编队飞行的飞机。

**物体：** 这些物体被确认为两架编队飞行的飞机。由于飞行员遭遇强劲的逆风，其地速几乎降至零。飞机的侧灯熄灭，仅留闪烁的红色尾灯可见。物体移动和倾斜的现象被归因于飞行员试图寻找阻力较小的气流。

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）联系了 Bill Wright 寻求协助。加拿大交通部随后向林比分遣队确认，在目击事件发生时，该地区确实有两架直升机。该报告被抄送至加拿大国家研究委员会行星科学部门。

**Witnesses:** Lynne Wanamaker, Lorraine Parkhouse, and Maureen Connor.

**Date / Time:** September 25, 1968, at 9:15 PM PDT.

**Location:** The intersection of Moscrop and Barker Streets, Burnaby, BC.

**Sighting:** On the evening of September 25, 1968, at approximately 9:15 PM PDT, three witnesses—Lynne Wanamaker, Lorraine Parkhouse, and Maureen Connor—were positioned at the intersection of Moscrop and Barker Streets in Burnaby, BC. The witnesses observed two bright orange lights situated in the northwest sky. The weather conditions at the time of the sighting were reported as clear. 

The observation lasted for a total duration of 10 minutes. During this time, the lights exhibited a distinct swaying motion. One of the two lights remained stationary, while the second light performed an anti-clockwise rotation, eventually coming to a stop directly below the top light. The witnesses noted that the lights eventually faded away, moving in a westerly direction. No sounds were reported in connection with the objects throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Object:** The objects were described as two bright orange lights, visually comparable to street lights. In terms of size and positioning, they appeared to be 1 1/2 inches in diameter (as perceived by the witnesses) and were spaced approximately 1.5 diameters (or 4 inches) apart. The movement was characterized by a swaying motion, with one light remaining stationary while the other executed an anti-clockwise rotation before settling into a position beneath the stationary light. No auditory phenomena were associated with the objects.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the event, the witnesses contacted the Department of Transport (DOT) at the Vancouver International Airport. The DOT officials advised the witnesses to report the incident to the local police. Consequently, the Burnaby RCMP detachment was contacted and subsequently reached out to the airport control tower to verify if other reports had been filed. The airport tower confirmed that no other UFO reports had been received regarding the event.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 琳恩·瓦纳梅克 (Lynne Wanamaker)、洛林·帕克豪斯 (Lorraine Parkhouse) 和莫琳·康纳 (Maureen Connor)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年9月25日，太平洋夏令时间 (PDT) 晚上9:15。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省本拿比市，莫斯克罗普街 (Moscrop Street) 与巴克街 (Barker Street) 的交叉路口。

**目击经过：** 1968年9月25日晚，约太平洋夏令时间晚上9:15，三名目击者——琳恩·瓦纳梅克、洛林·帕克豪斯和莫琳·康纳——位于不列颠哥伦比亚省本拿比市的莫斯克罗普街与巴克街交叉路口。目击者观察到西北方天空中出现了两道明亮的橙色光芒。据报告，当时天气状况晴朗。

观测过程持续了10分钟。在此期间，这些光点呈现出明显的摇摆运动。其中一个光点保持静止，而另一个光点则进行了逆时针旋转，最终停在上方光点的正下方。目击者注意到，这些光点最终向西移动并逐渐消失。在整个目击过程中，未听到与这些物体相关的任何声音。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为两道明亮的橙色光芒，视觉上类似于路灯。就大小和位置而言，它们看起来直径约为1.5英寸（目击者的感知），彼此间隔约1.5个直径（或4英寸）的距离。其运动特征为摇摆式移动，其中一个光点保持静止，另一个则执行逆时针旋转，随后停留在静止光点的下方。这些物体未伴随任何听觉现象。

**调查/后续：** 事件发生后，目击者联系了温哥华国际机场的交通部 (DOT)。交通部官员建议目击者向当地警方报告此事。随后，目击者联系了本拿比皇家骑警 (RCMP) 分局，警方随即与机场控制塔取得联系，以核实是否还有其他相关报告。机场控制塔确认，未收到任何关于此次事件的其他不明飞行物报告。

**Witnesses:** George Lumb

**Date / Time:** November 14, 1968, at 8:00 PM

**Location:** A farm residence approximately 6 miles north of Rocky Mountain House, Alberta

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 14, 1968, at approximately 8:00 PM, George Lumb was on foot, crossing a road to visit a neighbor’s residence. During this time, he observed an unidentified object in the sky. The weather conditions were noted as clear and dark. Mr. Lumb observed the object traveling from the southwest toward the northeast. He noted that the object’s flight path followed the same course regularly taken by jet aircraft in that area. However, he emphasized that the object was moving at an extremely high rate of speed—significantly faster than any jet he had previously observed—and notably lacked the engine noise typically produced by jets flying over the region. The total duration of the sighting was approximately 2 to 3 minutes.

**Object:** The object was observed at a high altitude, which prevented the witness from distinguishing its specific physical shape. However, Mr. Lumb described its visual appearance as resembling "two light bulbs together." The lighting configuration consisted of a green light at the front and a red light at the back. The object moved at an extremely high rate of speed and was completely silent throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation consists of multiple reports detailing the account of George Lumb regarding the sighting near Rocky Mountain House. The reports confirm the witness's location (a farm 6 miles north of the town), the specific time (8:00 PM), and the environmental conditions (clear and dark). The investigation notes highlight the witness's comparison of the object's trajectory to known jet flight paths, specifically emphasizing the discrepancy between the object's high velocity and lack of noise compared to conventional aircraft. No further official follow-up or meteorological data beyond the witness's observation of "clear and dark" conditions was recorded in these pages.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:

**Witnesses:** Donald Lynn, his wife, and their four children (aged 8–15 years).

**Date / Time:** November 12, 1968 (primary report); conflicting/erroneous dates noted in file include November 6, 1968, and November 13, 1958. Time recorded as 6:00 PM – 6:30 PM MST.

**Location:** Near Barons, Alberta (Lethbridge area).

**Sighting:** The Lynn family, consisting of Donald Lynn, his wife, and their four children, observed an unidentified object in the sky while near Barons, Alberta. The sighting occurred between 6:00 PM and 6:30 PM MST. The witnesses reported that the object appeared to be "quite low" in the sky. It was first sighted in the southwest, moved gradually toward the west, then shifted back to the southwest before finally disappearing over the horizon. While the primary case file identifies the date as November 12, 1968, other documents within the same file inconsistently record the event as occurring on November 6, 1968, or November 13, 1958.

**Object:** The object was described as oval-shaped. It exhibited a distinct color-changing property, transitioning between bright red and yellow-orange. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented as report L2007, with internal references to correspondence CIB2986/5. The report was forwarded to the NRC Meteor Centre in Ottawa for analysis. The Lethbridge Weather Office provided an official assessment of the sighting, concluding that the object was, in all probability, the planet Venus. The weather office noted that on the date in question, Venus rose at an angle of 15 degrees from the southwest at 4:52 PM MST and set at 6:52 PM MST, which aligns with the duration and trajectory reported by the witnesses.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_02_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 唐纳德·林恩（Donald Lynn）、他的妻子以及他们的四个孩子（年龄在8至15岁之间）。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省巴伦斯（Barons）附近（莱斯布里奇地区）。

此次目击事件由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 卡莱尔 (Carlyle) 分队正式记录并上报。调查及随后的报告归档工作均严格遵守了加拿大皇家骑警《行动手册》中的 CO-AIR 协议。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian resident of Edmonton, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On February 1, 1969, at approximately 8:00 A.M., a witness traveling west on Highway 43, one mile east of Sangudo, Alberta, observed strange objects in the sky. The first object was described as small, oblong, bright white, and moving north at a rapid speed at high altitude; it was visible for 10 seconds. Three minutes later, the witness observed a second, much larger object. This object was estimated to be 1,000 feet away, featuring a flat base, an oval top, and a bright white glow. It was also visible for 10 seconds before disappearing to the north. The sky was covered with heavy clouds at the time.

**Object:** Two objects: one small, oblong, and bright white; the second larger, with a flat base and oval top, glowing bright white.

**Aftermath:** The Mayerthorpe RCMP detachment drafted a message to the Edmonton Sub-Division. Patrols were conducted in the Sangudo area, but no other witnesses were found. The witness's reliability is unknown, though he claimed to have seen a similar object four years prior in British Columbia. The file was concluded on February 4, 1969, with no further action taken.

**物体：** 两个物体：第一个体积小、长方形且呈亮白色；第二个体积较大，底部平坦，顶部呈椭圆形，发出亮白色的光。

**后续：** 梅耶索普皇家骑警分队向埃德蒙顿分区发送了报告。警方在桑古多地区进行了巡逻，但未发现其他目击者。该目击者的可靠性未知，尽管他声称四年前在不列颠哥伦比亚省见过类似的物体。该档案于1969年2月4日结案，未采取进一步行动。

**Witnesses:** A woman, her brother, and several other people in the Spruce Lake area.

**Sighting:** On December 30, 1968, at 8:30 PM Atlantic Standard Time, witnesses observed an unidentified flying object in the Spruce Lake area for approximately 30 minutes. It appeared to be at varying altitudes, sometimes very high and at other times as close as a few hundred yards away.

**Object:** The object was described as being similar to a half-moon, flat on the bottom and round on the top, roughly the size of a helicopter. It featured a white light that would change in brightness, and also displayed red and green lights.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP questioned the witnesses and concluded they were sober and reliable. No further action was taken by the detachment.

**物体：** 该物体被描述为类似于半月形，底部平坦，顶部呈圆形，大小约为直升机大小。它有一个亮度会变化的白光，并显示出红色和绿色的灯光。

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）对目击者进行了询问，认为他们当时清醒且可靠。该分局未采取进一步行动。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. [name redacted], a licenced astronomer from Deer Lake, Nfld.

**Sighting:** The page describes reports of objects in the sky that some people felt were jumping or vibrating. An astronomer was consulted regarding these sightings.

**Object:** The astronomer identified the object as the planet Venus. She explained that the perceived jumping or vibrating motion is an optical illusion caused by high atmospheric pressure and heavy atmospheric conditions such as haze, clouds, and smoke.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP concluded that the sightings reported in this regard should be classified as meteors, fireballs, or Unidentified Flying Objects, specifically noting that the incident on 30 DEC 68 was the planet Venus. The report was submitted for information purposes by Cst. D.J. Morrison of the Corner Brook City Detachment.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:

**目击：** 该页面描述了有关天空中物体跳动或振动的报告。为此咨询了一位天文学家。

**物体：** 该天文学家确认该物体为金星。她解释说，观察到的跳动或振动现象是由高气压以及雾霾、云层和烟雾等恶劣大气条件引起的视觉错觉。

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）得出结论，认为相关报告应归类为流星、火球或不明飞行物，并特别指出 1968 年 12 月 30 日的事件即为金星。该报告由科纳布鲁克市分局的 D.J. Morrison 警员提交，仅供参考。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Paul Lucier, a DPW fireman, and Fred Koch, a businessman.

**Sighting:** On November 24, 1968, at 5:00 PM, the witnesses observed an object from the corner of 6th and Ray in Whitehorse, Yukon. The object was approximately one mile away.

**Object:** The object was described as elliptical and white, appearing very bright, similar to an aircraft landing light rather than a gaseous or burning light. It was mostly stationary, though it exhibited slight sideways movement while traveling in a north-south direction. The sighting lasted approximately 5 to 6 minutes. No sound was reported.

**Aftermath:** During the observation, 3 to 4 pieces fell from the object. The light became brighter, then dimmer, then bright again for about 5 to 6 times before finally fading. Local Department of Transport (DOT) reports indicated that no aircraft were in the area at that time.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** DPW消防员Paul Lucier和商人Fred Koch。

**目击：** 1968年11月24日下午5点，目击者在育空地区怀特霍斯（Whitehorse）的第6街和雷街（Ray）拐角处观察到一个物体，距离约1英里。

**物体：** 该物体呈椭圆形，白色，非常明亮，看起来更像飞机着陆灯，而不是燃烧或气体发出的光。物体基本保持静止，但在南北方向上有轻微的侧向移动。目击持续了约5到6分钟。未听到任何声音。

**后续：** 观察期间，有3到4块碎片从物体上掉落。光线在变亮、变暗、再变亮之间循环了约5到6次，最后逐渐消失。当地交通部（DOT）报告称，当时该地区没有飞机。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Seven employees of Brodsky Construction, including one named individual and six others.

**Sighting:** On October 15, 1968, at 8:50 PM Central Daylight Saving Time, witnesses observed an object at Pipe Lake, Manitoba, north of the 55th parallel. The weather conditions included 7/10ths cloud cover with a 1200-foot broken ceiling.

**Object:** The object had no discernible shape and was estimated to be at an altitude of 1500 feet, moving very fast. It displayed three lights: red, green, and amber. Initially, red and green lights were blinking side-by-side. The red light then extinguished, while the green light remained on but stopped blinking. An amber light subsequently appeared below and behind the green light. The lights were described as being the size of traffic control lights and very bright. The observation lasted for 3 or 4 minutes.

**Aftermath:** The report was filed by the Thompson Rural Detachment of the RCMP.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 七名 Brodsky Construction 的员工，包括一名被提及姓名的人员及其他六人。

**目击：** 1968年10月15日中部夏令时间晚上8点50分，目击者在曼尼托巴省北纬55度以北的派普湖（Pipe Lake）观察到一个物体。当时天气状况为7/10云层覆盖，云底高度为1200英尺。

**物体：** 该物体没有明确形状，估计高度为1500英尺，移动速度非常快。它显示出红、绿、琥珀色三种灯光。起初，红色和绿色灯光并排闪烁。随后红灯熄灭，绿灯保持常亮但停止闪烁。接着在绿灯下方和后方出现了一盏琥珀色灯光。灯光被描述为交通信号灯大小且非常明亮。观察持续了3到4分钟。

**后续：** 该报告由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）汤普森农村分遣队提交。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Goulet, a Protonotary of the Amos County Court.

**Sighting:** On July 27, 1968, between 10:00 P.M. and 10:30 P.M. D.S.T., the witness observed an object while standing outside his house at 72 - 10th Ave. East, Amos, Quebec. The sky was very clear with visible stars. The sighting lasted between 3 to 5 minutes.

**Object:** The object was round, approximately the size of a grapefruit, and emitted a white light comparable in brightness to the morning star (Venus). It moved in a straight line from due south to due north at a very fast speed. It left no persistent train or tail and made no sound.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP report notes that the observer is considered a reliable person with a good knowledge of astronomy. The file was submitted for information and concluded.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:

**目击：** 1968 年 7 月 27 日，夏令时间晚上 10:00 至 10:30 之间，目击者在位于魁北克省 Amos 市 10th Ave. East 72 号的住所外观察到了一个物体。当时天空非常晴朗，可以看到星星。目击持续了 3 到 5 分钟。

**物体：** 该物体呈圆形，大小约为葡萄柚，发出与晨星（金星）亮度相当的白光。它以极快的速度沿直线从正南向正北移动。它没有留下持续的尾迹，也没有发出任何声音。

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）报告指出，目击者被认为是一个可靠的人，并且具备良好的天文学知识。该文件已提交以供参考，并已结案。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Constable S.B. Barrie and his wife, Mrs. Vivian Barrie.

**Sighting:** On October 3, 1969, at approximately 8:45 PM CST, the witnesses were traveling near Highway 44 in the Whiteshell area of Manitoba. They observed a light that initially appeared to be a reflection on the windshield, but upon stopping, they identified it as an object hovering over the bush.

**Object:** The object was described as an inverted saucer, approximately 20 feet in diameter, light pink in color, and intensely bright. It exhibited short, jerky movements and displayed a white tail that snaked downwards toward the earth. The object eventually disappeared noiselessly at a high rate of speed toward the southwest.

**Aftermath:** When the vehicle was approximately 500 feet from the object, the electrical windshield wipers stopped working, the headlights went out, and the 1968 Falcon car stalled. After the object disappeared, the car's systems functioned again. The area was left with a heaviness and a strange odor. The incident was reported to Cpl. D.E. Shaw on October 29, 1969, at the Pine Falls Detachment.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_26_-_Pages_75.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 警员 S.B. Barrie 及其妻子 Vivian Barrie 夫人。

**目击：** 1969年10月3日晚约8:45（中部标准时间），目击者在曼尼托巴省怀特谢尔（Whiteshell）地区的44号公路附近行驶。他们观察到一个起初被误认为是挡风玻璃反射的光点，停车后确认该物体悬浮在灌木丛上方。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一个倒置的碟状物，直径约20英尺，呈浅粉色，亮度极高。它呈现出短促、颠簸的移动方式，并带有一条向下延伸至地面的白色尾迹。最终，该物体以极高的速度向西南方向无声消失。

**后续：** 当车辆距离该物体约500英尺时，电动雨刷停止工作，前大灯熄灭，1968年款猎鹰（Falcon）汽车熄火。物体消失后，车辆功能恢复正常。现场留有一种沉重感和奇怪的气味。该事件于1969年10月29日在派恩福尔斯（Pine Falls）分局向 D.E. Shaw 下士报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** H. Curry, his son, and Cst. F.W. Pushka.

**Sighting:** On August 4, 1968, at approximately 4:00 a.m., witnesses observed a large object hovering over a barn near Qu'appelle, Saskatchewan. The object was described as spinning and appeared to be 25-30 feet across. It hovered for about one minute before moving to the southeast for another minute and then departing.

**Object:** The object appeared large with revolving lights on the bottom. It was estimated to be hovering at approximately twice the height of the barn. The witness noted the object moved very quickly between positions, appearing to stop spinning while in transit.

**Aftermath:** Statements were taken by the RCMP on August 9, 1968.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** H. Curry、其子以及 F.W. Pushka 警员。

**目击：** 1968年8月4日凌晨4点左右，目击者在萨斯喀彻温省 Qu'appelle 附近观察到一个悬停在谷仓上方的巨大物体。该物体被描述为正在旋转，直径约为25至30英尺。它悬停了约一分钟，随后向东南方向移动了约一分钟，然后离开。

**物体：** 该物体看起来很大，底部有旋转的灯光。据估计，它悬停的高度约为谷仓高度的两倍。目击者指出，该物体在不同位置之间移动得非常快，在移动过程中似乎停止了旋转。

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）于1968年8月9日记录了相关证词。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A civilian resident of the Qu'appelle District.

**Sighting:** On August 4, 1968, at approximately 4:00 am, a witness observed an illuminated object hovering above their house. The object was described as circular in shape and moved in an oval shape about 100 feet above the house. The witness watched the object for about 10 minutes, then went inside to wake their father. Upon returning outside, the object was observed above the barn, moving away and then returning. The object made no noise and emitted no light rays.

**Object:** A circular, illuminated object that moved in an oval pattern and hovered above a house and barn.

**Aftermath:** The witness reported finding circular marks in the pasture near the barn, ranging from 4.5 to 5 feet in diameter. Six marks were found, three of which were well-pronounced. RCMP officers from the Regina Identification Section examined the marks but could not provide an explanation for them.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Qu'appelle地区的一名平民居民。

**目击：** 1968年8月4日凌晨4点左右，一名目击者观察到一个悬停在房屋上方的发光物体。该物体被描述为圆形，并以椭圆形轨迹在房屋上方约100英尺处移动。目击者观察了该物体约10分钟，随后进屋叫醒了父亲。再次回到室外时，该物体位于谷仓上方，移动离开后又返回。该物体没有发出任何声音，也没有发出光线。

**物体：** 一个圆形的、发光的物体，以椭圆形模式移动并悬停在房屋和谷仓上方。

**后续：** 目击者报告在谷仓附近的牧场发现了圆形痕迹，直径从4.5英尺到5英尺不等。共发现了六个痕迹，其中三个非常明显。来自里贾纳鉴定部门的皇家骑警警官检查了这些痕迹，但无法给出解释。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two unnamed individuals located in a home farmyard one and one-half miles south of Qu'Appelle, Saskatchewan.

**Sighting:** On August 4, 1968, at 4:00 A.M., during a period of cloudy sky, thunder, and lightning, an object was observed for 3-4 minutes. The witnesses observed the object from a distance of approximately 150 yards before taking cover.

**Object:** The object was described as saucer-shaped, greyish-white in color, and 20-30 feet in diameter. It maintained an altitude of 80-100 feet and exhibited circular motion around the farmyard, appearing to dart at right angles from point to point.

**Aftermath:** The Indian Head detachment investigated the site and discovered four circular marks, approximately 5 feet in diameter, in a pasture near the farm buildings. The incident was not reported until the afternoon of the sighting. The reliability of the report is unknown.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 位于萨斯喀彻温省奎阿佩尔以南一英里半处农场的两名未具名人士。

**目击：** 1968年8月4日凌晨4点，在多云、有雷电的天气下，目击者观察到一个物体持续了3至4分钟。目击者在约150码的距离观察该物体后采取了隐蔽措施。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为碟形，呈灰白色，直径为20至30英尺。它保持在80至100英尺的高度，在农场周围做圆周运动，并似乎以直角从一点移动到另一点。

**后续：** 印第安角分遣队进行了调查，并在农场建筑物附近的牧场中发现了四个直径约5英尺的圆形痕迹。该事件直到目击当天下午才被报告。报告的可靠性未知。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Tim Czyz, Elaine Hanna, and two others.

**Sighting:** The event occurred on March 21, 1979, at 210205Z. The sky was clear. The witnesses were located at Fraser and 2nd Avenue in North Bay, looking east.

**Object:** The object was described as red and light blue, and revolving. It was observed at an angle of 45 degrees from ground level. The duration of the sighting was 3 minutes.

**Aftermath:** No further details are provided.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Tim Czyz、Elaine Hanna 以及另外两人。

**目击：** 事件发生于1979年3月21日 210205Z。当时天空晴朗。目击者位于北湾（North Bay）的Fraser街和第二大道路口，向东观测。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为红色和浅蓝色，且在旋转。观测到的仰角为地面以上45度。目击持续时间为3分钟。

**后续：** 未提供更多细节。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Elizabeth McKibbon (nurse), Melita Dyson (nurse's aid), Robert Clark, Sam Holwell, Jesse Turnbull and family, Stephan Macdonald, and Bernard Dyson.

**Sighting:** On 13 November 1978 at approximately 1600 hours, witnesses observed a bright red circular object high in the sky, surrounded by a red glow and emitting a short jet-plane-like trail. The object was stationary for about 30 minutes and viewed with binoculars. A second, larger object appeared, and both moved toward each other on a collision course before changing direction and entering a dark grey cloud formation, which dissipated as they passed through. Earlier that afternoon, between 1300 and 1400 hours, other witnesses observed fireballs hitting the ground near Martins Pond.

**Object:** Bright red circular objects with a red glow and trail; fireballs.

**Aftermath:** Miss McKibbon and school teacher Stephan Macdonald checked the area at Martins Pond, where fireballs had reportedly burned approximately one acre of bog land. No debris was found. Numerous residents observed the events, and some are showing concern regarding the local water supply.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 护士 Elizabeth McKibbon、护士助理 Melita Dyson、Robert Clark、Sam Holwell、Jesse Turnbull 及其家人、Stephan Macdonald 和 Bernard Dyson。

**目击：** 1978年11月13日约1600时，目击者观察到一个高空中的明亮红色圆形物体，周围有红光，并留下一条类似喷气式飞机的短尾迹。该物体静止约半小时，并被用双筒望远镜观察。随后出现了第二个类似的较大物体，两者在移动中似乎处于碰撞航线上，但在接近时改变方向并进入一团深灰色云层，云层在物体穿过后消散。当天下午1300至1400时之间，其他目击者观察到火球击中 Martins Pond 附近的地面。

**物体：** 带有红光和尾迹的明亮红色圆形物体；火球。

**后续：** McKibbon 小姐与教师 Stephan Macdonald 检查了 Martins Pond 地区，据报道火球烧毁了约一英亩的沼泽地。未发现任何碎片。许多居民目击了这些事件，一些居民对当地供水表示担忧。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Michel Janetakes of 4360 Bathurst Street, Toronto.

**Sighting:** On July 8, a sighting occurred at Boyd Park in the Woodbridge, Ontario area.

**Object:** The object was described as shiny, oval in shape, and silent. It was observed at a high altitude flying in an easterly direction, leaving a short trail.

**Aftermath:** A picture of the third sighting was taken and will be forwarded by the Trenton Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) as soon as possible.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 多伦多Bathurst街4360号的Michel Janetakes先生。

**目击：** 7月8日，在安大略省Woodbridge地区的Boyd公园发生了一起目击事件。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为闪亮、椭圆形且无声。它被观察到在高空向东飞行，并留下一条短尾迹。

**后续：** 第三次目击事件的照片已被拍摄，并将由特伦顿救援协调中心（RCC）尽快转发。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Senecal and her children.

**Sighting:** The page reports a sighting occurring on September 4, 1979. The object was observed in Montreal by Mrs. Senecal's children using a telescope.

**Object:** The object consisted of three lights, described as red, white, and green. The lights were positioned in the east, west, and south. The duration of the sighting was 4 hours and 38 minutes. The object was reported at an altitude of 50,000 feet and showed no movement.

**Aftermath:** The report was transmitted via teletype from LAC CFS St Denis to NDOC Ottawa, AIRCOM Winnipeg, and ADGHQ North Bay, with information copies sent to the NRC.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Senecal 女士及其子女。

**目击：** 该页面报告了一起发生在 1979 年 9 月 4 日的目击事件。Senecal 女士的孩子们通过望远镜在蒙特利尔观测到了该物体。

**物体：** 该物体由三盏灯组成，颜色为红色、白色和绿色。灯光分别位于东、西、南方向。目击持续时间为 4 小时 38 分钟。据报告，该物体高度为 50,000 英尺，且没有移动。

**后续：** 该报告通过电传打字机从 LAC CFS St Denis 发送至渥太华 NDOC、温尼伯 AIRCOM 和北湾 ADGHQ，并抄送至加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC)。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Jack Dow of Pouce Coupe, B.C.

**Sighting:** On February 21, an object was observed overhead in Pouce Coupe, B.C., while the sky was 8/10ths cloudy. The object was sighted traveling in a northerly direction in the area of the Big Dipper.

**Object:** The object was described as bright, easily distinguishable, and bright orange in color. It appeared round, roughly the size of a large star, and was observed to be very high and slow-moving. The duration of the sighting was 4 to 5 minutes.

**Aftermath:** The report was filed by Station Beaver Lodge to CANFORCEHQ OPS, with information provided to Dr. J.A. Jacobs at UBC, Vancouver.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省 Pouce Coupe 的 Jack Dow 先生。

**目击：** 2月21日，在不列颠哥伦比亚省 Pouce Coupe 上空观测到一个物体，当时天空有 8/10 的云层。该物体被目击到在北斗七星区域向北移动。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为明亮、清晰可见且呈亮橙色。它呈圆形，大小约为一颗大恒星，观测显示其高度很高且移动缓慢。目击持续时间为 4 到 5 分钟。

**后续：** 该报告由 Beaver Lodge 站提交给 CANFORCEHQ OPS，并抄送给温哥华不列颠哥伦比亚大学的 J.A. Jacobs 博士。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A party of local citizens.

**Sighting:** An unidentified flying object was observed on 27-JAN-68 near Queen Charlotte City, B.C.

**Object:** The object was determined to be a man-made device constructed of a paper tissue body with a lighted candle inside. It was built in the form of a 45-gallon drum and was not anchored to the ground.

**Aftermath:** An investigation by the RCMP revealed that the object was constructed and launched by a local resident of Queen Charlotte City. The individual stated that lighting the candle warmed the air inside the object, causing it to rise. The individual further stated that the object was not launched for the purpose of causing an unnecessary investigation. The file was concluded with no further action required.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 当地居民一行。

**目击：** 1968年1月27日，在不列颠哥伦比亚省夏洛特皇后市附近观察到一个不明飞行物体。

**物体：** 该物体被确定为人造装置，由纸巾制成，内部装有蜡烛。其形状类似于45加仑的油桶，且未固定在地面上。

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的调查显示，该物体由夏洛特皇后市的一名当地居民制造并放飞。该居民表示，点燃蜡烛后，物体内部的空气变暖，从而使其升空。该居民进一步表示，放飞该物体并非为了引起不必要的调查。此案已结案，无需进一步行动。
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_label: Summary (restored from OCR cache for boundary repair)

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Four individuals from Skidegate Mission, B.C.

**Sighting:** On January 27, 1968, at 2:15 P.M., witnesses observed an object while standing in front of the Apollo Bowling Alley in Queen Charlotte City, B.C. The sky was cloudy and overcast with a ceiling of approximately 750 feet.

**Object:** The object appeared over Robertson Island in Skidegate Inlet at an altitude of approximately 400 to 500 feet. It was described as being shaped similar to a helicopter but smaller, noiseless, and dark in color (possibly black). It had no external moving parts but emitted smoke or vapor while hovering. It eventually moved away in a southwesterly direction using a quick zig-zag motion. The observation lasted between three and five minutes.

**Aftermath:** An investigation was conducted by the RCMP, who concluded that the witnesses were of a reliable type and the information provided should be considered reliable.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_25_-_Pages_72.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 四名来自卑诗省Skidegate Mission的居民。

**目击：** 1968年1月27日下午2点15分，目击者在卑诗省夏洛特皇后市的Apollo保龄球馆前观察到了该物体。当时天空多云阴沉，云层高度约为750英尺。

**物体：** 该物体出现在Skidegate Inlet的Robertson岛上空，高度约为400至500英尺。据描述，该物体形状类似于直升机，但体积较小，无声，颜色较深（可能是黑色）。它没有外部运动部件，但在悬停时会散发出烟雾或蒸汽。随后，该物体以快速的之字形运动向西南方向飞离。观察持续了三到五分钟。

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）进行了调查，结论认为受访者属于可靠类型，所提供的信息应被视为可靠。

**Sighting:** The event occurred on July 29, 1966, at 2330Z. The weather was reported as high, thin, scattered cirrus clouds. The object was observed in Richmond.

**Object:** The object was described as metallic gray in color and circular in shape. The duration of the sighting was 30 to 40 seconds.

**Aftermath:** The object flew north, stopped, flew south, and then appeared to go straight up out of sight.

**见证者：** Mr. Davidson 和 Mr. Gallant，两人均为前加拿大皇家空军（RCAF）飞行员。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为金属灰色，形状呈圆形。目击持续时间为30至40秒。

**后续：** 该物体向北飞行，随后停止，转而向南飞行，最后垂直向上飞离视线。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. and Mrs. C. Adams of Beaton Rd., Coxheath, and Mr. and Mrs. Paul Norman of Harold St. Extension.

**Sighting:** The event occurred on July 1, 1979, under a clear sky. The witnesses observed the object from their homes in Coxheath.

**Object:** The object was described as tubular and very bright orange. It remained stationary for a duration of two to three minutes.

**Aftermath:** The object turned cloudy and then disappeared.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 居住在Coxheath的C. Adams夫妇，以及Harold街延伸段的Paul Norman夫妇。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Robert Kenwood (age 12), his parents, and his sister.

**Sighting:** On March 1, 1967, at 0300Z, the witnesses observed an object from their residence at 3485 West 32nd Ave, Vancouver, BC. The weather conditions were reported as 7,000 feet broken visibility, clear.

**Object:** The object was described as oval-shaped and white. It was observed for a duration of seven minutes. The object exhibited non-directional movement and was seen below the clouds. It appeared to rotate at times, displaying red rings during rotation. The object was observed both with and without binoculars.

**Aftermath:** The report was transmitted by RCC Vancouver to CANFORCEHED and noted for the attention of Dr. Millman at the Meteor Centre.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Robert Kenwood（12岁）、他的父母以及他的姐妹。

**目击：** 1967年3月1日0300Z，目击者在位于不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华市西32大道3485号的住所观察到了一个物体。当时的天气状况记录为7000英尺云底高度，能见度清晰。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为椭圆形、白色。观察持续了七分钟。物体呈现无方向性移动，出现在云层下方。它有时会旋转，旋转时显示出红色环状物。目击者通过肉眼和双筒望远镜观察到了该物体。

**后续：** 该报告由温哥华救援协调中心（RCC Vancouver）发送至加拿大部队总部（CANFORCEHED），并注明转交至流星中心（Meteor Centre）的Millman博士。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The crew of the vessel Reel Fisher.

**Sighting:** On November 6, 1966, a fireball was observed near Bella Bella. The object was seen moving from west to east.

**Object:** The object was described as red at first, then turning to snow white. It appeared to disintegrate at the end of the sighting. The duration of the event was 15 to 20 minutes.

**Aftermath:** The report was transmitted to the National Research Council (NRC) for fireball and meteorite observations.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Reel Fisher 号船只的船员。

**目击：** 1966年11月6日，在贝拉贝拉（Bella Bella）附近观测到一个火球。该物体被观察到从西向东移动。

**物体：** 该物体起初呈红色，随后转为雪白色。在目击结束时，它似乎发生了瓦解。事件持续时间为15至20分钟。

**后续：** 该报告被提交给加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC），用于火球和陨石观测记录。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. A. Rayworth.

**Sighting:** The observer was located about two blocks from the object. The event lasted for two minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright, triangular light, white and blue in color. It was silent and hovered just above power lines. The object appeared to be taking juice from the high-power wires, causing house lights to go out until the object disappeared. It bobbed slightly from side to side and up and down while hovering. Upon departure, it flew straight away at an amazing speed.

**Aftermath:** The report was transmitted by CANDEFRAD FALCONBRIDGE to RCCWC/CANFORCENED OPS and the National Research Council.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** A. Rayworth 先生。

**目击：** 观察者距离物体约两个街区。事件持续了两分钟。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为明亮的三角形光点，颜色为白色和蓝色。它保持静止且无声，悬停在高压线正上方。物体似乎在从高压线汲取能量，导致房屋灯光熄灭，直到物体消失。在悬停时，它会轻微地左右及上下摆动。离开时，它以惊人的速度径直飞走。

**后续：** 该报告由 CANDEFRAD FALCONBRIDGE 发送至 RCCWC/CANFORCENED OPS 以及加拿大国家研究委员会。
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_label: Summary (restored from OCR cache for boundary repair)

**Sighting:** The report describes an event occurring on November 15, 1967, at 0215Z in Sudbury. The weather was clear.

**Object:** The object was described as very bright, round, and displaying red, green, and blue colors. It was observed for ten minutes, positioned far to the north-east.

**Aftermath:** The document includes a handwritten note stating "No further action req'd. Letter only."
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Roland Fortin 和 Rick Boulet。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** John Tait and his daughter Gail Tait.

**Sighting:** On 19 November at 1700Z, the witnesses observed a flash of light in the sky, which later turned into a flashing light. The object was hovering directly above, much higher than the clouds.

**Object:** The object was described as a flash of light that turned into a flashing light. Later, at 2300Z, the witness reported seeing five objects resembling rockets with swept-back wings, with no distinguishable color, located in the same area at an extreme height.

**Aftermath:** The sighting lasted approximately 5 minutes.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** John Tait 和他的女儿 Gail Tait。

**目击：** 11月19日 1700Z，目击者观察到天空中出现一道闪光，随后变成闪烁的灯光。该物体悬停在正上方，高度远高于云层。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一道闪光，随后变成闪烁的灯光。后来在 2300Z，目击者报告看到五个类似火箭的物体，带有后掠翼，没有可辨别的颜色，位于同一区域的极高空。

**后续：** 目击持续了大约 5 分钟。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two individuals, one residing on Atlantic Ave, Winnipeg, and one on Kilbride Ave, Winnipeg.

**Sighting:** On October 9, 1969, at approximately 11:15 PM, the witnesses were traveling west on Highway 15, five miles west of Anola, Manitoba. They stopped their vehicle and observed an object for two to three minutes before it disappeared. The sky was clear at the time.

**Object:** The object was described as circular in shape, dull metal in appearance, with red flashing lights. It appeared to be about one mile away, moving in an up and down pattern, falling from high in the sky almost to the ground before returning back up into the sky.

**Aftermath:** The incident was reported to the RCMP and documented in a communication dated October 12, 1969.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:

**Witnesses:** Several civilians in the community of Westport, Newfoundland.

**Sighting:** On August 22, 1969, at approximately 10:30 P.M., witnesses observed a bright, round, red object stationary in the sky east of the community. The sky was clear. The object had blue smoke trailing above it in the shape of the letter "S". It appeared to be sparkling around its circumference before exploding with pieces flying in all directions. Following the explosion, the object decreased in size, resembling a distant star, and slowly descended behind a hill. The total observation time was about five minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright, round, red light. Estimates of its size varied from one to two feet in diameter to 25 feet in diameter. One witness estimated it was 8 miles above the earth and initially thought it was a jet plane on fire.

**Aftermath:** Witnesses reported a loud jukebox playing nearby, but heard no noise from the explosion. The RCMP Baie Verte detachment investigated the report, interviewed witnesses, and forwarded a message (BV 54) to the O.C. St. John's Sub/Division. The witnesses were considered steady and reliable.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 纽芬兰韦斯特波特社区的几位平民。

**目击：** 1969年8月22日晚上10点30分左右，目击者观察到一个明亮的圆形红色物体停留在社区东部的天空中。当时天空晴朗。该物体上方拖着蓝色的烟雾，形状呈“S”型。它在爆炸前圆周闪烁，随后碎片向四面八方飞散。爆炸后，物体体积缩小，看起来像一颗遥远的星星，并缓慢下降到山后。总观测时间约为五分钟。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一个明亮的圆形红光。对其尺寸的估计各不相同，从直径一到两英尺到直径25英尺不等。一位目击者估计它距离地面约8英里，最初以为是一架着火的喷气式飞机。

**后续：** 目击者报告说附近有自动点唱机在播放音乐，但没有听到爆炸声。加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）贝维尔特分遣队对此进行了调查，采访了目击者，并将一份报告（BV 54）转发给了圣约翰斯分区指挥官。目击者被认为是稳重可靠的人。

One witness described the object as round with a steady beam of light, resembling a car's headlight seen at night. The object traveled in an easterly direction for approximately ten minutes.

**Object:** A round object displaying a steady beam of light, described as appearing like a car's headlight.

**Aftermath:** A telex was sent to the NRC Meteor Center and other authorities. On August 24, 1969, an RCMP patrol visited the community to interview witnesses. **Sighting:** On July 1, 1969, at approximately 2:00 a.m., the witness was in the front yard of their home at 212 East 20th Street, North Vancouver, looking toward Vancouver Airport. The witness observed a bright red light that appeared to be an airplane landing light but remained stationary.

**Object:** The witness used a TASCO telescope at 35 power to view the object. Through the scope, the light appeared ten times larger but remained in the same location. The light was bright orange, particularly on the bottom and right side. It eventually moved slowly in a west-south-westerly direction.

**Aftermath:** The witness contacted the Vancouver Airport Meteorological Section to inquire about weather balloons, but was informed there were none. Upon returning outside, the witness observed the light disappear in the direction it had been traveling. The weather was clear and warm with many stars visible.

**后续：** 目击者联系了温哥华机场气象部门询问是否有气象气球，但被告知没有。当目击者再次回到室外时，发现光点已消失在它移动的方向。当晚天气晴朗温暖，星空清晰可见。

**Witnesses:** Two individuals from Taber, Alberta.

**Sighting:** On April 27, 1969, at approximately 2:01 am, two witnesses observed an object near Fincastle, Alberta. The sighting lasted 5 to 6 seconds.

**Object:** The object was described as a large white light, 2 to 3 feet in diameter, which narrowed as it approached. It was grey in color, traveled North, and then left towards the North-East. The object moved fast when approaching, slowed down near the witnesses' vehicle, and sped up again when moving away. A terrible odor was noted from the object's vapour trail.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP conducted inquiries in the Fincastle District but found no other witnesses. The witnesses' brother and another individual were in the vehicle but were asleep and did not see the object, though they were awakened by the witnesses and observed the vapour trail. The RCMP concluded the witnesses were reliable, a sentiment supported by the Taber Town Police. The file was closed as no further information could be obtained.

**后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）在芬卡斯尔地区进行了调查，但未发现其他目击者。目击者的兄弟和另一名人员当时也在车内，但因处于睡眠状态未看到物体，不过他们被目击者叫醒后看到了蒸汽尾迹。加拿大皇家骑警认为目击者是可靠的，塔伯镇警察局也持相同意见。由于无法获得更多有价值的信息，该档案被结案。

**Witnesses:** Three adult residents of Porter Creek, Y.T., and two teenagers in the Whitehorse area.

**Sighting:** On March 4, 1969, between 8:35 p.m. and 8:45 p.m. Y.S.T., three men on the ice at Fish Lake observed a round bluish ball, stationary and half the size of the moon. The object split into two pieces; one remained half-moon sized, while the other turned dark orange, increased in size, and moved back to the original position before both faded away. The objects were 10 degrees above the horizon in the north.

**Object:** A round bluish ball that split into two, with one piece changing color to dark orange and increasing in size.

**物体：** 一个圆形的蓝色球体，分裂成两部分，其中一部分变色为深橙色并增大。

**后续：** 物体消失五分钟后，当三名男子驾驶雪地摩托前往岸边时，整个区域被类似电弧焊的蓝光照亮。光线持续了两到三秒，期间雪地摩托引擎熄火，随后恢复正常。目击者称感受到了类似阳光透过窗玻璃照射的热量。

**Witnesses:** A man, his wife, and their two children residing at 111-5th St NE, Portage la Prairie.

**Sighting:** On April 26, 1969, between 9:45 PM and 9:48 PM Central Daylight Time, a pinkish-colored light was observed from the front yard of the residence. The object was estimated to be approximately one thousand feet above the ground and roughly the size of a headlight at one-quarter mile or one-twentieth size of the moon. It was initially traveling from north to south, approximately five miles north of Portage la Prairie. The light flashed three times, then a minute later flashed two times, before turning in an easterly direction and appearing to go straight down behind the horizon. The object appeared to be waving in an up and down motion and had no trailing effect in the clear sky.

**Object:** A pinkish-colored light, size of a headlight at one-quarter mile, moving with an up and down motion.

**Aftermath:** No other local reports of the sighting were made at the time. The Portage Flying Club, CFB Southport, and Winnipeg Traffic Control advised they had no knowledge of any traffic in the area. The reliability of the information is unknown.

**物体：** 一个粉红色的光点，大小相当于四分之一英里处的车前灯，移动时伴有上下波动。

**Witnesses:** Local residents, including a family group, and RCMP Constable SIGMUNDSON.

**Sighting:** On February 8, 1969, at approximately 9:50 PM, local residents reported a bright object in the sky while traveling west near Two Hills, Alberta. The object appeared to change color from white to orange and back. RCMP Constable SIGMUNDSON observed the object at a distance of approximately one mile north, noting it was low in altitude. The object was lost from sight for 3 to 4 minutes before reappearing, traveling west, and eventually blending into the horizon until it disappeared.

**Object:** A bright, low-altitude object capable of changing color and appearing to travel west.

**Aftermath:** The RCMP detachment sent a Telex message to the Edmonton Sub-Division. On February 9, 1969, a patrol was conducted in the Hairy Hill District to investigate, but no further sightings were reported by area residents. The reporting officer noted that the witnesses were considered credible.
