CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Miss Kimberley Warren (24, insurance agent), Lucille Chaisson (26, secretary), Jack MacPherson, and Patricia MacPherson.

**Date / Time:** July 23, 1979, at approximately 2245 hours (10:45 p.m.) Atlantic Time. *(Note: Page 188 contains a clerical error citing 1953; the case file context confirms the 1979 date).*

**Location:** Heatherton, Antigonish County, Nova Scotia, specifically along Highway 104 and near Malignant Cove/Cape George.

**Sighting:** At 2245 hours, Kimberley Warren and Lucille Chaisson were traveling west on Highway 104, returning from Cape Breton. Five miles east of Heatherton, they observed lights and stopped their vehicle to investigate. Initially mistaking the object for a helicopter, they exited their car and turned off the engine to listen for noise, but heard nothing despite the object’s perceived proximity. They observed the object for seven to eight minutes as it moved in an arched, back-and-forth path. Eventually, the object moved toward George Bay and accelerated at a high rate of speed, disappearing into the Northumberland Strait.

At 2300 hours, Jack and Patricia MacPherson, located at their cottage near Malignant Cove, observed an identical object that remained stationary for 8 to 10 minutes before vanishing. Mr. MacPherson further reported seeing a second set of lights simultaneously, estimated to be five miles or more west of the Cape George sighting. Other unspecified sightings were reported in the area, though no further details were obtained.

**Object:** The object lacked a discernible structural shape. It was described as being comparable in size to a helicopter and appeared at a low altitude. The light configuration consisted of three lights: two very bright white lights at either end that shone continually, and a less bright light in the center that flashed at approximately 15-second intervals. The object moved in an arched path rather than a straight line before accelerating rapidly toward the water.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report was filed by Cst. W.A. Penny and Sgt. J.E. McLean of the RCMP Antigonish Detachment. Statements were taken from the witnesses and reconfirmed the following day. The RCMP noted that the trajectory reported by Warren and Chaisson coincided with the location of the MacPherson sighting over Cape George. The report was relayed via telex to the NRC Meteor Centre in Ottawa on July 24, 1979. While the reliability of Warren and Chaisson was listed as "unknown," the RCMP characterized Mr. and Mrs. MacPherson as "very reliable." Weather conditions at the time were reported as clear.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 金伯利·沃伦（Kimberley Warren，24岁，保险代理人）、露西尔·谢森（Lucille Chaisson，26岁，秘书）、杰克·麦克弗森（Jack MacPherson）以及帕特里夏·麦克弗森（Patricia MacPherson）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1979年7月23日，大西洋时间约22:45（晚上10:45）。*（注：第188页存在笔误，误写为1953年；案件档案背景确认日期为1979年）。*

**地点：** 新斯科舍省安蒂戈尼什县希瑟顿（Heatherton），具体位于104号高速公路沿线及马利格南特湾（Malignant Cove）/乔治角（Cape George）附近。

**目击经过：** 22:45，金伯利·沃伦和露西尔·谢森正驾车沿104号高速公路向西行驶，从布雷顿角返回。在希瑟顿以东五英里处，她们观察到了灯光并停车查看。起初她们误以为该物体是一架直升机，于是下车并关闭引擎以聆听声音，但尽管物体看起来距离很近，她们却未听到任何声响。她们观察了该物体七到八分钟，它呈弧线状来回移动。最终，该物体向乔治湾方向移动，并以极高的速度加速，消失在诺森伯兰海峡中。

23:00，位于马利格南特湾附近小屋的杰克·麦克弗森和帕特里夏·麦克弗森观察到了一个相同的物体，该物体保持静止8到10分钟后消失。麦克弗森先生进一步报告称，同时看到了第二组灯光，估计位于乔治角目击点以西五英里或更远的地方。该地区还报告了其他未指明的目击事件，但未获得更多细节。

**物体描述：** 该物体没有明显的结构形状。据描述，其大小与直升机相当，且出现在低空。灯光配置由三盏灯组成：两端各有一盏持续发光的强亮白灯，中间有一盏亮度较低的灯，每隔约15秒闪烁一次。该物体以弧线而非直线路径移动，随后迅速向水面加速离去。

**调查/后续：** 该报告由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）安蒂戈尼什分局的W.A. 彭尼（W.A. Penny）警员和J.E. 麦克林（J.E. McLean）警长提交。警方记录了目击者的陈述，并于次日进行了复核。加拿大皇家骑警指出，沃伦和谢森报告的轨迹与麦克弗森夫妇在乔治角上空的目击位置相吻合。该报告于1979年7月24日通过电传发送至渥太华的加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心。虽然沃伦和谢森的可靠性被列为“未知”，但加拿大皇家骑警将麦克弗森夫妇描述为“非常可靠”。据报告，当时天气状况晴朗。

**Witnesses:** Mrs. McCormick

**Date / Time:** July 25, 1979, at 0200Z (also recorded as 0202Z)

**Location:** Trans Canada Highway, near Ville St. Laurent, Quebec

**Sighting:** 
The sighting occurred in the early morning hours of July 25, 1979. The witness, Mrs. McCormick, who resided at 2388 Gold St. in Ville St. Laurent, observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while in the vicinity of the Trans Canada Highway. According to the reports, the atmospheric conditions at the time were clear, though a degree of haze was noted. Mrs. McCormick observed the object performing specific maneuvers, noting that it would stop, hover in place, and then suddenly disappear.

**Object:** 
The object was described as round in shape with a diameter of approximately 2 1/2 inches (as perceived from the witness's vantage point). It was pale white in color. The object was observed at an altitude estimated between 3,000 and 4,000 feet. No sound was reported in association with the object's movement or hovering behavior.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The incident was formally documented and transmitted through official military and governmental channels. The report originated from 22 NRHQ (North Bay) and was sent to the RCCMC/NDOC (National Defence Operations Centre) in Ottawa. Information copies of the sighting report were also distributed to the National Research Council (NRC) in Ottawa for further review. No additional physical evidence or sketches were noted in the provided documentation.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Roger Mainville (Canadair guard), Lieutenant J.M. Guay (also referred to as Lieut J.M. Gray), two unnamed individuals, Marcel Campeau (industrial security investigator), Tom Way (Public Relations), John Robinson (Public Relations).

**Date / Time:** Mid-June 1979, approximately 4:30 PM.

**Location:** Canadair Limited facility, Ville St-Laurent, Quebec (specifically the back of the airfield).

**Sighting:** The incident originated from a telephone report received by Lieutenant J.M. Guay at the Canadair facility. A caller and his friend reported observing an unidentified flying object (O.V.N.I.) hovering above the Canadair airfield in mid-June 1979 at approximately 4:30 PM. Following this report, internal inquiries were conducted among the night shift guards to determine if others had witnessed the event; initially, all guards denied seeing anything unusual. 

However, on July 27, 1979, guard Roger Mainville came forward to report that he had indeed observed an unidentified object near the Canadair facility during that same mid-June period. Mainville admitted he had hesitated to report the sighting earlier due to a fear of ridicule from others. Notably, Mainville claimed that Lieutenant M. Guay had reported a similar observation of an object only a few hours earlier on the same morning that Mainville had his sighting.

**Object:** The reports consistently describe the phenomenon as an Unidentified Flying Object (O.V.N.I. / Objet Volant Non Identifié). While specific physical dimensions, colors, or sounds were not detailed in the surviving documentation, the object was observed in the vicinity of the Canadair airfield. Roger Mainville provided drawings of his observation as part of his formal statement.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The investigation involved multiple departments at Canadair and the RCMP. Lieutenant J.M. Guay initially passed the contact information for the two anonymous witnesses to Tom Way in Public Relations. John Robinson, also of Public Relations, attempted to contact these individuals by phone repeatedly over two days but received no answer; the contact information was subsequently discarded, and the call was dismissed by some officials as likely coming from an "irrational person."

Following Roger Mainville’s late report on July 27, 1979, Marcel Campeau, an industrial security investigator, formally notified the RCMP. Mainville requested and received permission to share his account and drawings with a team of UFO specialists based in Beloeil, Quebec, to seek an expert opinion. The official file, managed by Captain M.J. Jacques of the S.E.G. Montreal, was eventually marked "TERMINE" (Terminated/Closed). A copy of the final report was forwarded to the National Research Council, Planetary Sciences Section, in Ottawa.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_14_-_Pages_39.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗杰·曼维尔（Roger Mainville，加拿大飞机公司警卫）、J.M. 盖伊中尉（Lieutenant J.M. Guay，亦被称为 J.M. 格雷中尉）、两名未具名人士、马塞尔·坎波（Marcel Campeau，工业安全调查员）、汤姆·韦（Tom Way，公共关系部）、约翰·罗宾逊（John Robinson，公共关系部）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1979年6月中旬，下午4:30左右。

**地点：** 魁北克省圣洛朗市（Ville St-Laurent）加拿大飞机公司（Canadair Limited）设施（具体位于机场后方）。

**目击经过：** 事件源于加拿大飞机公司设施内的 J.M. 盖伊中尉接到的一通电话报告。一名来电者及其朋友报告称，1979年6月中旬下午4:30左右，他们观察到一个不明飞行物（O.V.N.I.）悬停在加拿大飞机公司机场上空。此后，公司内部对夜班警卫进行了询问，以确定是否还有其他人目击了该事件；起初，所有警卫均否认看到任何异常情况。

然而，1979年7月27日，警卫罗杰·曼维尔主动报告称，他在6月中旬的同一时期确实在加拿大飞机公司设施附近观察到了一个不明物体。曼维尔承认，他此前因担心遭到嘲笑而迟迟未敢报告。值得注意的是，曼维尔声称，在曼维尔目击事件的当天上午，盖伊中尉也曾报告过类似的物体目击事件。

**物体描述：** 报告一致将该现象描述为不明飞行物（O.V.N.I. / Objet Volant Non Identifié）。虽然现存文件中未详细说明具体的物理尺寸、颜色或声音，但该物体是在加拿大飞机公司机场附近被观察到的。罗杰·曼维尔在正式陈述中提供了他所观察到的物体绘图。

**调查/后续：** 
调查涉及加拿大飞机公司的多个部门以及加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）。J.M. 盖伊中尉最初将两名匿名目击者的联系方式交给了公共关系部的汤姆·韦。同属公共关系部的约翰·罗宾逊曾尝试在两天内多次通过电话联系这些人，但无人接听；随后这些联系信息被丢弃，一些官员认为该电话很可能来自“非理性人士”。

在罗杰·曼维尔于1979年7月27日迟来的报告之后，工业安全调查员马塞尔·坎波正式通知了加拿大皇家骑警。曼维尔请求并获得了许可，将其陈述和绘图分享给位于魁北克省贝洛伊尔（Beloeil）的一个不明飞行物专家小组，以寻求专家意见。由蒙特利尔 S.E.G. 的 M.J. 雅克上尉（Captain M.J. Jacques）管理的官方档案最终被标记为“TERMINE”（已终止/结案）。最终报告的副本被转交至位于渥太华的国家研究委员会行星科学部门。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Two separate observers on West 19th Street (Vancouver), and unspecified witnesses at the foot of 21st Avenue (West Vancouver).

**Date / Time:** July 31, 1965; sightings reported at 0400Z and 0630Z–0645Z.

**Location:** Vancouver, British Columbia (specifically West 19th Street and the shoreline of Burrard Inlet at the foot of 21st Avenue, West Vancouver).

**Sighting:** This event involves two distinct sets of observations reported on the same day. The first sighting occurred at 0400Z at the foot of 21st Avenue in West Vancouver, along the Burrard Inlet shoreline. Witnesses observed an object positioned south, approximately 5 degrees above the horizon, under clear weather conditions. The object remained visible for 15 minutes before it appeared to break down into four separate lights. It remained steady in the sky for a duration before falling toward the earth at a 45-degree angle and disappearing.

A second, independent report was filed by two observers living on West 19th Street, who reported the event without knowledge of the other’s account. This sighting began at 0630Z and lasted for at least 30 minutes, concluding at 0645Z. The object was observed moving slowly toward the west, positioned west of the airport at an altitude of approximately 5,000 feet.

**Object:** The descriptions vary by observation time. The 0400Z object was described as brighter than a star, bright white in color, and oblong in shape. It exhibited a unique behavior of splitting into four separate lights before descending. The 0630Z object was also described as brighter than a star and larger than planets, but it was characterized by a flashing red and white light pattern. No sound was reported for either observation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Official inquiries were conducted following the reports. The Vancouver Air Traffic Control tower attempted to verify the 0630Z sighting but was unable to locate the object either visually or via radar. The reports were processed by the Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) Vancouver and forwarded to CANFORCEHED OPS. The documentation was also sent to W. Slawson at the University of British Columbia, with an official notation indicating that the file was scheduled for review by the Meteor Centre at the National Research Council (NRC).
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 西19街（温哥华）的两名独立观察者，以及西温哥华21大道尽头的若干未具名目击者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1965年7月31日；目击报告时间分别为0400Z和0630Z–0645Z。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华（具体地点为西19街及西温哥华21大道尽头的布拉德内湾海岸线）。

**目击经过：** 此事件涉及同一天报告的两组不同观测记录。第一次目击发生在0400Z，地点位于西温哥华21大道尽头，布拉德内湾（Burrard Inlet）沿岸。在天气晴朗的条件下，目击者观察到一个位于南方、地平线上方约5度位置的物体。该物体可见时长为15分钟，随后似乎分裂成四个独立的光点。它在空中保持了一段时间的稳定，之后以45度角向地面坠落并消失。

第二份独立报告由居住在西19街的两名观察者提交，他们在互不知情的情况下报告了此次事件。该次目击始于0630Z，持续了至少30分钟，于0645Z结束。物体被观察到正缓慢向西移动，位于机场以西，高度约为5000英尺。

**物体描述：** 描述因观测时间而异。0400Z出现的物体被描述为比恒星更亮，呈亮白色，形状为长方形。它表现出一种独特的行为，即在下降前分裂成四个独立的光点。0630Z出现的物体同样被描述为比恒星更亮、比行星更大，但其特征是闪烁着红白相间的光。两次观测均未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 报告提交后进行了官方调查。温哥华空中交通管制塔台曾试图核实0630Z的目击事件，但无论是通过目视还是雷达均未能发现该物体。这些报告由温哥华救援协调中心（RCC）处理并转交至加拿大武装部队总部作战部（CANFORCEHED OPS）。相关文件也被送交至不列颠哥伦比亚大学的W. 斯劳森（W. Slawson），官方记录显示该档案已列入国家研究委员会（NRC）流星中心的审查计划。

**Witnesses:** Personnel at the Comox Control Tower.

**Date / Time:** April 7, 1966, at 0505Z.

**Location:** Comox, British Columbia.

**Sighting:** On April 7, 1966, at 0505Z, personnel at the Comox Control Tower reported an unidentified aerial phenomenon described as a fireball or meteorite. Simultaneously, radar data recorded the event, with a bearing of 190 degrees from the Comox TACAN and RATCON stations. Radar operators plotted the target and noted that it exhibited erratic flight patterns. The radar tracking indicated that the targets initially came close together before moving apart. The observation was further corroborated by visual sightings through field glasses; observers noted that there was no moon present during the event to interfere with the visual identification. The report of this sighting was officially transmitted by the Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) in Vancouver to CANFORCENED OPS and to Dr. B. Slauson at the University of British Columbia for further review.

**Object:** The object was described as two white lights of variable intensity. The lights were roundish in shape. Radar tracking confirmed the presence of the targets, noting erratic flight behavior. No specific speed was recorded for the objects, and while they were initially tracked as a single radar return that moved in proximity, they eventually separated. The duration of the sighting is linked to the 0505Z timestamp, though the total length of the observation is not explicitly stated.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented in official records, including a typed summary table (labeled "PAGE 2 RCVC 18"). The investigation involved both radar plotting and visual confirmation via field glasses. The report was formally processed by RCC Vancouver and forwarded to military operations (CANFORCENED OPS) and the academic community (Dr. B. Slauson at UBC). A handwritten notation, "DT 139," appears on the documentation, though its specific significance remains unclear. Despite the detailed radar and visual reporting, the official entry for witnesses on the summary table (item J) was recorded as "NIL," likely referring to the absence of civilian witnesses in that specific reporting format, even though Comox Control Tower personnel were the primary observers.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 科莫克斯（Comox）控制塔工作人员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1966年4月7日，0505Z（协调世界时）。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省，科莫克斯。

**目击经过：** 1966年4月7日0505Z，科莫克斯控制塔的工作人员报告称目击到一种不明空中现象，被描述为火球或陨石。与此同时，雷达数据记录了该事件，方位为科莫克斯战术空中导航系统（TACAN）和雷达终端控制（RATCON）站的190度方向。雷达操作员对目标进行了标绘，并指出其飞行模式不稳定。雷达追踪显示，这些目标最初靠得很近，随后又分离开来。通过双筒望远镜进行的目视观测进一步证实了这一现象；观察者指出，当时没有月光干扰目视识别。该目击报告由温哥华救援协调中心（RCC）正式传达给加拿大部队指挥中心（CANFORCENED OPS）以及不列颠哥伦比亚大学的B. 斯劳森（B. Slauson）博士进行进一步审查。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为两道亮度不一的白光，形状呈圆形。雷达追踪证实了目标的存在，并记录到其不稳定的飞行行为。报告未记录物体的具体速度，虽然它们最初被追踪为一个移动接近的单一雷达回波，但最终分开了。目击持续时间与0505Z的时间戳相关，但未明确说明总观测时长。

**调查/后续：** 该事件被记录在官方档案中，包括一份打印的汇总表（标记为“PAGE 2 RCVC 18”）。调查涉及雷达标绘和通过双筒望远镜进行的目视确认。该报告由温哥华救援协调中心正式处理，并转发给军事行动部门（CANFORCENED OPS）和学术界（不列颠哥伦比亚大学的B. 斯劳森博士）。文档上出现了一个手写标注“DT 139”，但其具体含义尚不明确。尽管有详细的雷达和目视报告，汇总表（J项）中关于目击者的官方条目仍被记录为“无”（NIL），这很可能是指在该特定报告格式中缺乏平民目击者，尽管科莫克斯控制塔的工作人员是主要的观测者。

**Witnesses:** Mr. Lloyd Williams, Mr. and Mrs. Join Andrews, Mr. Smith, and several other members of the Mount Currey Indian Reserve.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Frank Schleiermacher (age 12), Mrs. Schleiermacher, and several unnamed drivers/observers in the Nelson area.

**Date / Time:** December 29, 1967, at 4:55 PM PST.

**Location:** North Shore, Nelson, British Columbia (near Elephant Mountain, Kootenay River, and the West Arm of Kootenay Lake).

**Sighting:** On the evening of December 29, 1967, multiple witnesses in the Nelson, B.C. area observed a mysterious aerial phenomenon. Frank Schleiermacher, age 12, observed the object from his parents' driveway on the North Shore. According to his account, the object emerged from behind Elephant Mountain and traveled south across Kootenay Lake. The object moved at a very low altitude, appearing to pass behind a cloud, reappearing, and eventually disappearing behind a low cloud base. The sighting lasted approximately 2–3 minutes. Several other drivers and observers in the same vicinity also reported seeing the object, as corroborated by a map/sketch in the official file that plots the trajectory relative to the Kootenay River and the West Arm.

**Object:** The object was described with varying details by witnesses. Frank Schleiermacher initially described it as an "orange ball" with sparks falling from it, noting it resembled a helicopter on fire. Other descriptions characterized it as a bright, whitish, fiery object with a small beam of light emitting from the top. The object was observed at an elevation of 70 degrees, bearing Southeast. No sounds were reported by the primary witness.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The event was documented by R.D. McAllister in Rossland, B.C., on December 30, 1967. The National Research Council of Canada file includes a handwritten sketch mapping the object's path relative to local landmarks. Official inquiries were made with Air-Sea Rescue in Vancouver, who confirmed they had received no reports of aircraft in distress. Initially, the RCMP stated they had no knowledge of the event. However, a subsequent handwritten note added to the file by authorities concluded that the incident was "explained as [a] children's prank."
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 弗兰克·施莱尔马赫（Frank Schleiermacher，12岁）、施莱尔马赫夫人，以及纳尔逊（Nelson）地区的几位未具名司机/观察者。

**日期 / 时间：** 1967年12月29日下午4:55（太平洋标准时间）。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省纳尔逊北岸（靠近象山、库特奈河及库特奈湖西湾）。

**目击经过：** 1967年12月29日傍晚，不列颠哥伦比亚省纳尔逊地区的数名目击者观察到一种神秘的空中现象。12岁的弗兰克·施莱尔马赫在他父母位于北岸的私家车道上观察到了该物体。据他描述，该物体从象山（Elephant Mountain）后方出现，向南飞越库特奈湖。物体飞行高度极低，在穿过云层后方时消失，随后又再次出现，最终消失在低云层后。目击过程持续了约2至3分钟。该地区的其他几名司机和观察者也报告看到了该物体，官方档案中的地图/草图证实了这一点，该图绘制了物体相对于库特奈河和西湾的飞行轨迹。

**物体描述：** 目击者对该物体的描述细节各异。弗兰克·施莱尔马赫最初将其描述为一个带有火花坠落的“橙色球体”，并称其看起来像一架着火的直升机。其他描述则将其形容为一个明亮的、发白的火球，顶部射出一束微弱的光。观察时该物体仰角为70度，方位东南。主要目击者称未听到任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由罗斯兰（Rossland）的R.D.麦卡利斯特（R.D. McAllister）于1967年12月30日记录。加拿大国家研究委员会的档案中包含一张手绘草图，标绘了该物体相对于当地地标的飞行路径。官方曾向温哥华的海空救援中心（Air-Sea Rescue）进行查询，对方确认未收到任何飞机遇险的报告。起初，加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）表示对此事件一无所知。然而，当局随后在档案中添加的一份手写备注得出结论，称该事件“解释为儿童恶作剧”。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary: The three pages are best read as one continuing account from Douglas. A later note adds that a neighbor saw a similar light in Sept. 1967 in the same area near the C.N.R. tracks, but the writer suspects it may have been a person with a flashlight near the railroad line. The final page narrows the location to Douglas station between the 1st and 2nd crossings, just east of the 1st crossing.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Charles Forbes (also referred to as Mrs. Forbes)

**Date / Time:** January 7, 1968; 3:00 AM to approximately 4:30 AM (sighting duration noted as 20 minutes in one account and 1.5 hours in another)

**Location:** Southview Avenue, near the Cornwallis River, Kentville, Nova Scotia

**Sighting:** 
On January 7, 1968, at 3:00 AM, Mrs. Charles Forbes observed an unidentified aerial object from her residence on Southview Avenue, near the Cornwallis River. According to the witness, the object approached from the north, slowed down, and hovered in the vicinity for a period estimated between 20 minutes and one and a half hours. 

During the observation, the object exhibited erratic behavior, including stopping and appearing to "disintegrate" at intervals. Mrs. Forbes reported that the object eventually turned and moved directly toward her house. Due to fear, the witness remained inside and did not open the door to investigate further. She also chose not to wake her husband, fearing the object would vanish before he could witness it. The sighting concluded when the witness, unsettled by the object's proximity to the house, went to bed.

**Object:** 
The object was described as orange in color with distinct blue tinges, particularly on the bottom. In terms of scale, the witness compared its size to that of the sun, though she noted it was significantly less bright. The object emitted "balls of fire" or "star balls" from its underside, which the witness likened to engine exhaust. Additionally, the object produced blue flashes that caused visible reflections on the windows of the house. No sound was reported during the duration of the event.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The documentation consists of two separate reports detailing the same event. The records indicate that the witness was too frightened to leave the safety of her home to obtain a better view or to verify the object's physical presence outside. There is no mention of external physical evidence, such as ground traces or radar confirmation, in the provided files. The investigation notes focus primarily on the witness's subjective experience and her decision-making process during the encounter.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 查尔斯·福布斯夫人（Mrs. Charles Forbes，亦被称为福布斯夫人）

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年1月7日；凌晨3:00至大约4:30（目击时长在不同记录中分别被描述为20分钟和1.5小时）

**地点：** 新斯科舍省肯特维尔，康沃利斯河附近的南景大道（Southview Avenue）

**目击经过：**
1968年1月7日凌晨3:00，查尔斯·福布斯夫人在其位于康沃利斯河附近南景大道的住所内，观察到一个不明飞行物体。据目击者称，该物体从北方靠近，随后减速并在附近盘旋，停留时间估计在20分钟到1.5小时之间。

在观察过程中，该物体表现出不规则的飞行行为，包括停滞以及间歇性地出现“解体”现象。福布斯夫人报告称，该物体最终转向并径直朝她的房子飞来。由于感到恐惧，目击者一直待在室内，没有开门进一步查看。她还选择不去叫醒丈夫，担心在丈夫赶来之前物体就会消失。当目击者因物体过于靠近住所而感到不安并上床休息时，此次目击事件结束。

**物体描述：**
该物体被描述为橙色，带有明显的蓝色调，尤其是在底部。在比例方面，目击者将其大小比作太阳，但指出其亮度明显不及太阳。该物体从底部喷射出“火球”或“星状球体”，目击者将其比作引擎排气。此外，该物体还会产生蓝色闪光，在房屋窗户上形成可见的反射。整个事件过程中未报告任何声音。

**调查/后续：**

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. F. Van Vaals (Wooler), Mrs. J. (Jane) Dorland (Wooler), Mr. T.H. Burgess (Campbellford), and an unnamed CN employee (Brighton).

**Date / Time:** March 8, 1968; reports cluster between 0700Z and 0808Z (08h U.T.).

**Location:** Brighton, Wooler, and Campbellford, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On the morning of March 8, 1968, multiple residents across the Brighton, Wooler, and Campbellford areas reported a significant aerial event. Radio station CJBQ broadcast reports from Brighton residents describing a yellow light in the sky accompanied by a noise likened to a truck traveling at high speed. 

Specific witness accounts provide varying details:
*   **Mr. F. Van Vaals (Wooler):** Reported being awakened by a loud roar that shook his house. He specifically noted hearing a buzzing sound followed by a loud bang, emphasizing that the noise was distinct and unlike any aircraft sounds typically heard from the nearby Trenton base.
*   **Mrs. Jane Dorland (Wooler):** A neighbor to Mr. Van Vaals, she was also awakened by an explosion. She observed a "ball of fire" passing from east to west. In a separate account, she described the object as a bright white light, as luminous as a full moon, moving south at a speed comparable to an airplane, though slower than a falling star.
*   **CN Employee (Brighton):** Alerted by an explosion, this witness went outside and observed a light flashing for approximately two minutes.
*   **Mr. T.H. Burgess (Campbellford):** The owner of the Crest Hardware Store reported that a window at his place of business was blown out at 0800Z–0808Z, coinciding with the timing of the aerial reports.

**Object:** The object was described variously as a "yellow light," a "ball of fire," and a "bright white light." It was associated with a loud, house-shaking roar, a buzzing sound, and a distinct explosion or "bang." The duration of the light was noted as approximately two minutes by one witness. The movement was described as traveling east to west, or south, at a speed similar to an airplane.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The reports were formally documented and logged by the National Research Council of Canada under file numbers N68/1015, N68/016, and N68/017. The event was widely reported via local media, including radio station CJBQ. The physical damage to the Crest Hardware Store window in Campbellford serves as the primary physical evidence associated with the timing of the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** F. 范·瓦尔斯先生（F. Van Vaals，伍勒）、J.（简）多兰夫人（Mrs. J. (Jane) Dorland，伍勒）、T.H. 伯吉斯先生（T.H. Burgess，坎贝尔福德），以及一名未透露姓名的加拿大国家铁路（CN）员工（布莱顿）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年3月8日；报告集中在 0700Z 至 0808Z（世界协调时 08 时）之间。

**地点：** 安大略省布莱顿（Brighton）、伍勒（Wooler）和坎贝尔福德（Campbellford）。

**目击经过：** 1968年3月8日上午，布莱顿、伍勒和坎贝尔福德地区的众多居民报告了一起重大的空中事件。CJBQ广播电台播报了来自布莱顿居民的报告，描述天空中出现一道黄光，并伴有类似高速行驶卡车的噪音。

具体目击者描述的细节如下：
*   **F. 范·瓦尔斯先生（伍勒）：** 报告称被一阵震动房屋的巨大轰鸣声惊醒。他特别提到听到了一种嗡嗡声，随后是一声巨响，并强调这种噪音非常独特，与附近特伦顿（Trenton）空军基地常见的飞机声音完全不同。
*   **简·多兰夫人（伍勒）：** 作为范·瓦尔斯先生的邻居，她也被爆炸声惊醒。她观察到一个“火球”由东向西飞过。在另一份陈述中，她将该物体描述为一道明亮的白光，亮度如同满月，正向南移动，速度与飞机相当，但比流星慢。
*   **CN员工（布莱顿）：** 该目击者被爆炸声惊动后走到户外，观察到一道闪烁的光持续了约两分钟。
*   **T.H. 伯吉斯先生（坎贝尔福德）：** Crest五金店的老板报告称，他的店面窗户在 0800Z 至 0808Z 之间被震碎，这与空中目击报告的时间相吻合。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为“黄光”、“火球”和“明亮的白光”。它伴随着巨大的、震动房屋的轰鸣声、嗡嗡声以及明显的爆炸声或“巨响”。据一位目击者称，光芒持续了约两分钟。其运动轨迹被描述为由东向西或向南移动，速度与飞机相似。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大国家研究委员会（National Research Council of Canada）正式记录并归档了这些报告，档案编号为 N68/1015、N68/016 和 N68/017。该事件通过包括CJBQ广播电台在内的当地媒体进行了广泛报道。坎贝尔福德Crest五金店窗户的物理损坏，是与此次目击事件时间相吻合的主要物证。

**Witnesses:** John Lloyd Walters, Mrs. J.L. Walters, Mr. J.A. Blyer

**Date / Time:** March 24, 1968, at 8:00 PM

**Location:** Merritt, British Columbia (specifically near the Merritt dumpyard)

**Sighting:** On the evening of March 24, 1968, at approximately 8:00 PM, three witnesses—John Lloyd Walters, Mrs. J.L. Walters, and Mr. J.A. Blyer—observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while in the vicinity of Merritt, BC. The witnesses reported that the sky was clear with visible stars at the time of the sighting. The object was observed at an estimated altitude of one mile. The sighting lasted for a duration of approximately 20 minutes. According to the collective account of the witnesses, the object appeared to descend and land in the area of the Merritt dumpyard. Despite the proximity of the landing site, no noise was reported by any of the observers.

**Object:** The object was described as a single, bright amber light. When the object was in motion, it exhibited a distinct pulsation, shifting in color from amber to white. No other physical characteristics, such as shape or size, were explicitly detailed beyond the appearance of a bright light. The object remained visible for a total of 20 minutes before its apparent landing.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the report of the sighting, an official search of the Merritt dumpyard area was conducted to locate any evidence of the object or its landing; however, the search yielded no results. The incident was formally documented by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). The report was subsequently transmitted via RCMP telex to CANFORCEHEAD (Canadian Forces Headquarters). As part of the administrative follow-up, the RCMP included a request for clarification regarding the proper reporting procedures to be followed for future UFO sightings of this nature.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 约翰·劳埃德·沃尔特斯 (John Lloyd Walters)、J.L. 沃尔特斯夫人 (Mrs. J.L. Walters)、J.A. 布莱尔先生 (Mr. J.A. Blyer)

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年3月24日，晚上8:00

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省梅里特 (Merritt)（具体位于梅里特垃圾场附近）

**目击经过：** 1968年3月24日晚约8:00，三名目击者——约翰·劳埃德·沃尔特斯、J.L. 沃尔特斯夫人和 J.A. 布莱尔先生在不列颠哥伦比亚省梅里特附近观察到一种不明空中现象。据目击者称，当时天空晴朗，星光可见。该物体被观测到的高度估计为一英里。目击过程持续了约20分钟。根据目击者们的共同描述，该物体似乎下降并降落在梅里特垃圾场区域。尽管降落地点距离很近，但所有观察者均表示未听到任何声响。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个单一的、明亮的琥珀色光点。当物体移动时，它呈现出明显的脉动，颜色从琥珀色变为白色。除了明亮的光点外，没有详细说明其他物理特征，如形状或大小。该物体在降落前总共可见20分钟。

**调查 / 后续：** 在接到目击报告后，官方对梅里特垃圾场区域进行了搜查，试图寻找该物体或其降落的任何证据；然而，搜查没有任何发现。该事件由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 正式记录在案。报告随后通过加拿大皇家骑警电传发送至加拿大武装部队总部 (CANFORCEHEAD)。作为行政后续行动的一部分，加拿大皇家骑警还请求明确未来此类不明飞行物目击事件应遵循的正确报告程序。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cst. Aird, Cst. Larochelle, Gordon Apostoliuk, Raymond Jones, and Wayne Neil Ayres.

**Date / Time:** April 27, 1968, at 12:10 AM. The objects were no longer sighted after 1:00 AM.

**Location:** North of Rossland, British Columbia.

**Sighting:** At 12:10 AM on April 27, 1968, a group consisting of Cst. Aird, Cst. Larochelle, Gordon Apostoliuk, Raymond Jones, and Wayne Neil Ayres observed three unidentified objects positioned north of Rossland, BC. At the time of the sighting, the sky was clear. 

In an attempt to identify or approach the phenomena, a patrol was conducted, moving toward the objects for a distance of 18 miles. Despite this significant change in proximity, the witnesses noted no difference in the appearance of the objects. During the observation period, two of the three objects were seen moving; one of these moving objects eventually traveled out of sight. The remaining two objects were observed for a duration of over half an hour using binoculars. The sighting concluded when the objects were no longer visible after 1:00 AM.

**Object:** The event involved three distinct objects. While the specific shape of the objects could not be determined by the witnesses, they were characterized by a distinct flashing pattern of three colors: red, yellow, and blue. The objects remained visible for approximately 50 minutes, with two of the three objects observed in motion before one disappeared from view.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The initial observations were documented by the attending officers and witnesses. Following the conclusion of the sighting at 1:00 AM, it was noted that a formal report regarding the incident was to be submitted by the Trail Detachment of the RCMP. No further atmospheric or physical anomalies were reported following the cessation of the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 艾尔德警官 (Cst. Aird)、拉罗谢尔警官 (Cst. Larochelle)、戈登·阿波斯托柳克 (Gordon Apostoliuk)、雷蒙德·琼斯 (Raymond Jones) 以及韦恩·尼尔·艾尔斯 (Wayne Neil Ayres)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年4月27日凌晨12:10。凌晨1:00后，这些物体消失不见。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省罗斯兰 (Rossland) 北部。

**目击经过：** 1968年4月27日凌晨12:10，由艾尔德警官、拉罗谢尔警官、戈登·阿波斯托柳克、雷蒙德·琼斯和韦恩·尼尔·艾尔斯组成的一行人在不列颠哥伦比亚省罗斯兰北部观察到了三个不明物体。目击时，天空晴朗。

为了辨认或接近这些现象，一行人进行了巡逻，向物体方向行进了18英里。尽管距离发生了显著变化，但目击者指出物体的外观没有任何改变。在观察期间，三个物体中有两个在移动；其中一个移动的物体最终消失在视野之外。其余两个物体通过双筒望远镜被观察了半个多小时。目击事件于凌晨1:00物体消失后结束。

**物体描述：** 该事件涉及三个独特的物体。虽然目击者无法确定物体的具体形状，但它们呈现出红、黄、蓝三种颜色的独特闪烁模式。这些物体可见时长约为50分钟，其中两个物体在其中一个消失前被观察到处于运动状态。

**调查/后续：** 最初的观察结果由在场的警官和目击者记录在案。在凌晨1:00目击事件结束后，记录显示加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 特雷尔分遣队 (Trail Detachment) 将提交一份关于此事件的正式报告。在目击事件结束后，未再有关于大气或物理异常的报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** A patient at Northwestern General Hospital, four other unnamed persons in the same hospital ward, an unnamed male caller, a reporter from the *Kitchener Record*, and several unnamed residents of the Kitchener district and Elmira.

**Date / Time:** July 3, 1968; 030110Z to 030112Z (with a second report from a male caller occurring five minutes later).

**Location:** Northwestern General Hospital (Toronto, ON), Kitchener, ON, and Elmira, ON.

**Sighting:** On July 3, 1968, a series of sightings were reported across Southern Ontario. The primary account originated from a patient at Northwestern General Hospital, who, along with four other individuals in the same hospital ward, observed a bright, round object moving south at a high rate of speed. The witnesses noted that the object was emitting green sparks as it traveled. The weather conditions at the time of the observation were reported as clear. 

Approximately five minutes after the initial sighting, an anonymous male caller contacted the authorities to report the same phenomenon, providing a description consistent with the hospital witnesses. Simultaneously, the *Kitchener Record* newspaper reported receiving multiple inquiries and accounts from residents throughout the Kitchener district and Elmira regarding the activity. These reports were corroborated by independent sightings received by the Toronto International Airport, which also logged reports of the object. The collective accounts from these various locations suggest a widespread event involving a fireball or meteorite-like activity moving through the region.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright, round body. It was observed moving at a fast speed and was characterized by the emission of green sparks. No sound was reported. The duration of the primary sighting was approximately two seconds (030110Z to 030112Z).

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Official follow-up was initiated through the receipt of multiple reports by the Toronto International Airport and the *Kitchener Record*. The *Kitchener Record* actively investigated the event as a potential fireball or meteorite incident, noting that the volume of reports from the Kitchener and Elmira areas indicated a significant aerial event. The documentation confirms that the reports were cross-referenced between the hospital witnesses, the anonymous caller, and the regional newspaper inquiries to establish the timeline and trajectory of the object.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 西北总医院（Northwestern General Hospital）的一名患者、同病房的其他四名未具名人士、一名未具名的男性来电者、《基奇纳记录报》（Kitchener Record）的一名记者，以及基奇纳地区和埃尔迈拉（Elmira）的多名未具名居民。

**日期 / 时间：** 1968年7月3日；030110Z至030112Z（五分钟后收到第二份来自男性来电者的报告）。

**地点：** 西北总医院（安大略省多伦多市）、安大略省基奇纳市及埃尔迈拉。

**目击经过：** 1968年7月3日，安大略省南部地区报告了一系列目击事件。主要目击记录来自西北总医院的一名患者，他与同病房的其他四人共同观察到一个明亮的圆形物体正以极高的速度向南移动。目击者指出，该物体在飞行过程中不断喷射出绿色火花。据报告，观测时的天气状况晴朗。

在最初的目击事件发生约五分钟后，一名匿名男性来电者联系了有关部门报告了同样的现象，其描述与医院目击者提供的情况一致。与此同时，《基奇纳记录报》报告称，他们收到了来自基奇纳地区和埃尔迈拉各地居民关于该活动的多次询问和目击陈述。这些报告得到了多伦多国际机场收到的独立目击报告的证实，机场方面也记录了关于该物体的报告。来自这些不同地点的汇总记录表明，这是一起涉及火球或类似陨石的活动在区域内移动的广泛事件。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个明亮的圆形天体。据观察，它以极快的速度移动，并伴有绿色火花喷射。未报告有声音。主要目击持续时间约为两秒（030110Z至030112Z）。

**调查/后续：** 官方后续调查始于多伦多国际机场和《基奇纳记录报》收到的多份报告。《基奇纳记录报》积极对该事件进行了调查，将其视为潜在的火球或陨石事件，并指出基奇纳和埃尔迈拉地区的大量报告表明这是一起重大的空中事件。相关文件证实，通过对医院目击者、匿名来电者以及地区报纸询问记录的交叉比对，确定了该物体的飞行时间线和轨迹。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Local camera enthusiasts.

**Sighting:** On Wednesday, June 19th, 1968, at approximately 10:30 p.m., an unidentified flying object was observed in the sky above Frobisher Bay moving in a northerly direction.

**Object:** The object appeared to be a star moving very slowly across the sky in a west to east direction. It disappeared sometime after midnight.

**Aftermath:** The Department of Transport meteorological officer in Frobisher Bay expressed the opinion that the object was an experimental or weather balloon at a height of well over 100,000 feet. The report notes there were no reports of landings by "little green men or other weird sun-could creatures" or reports that "all our women are pregnant." The document was forwarded by D. Davies, Regional Administrator, and received by Ian Halliday of the Dominion Observatory, who noted it was forwarded as a non-meteoric sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_01_-_Pages_1-.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 当地的摄影爱好者。

**目击：** 1968年6月19日星期三晚上约10:30，在弗罗比舍湾上空观察到一个不明飞行物，向北移动。

**物体：** 该物体看起来像一颗星星，正非常缓慢地从西向东横穿天空。它在午夜后消失。

**后续：** 弗罗比舍湾的交通部气象官员认为该物体是一个高度超过10万英尺的实验性气球或气象气球。报告指出，没有关于“小绿人或其他怪异生物”着陆的报告，也没有关于“我们所有的妇女都怀孕了”的报告。该文件由区域行政官D. Davies转发，并由自治领天文台的Ian Halliday收到，他注明该报告是作为非流星目击事件转发的。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Jean Widish, John Widish, Janet Widish, Debbie Widish

**Date / Time:** January 31, 1977, at approximately 9:30 PM

**Location:** Rosenburg/Arborg, Manitoba (Land NBR NW19-24-3E)

**Sighting:** On the evening of January 31, 1977, at approximately 9:30 PM, the Widish family—Jean, John, and their daughters Janet and Debbie—were watching television when they noticed interference on their set. Looking out the window, they observed a strange light located approximately one mile west of their residence. The object hovered at an altitude of 40 to 50 feet above the ground. The family watched the object for approximately half an hour as it revolved very slowly. Eventually, the object appeared to descend or move behind a bush, where it disappeared from their line of sight. The weather conditions at the time were described as very clear, quiet, and windless. Additionally, Jean Widish reported that her husband, John, had witnessed a similar object in June 1976; that previous sighting occurred 300 yards away and featured yellow lights.

**Object:** The object was described as being approximately the size of a television screen. It featured red and blue revolving lights (or flashers). The object moved with a slow, revolving motion and remained visible for a duration of about 30 minutes before disappearing behind vegetation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The report was filed by Constable J.L.P. McMahon of the RCMP Arborg Detachment. Following the sighting, the RCMP conducted a patrol of the area to search for physical evidence; however, this search revealed no tracks or unusual markings on the ground. The RCMP also conducted inquiries with the nearest neighbors, all of which yielded negative results regarding similar sightings or unusual activity.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 简·威迪什 (Jean Widish)、约翰·威迪什 (John Widish)、珍妮特·威迪什 (Janet Widish)、黛比·威迪什 (Debbie Widish)

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年1月31日，晚上约9:30

**地点：** 马尼托巴省罗森堡/阿伯格 (Rosenburg/Arborg)（土地编号 NW19-24-3E）

**目击经过：** 1977年1月31日晚上约9:30，威迪什一家——简、约翰以及他们的女儿珍妮特和黛比——正在看电视时，注意到电视信号出现了干扰。他们向窗外望去，发现距离住所西侧约一英里处有一个奇怪的光源。该物体悬停在离地约40到50英尺的高度。全家人观察了该物体约半小时，它在空中缓慢旋转。最终，该物体似乎下降或移动到了灌木丛后，从他们的视线中消失了。当时的天气状况被描述为非常晴朗、安静且无风。此外，简·威迪什还提到，她的丈夫约翰曾在1976年6月目击过类似的物体；那次目击事件发生在300码外，当时看到的物体带有黄色的灯光。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为大约电视屏幕大小。它带有红色和蓝色的旋转灯（或闪光灯）。该物体以缓慢的旋转方式移动，并持续可见约30分钟，随后消失在植被后方。

**调查/后续：** 该报告由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 阿伯格分局的警官 J.L.P. 麦克马洪 (J.L.P. McMahon) 提交。目击事件发生后，加拿大皇家骑警对该地区进行了巡逻以搜寻物理证据；然而，搜寻结果显示地面上没有任何痕迹或异常标记。警方还向附近的邻居进行了询问，但均未获得有关类似目击事件或异常活动的反馈。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Earl Jeffrey (former pilot), Ruth Totten, Joseph Shaw (reporting witness)

**Date / Time:** January 2, 1977, at 8:20 P.M. Atlantic Standard Time (initial specific sighting); recurring sightings reported by Ruth Totten from late October 1976 through January 1977.

**Location:** Bible Hill and Upper Economy, Colchester County, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** 
On January 2, 1977, at 8:20 P.M. AST, Earl Jeffrey, a former pilot, observed an unidentified object from the Weather Station in Bible Hill. He tracked the object for approximately 10 minutes as it moved at a very slow speed in a westerly direction, positioned at an angle of roughly 20 degrees above the horizon. Mr. Jeffrey explicitly stated that the object was neither a star nor an aircraft.

Separately, Ruth Totten reported a series of recurring sightings beginning in late October 1976. She observed a round, oval-shaped object in the direction of Cape Blomidon on every clear night. According to Ms. Totten, the object typically appeared at dusk and remained visible until before midnight. She noted that the object would initially appear high in the sky and gradually move closer to the ground as the night progressed. She described the object as remaining stationary for periods of time before moving slowly away.

**Object:** 
The object was described as a round or oval-shaped sphere, smaller than the moon but brighter than the surrounding stars. Earl Jeffrey observed it as a pulsating sphere that cycled through red, white, and blue colors. Ruth Totten described the object as having red and green lights that flashed from the top, bottom, or ends of the craft. The object was reported to be silent, leaving no trail or exhaust behind it.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The investigation was initiated after Joseph Shaw, an employee at the Bible Hill Weather Station, received public inquiries and a letter from Ruth Totten regarding her persistent sightings. Mr. Shaw formally reported the matter to the RCMP on January 13, 1977. Cpl. E.E. Best of the Parrsboro Detachment conducted follow-up investigations, which included obtaining a formal statement from Ruth Totten on January 20, 1977. A telex summarizing the reports and the investigation was forwarded by the RCMP on January 19, 1977.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 厄尔·杰弗里（Earl Jeffrey，前飞行员）、露丝·托滕（Ruth Totten）、约瑟夫·肖（Joseph Shaw，报告目击者）

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年1月2日，大西洋标准时间晚上8:20（首次具体目击）；露丝·托滕报告称从1976年10月下旬至1977年1月期间有多次反复目击。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省科尔切斯特县，圣经山（Bible Hill）及上埃科诺米（Upper Economy）。

**目击经过：** 
1977年1月2日大西洋标准时间晚上8:20，前飞行员厄尔·杰弗里在圣经山气象站观测到一个不明物体。他追踪该物体约10分钟，当时物体正以极慢的速度向西移动，位于地平线上方约20度的角度。杰弗里先生明确表示，该物体既不是恒星，也不是飞机。

此外，露丝·托滕报告称，从1976年10月下旬开始，她经历了一系列反复的目击事件。在每个晴朗的夜晚，她都能在布洛米顿角（Cape Blomidon）方向观察到一个圆形或椭圆形的物体。据托滕女士描述，该物体通常在黄昏时分出现，并一直可见到午夜前。她注意到，物体起初出现在高空，随着夜色渐深，会逐渐向地面靠近。她描述该物体有时会保持静止，随后缓慢移开。

**物体描述：** 
该物体被描述为一个圆形或椭圆形的球体，比月亮小，但比周围的星星更亮。厄尔·杰弗里观察到它是一个会发出脉冲光的球体，颜色在红、白、蓝之间循环变换。露丝·托滕则描述该物体顶部、底部或末端闪烁着红光和绿光。据报告，该物体飞行时保持静止，没有留下任何尾迹或废气。

**调查/后续：** 
此次调查始于圣经山气象站员工约瑟夫·肖收到公众咨询以及露丝·托滕关于其持续目击事件的来信之后。肖先生于1977年1月13日正式向加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）报告了此事。帕斯伯勒（Parrsboro）分队的E.E.贝斯特（E.E. Best）下士进行了后续调查，其中包括于1977年1月20日获取了露丝·托滕的正式陈述。加拿大皇家骑警于1977年1月19日转发了一份总结了相关报告及调查情况的电传。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Arisma Gauvin, Mrs. Martial Gauvin, Isabelle Gauvin

**Date / Time:** February 2, 1977, at 9:27 PM AST

**Location:** Morais Office Road, Gloucester County, New Brunswick (facing north)

**Sighting:** On the evening of February 2, 1977, at 9:27 PM AST, three witnesses—Arisma Gauvin, Mrs. Martial Gauvin, and Isabelle Gauvin—were located on Morais Office Road in Gloucester County, New Brunswick. While facing north under a clear sky illuminated by a full moon, the witnesses observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sighting lasted for a duration of approximately two minutes. According to the witnesses, the object traveled in a northerly direction before the lights extinguished and the object disappeared from view.

**Object:** The object was described as a formation of lights rather than a solid, discernible mass. It consisted of three flashing red lights arranged in a triangular pattern, accompanied by one very brilliant, central red light. When viewed from the ground, the witnesses estimated the object’s size to appear roughly one foot in length. The estimated altitude of the object was comparable to that of a standard single-engine aircraft. The movement was described as a steady progression toward the north. The observation concluded when the central bright light went out, followed by the remaining lights turning off, resulting in the object's disappearance.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented by Constable T. Aucoin of the RCMP Caraquet Detachment. The official report notes that the sky conditions were clear with a full moon at the time of the sighting. At the time the report was filed, no further information or additional leads were available regarding the nature of the object.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 阿里斯马·戈万 (Arisma Gauvin)、马歇尔·戈万夫人 (Mrs. Martial Gauvin)、伊莎贝尔·戈万 (Isabelle Gauvin)

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年2月2日，大西洋标准时间晚上9:27

**地点：** 新不伦瑞克省格洛斯特县，莫赖斯办公路 (Morais Office Road)（朝北方向）

**目击经过：** 1977年2月2日晚9:27，三名目击者——阿里斯马·戈万、马歇尔·戈万夫人和伊莎贝尔·戈万——位于新不伦瑞克省格洛斯特县的莫赖斯办公路上。在满月照亮的晴朗夜空下，他们面向北方时观察到了一种不明空中现象。目击过程持续了约两分钟。据目击者称，该物体向北飞行，随后灯光熄灭，物体从视野中消失。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一组灯光，而非一个坚实、可辨认的实体。它由三个呈三角形排列的闪烁红灯组成，中心还伴有一盏非常明亮的红灯。从地面观察，目击者估计该物体看起来约一英尺长。其估计高度与标准的单引擎飞机相当。其运动轨迹被描述为向北的平稳行进。当中心亮光熄灭，随后其余灯光也随之关闭时，观察结束，物体随即消失。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 卡拉凯特分局的 T. 奥昆 (T. Aucoin) 警官记录在案。官方报告指出，目击时天空晴朗，且为满月。在报告提交时，关于该物体性质的更多信息或线索尚不明确。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Bobiwash and four other persons.

**Date / Time:** February 3, 1977, at 10:15 local time.

**Location:** A wooded area near Orell Street, Garson, Ontario.

**Sighting:** On February 3, 1977, at approximately 10:15 local time, Mr. Bobiwash and four other individuals were present in a wooded area near Orell Street in Garson, Ontario. During this time, the group observed two distinct aerial objects. The sighting lasted for a duration of approximately ten minutes. Following the observation, Mr. Bobiwash left the area and returned to his home specifically to contact the local air base to report the incident. No further information regarding the event was documented beyond this initial report.

**Object:** The witnesses reported observing two separate objects simultaneously:
*   **Object 1:** Described as square-shaped and featuring a green light.
*   **Object 2:** Described as round-shaped and featuring a flashing green light.
*   **Movement/Sound:** No specific movement patterns or auditory details were recorded in the provided documentation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The official records note that the weather conditions at the time of the sighting were described as "scattered" with a visibility range of 8 to 10 miles. The documentation consists of reports detailing the witnesses' account and the subsequent action taken by Mr. Bobiwash to notify the air base. No further official investigation notes, sketches, or RCMP interrogation transcripts were provided in the source material.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 博比瓦什（Bobiwash）先生及其他四人。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年2月3日，当地时间10:15。

**地点：** 安大略省加森（Garson）奥雷尔街（Orell Street）附近的林区。

**目击经过：** 1977年2月3日当地时间约10:15，博比瓦什先生和其他四人在安大略省加森市奥雷尔街附近的一片林区。期间，该群体观察到了两个独特的空中物体。目击过程持续了约十分钟。观察结束后，博比瓦什先生离开现场并返回家中，专门联系了当地空军基地报告了这一事件。除这份初步报告外，没有记录关于该事件的更多信息。

**物体描述：** 目击者称同时观察到了两个独立的物体：
*   **物体1：** 描述为方形，带有一盏绿灯。
*   **物体2：** 描述为圆形，带有一盏闪烁的绿灯。
*   **运动/声音：** 提供的文档中未记录具体的运动模式或声音细节。

**调查/后续：** 官方记录指出，目击时的天气状况被描述为“零散云层”，能见度范围为8至10英里。相关文档包括了目击者的陈述报告，以及博比瓦什先生随后通知空军基地的行动记录。原始资料中未提供进一步的官方调查记录、草图或加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）的审讯笔录。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Gary Wayne Robertson, Valerie Robertson, Simon Wright, and Mark Wright, all residing at the same residence in Clinton Creek, YT.

**Sighting:** The event occurred on February 4, 1977, at 8:50 PM Yukon Standard Time. The weather was slightly cloudy with light cover, and visibility was excellent with a visible full moon. The observation was made from the witnesses' residence.

**Object:** The object was described as a singular, extremely bright light that pulsed and changed colors between light blue, red, and green. It was positioned approximately 30 degrees above the horizon in the southern sky. The movement was slow, consistent, and uniform, with no erratic behavior. The object was estimated to be approximately 13 miles away, though there was no indication of its actual size or distance.

**Aftermath:** The sighting lasted for approximately 1.5 hours. The Whitehorse RCMP detachment reported that there were no reports of any aircraft in the immediate area of the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Gary Wayne Robertson、Valerie Robertson、Simon Wright 和 Mark Wright，均居住在育空地区克林顿溪的同一住所。

**目击：** 事件发生于1977年2月4日育空标准时间晚上8:50。当时天气微云，有轻微遮盖，能见度极佳，满月清晰可见。观察地点为见证者的住所。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一个单一且极其明亮的光点，呈现脉冲状，颜色在浅蓝色、红色和绿色之间变换。它位于南部天空，地平线上方约30度处。物体的移动缓慢、持续且均匀，没有任何不规则的动作。据估计该物体距离约13英里，但没有关于其确切大小或距离的迹象。

**后续：** 目击持续了约1.5小时。白马市皇家骑警分局报告称，在目击区域附近没有收到任何飞机活动的报告。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Miles Ward, who was observed by his mother, Mrs. Joyce Ward, who called in the report.

**Sighting:** On February 15, 1977, at 4:00Z, a single light was observed following the witness while he was on his ski-doo. The object traveled northwest toward Lake Manitoba and descended behind trees as if to land.

**Object:** A single light.

**Aftermath:** The report notes that there was no sound made by the UFO. The incident was reported to CFB Portage La Prairie and forwarded to DREO and NDHQ.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Miles Ward，由其母亲 Mrs. Joyce Ward 观察到并报告。

**目击：** 1977年2月15日 4:00Z，目击者在驾驶雪地摩托时，发现一个单体光点跟随他。该物体向西北方向朝曼尼托巴湖移动，并降落在树后，看起来像是要着陆。

**物体：** 一个单体光点。

**后续：** 报告指出该不明飞行物未发出任何声音。此事件已报告给 CFB Portage La Prairie，并转交至 DREO 和 NDHQ。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Eric Brown, Rob Brown (brother), and Glen Morse (step-brother).

**Sighting:** On February 16, 1977, at 23:00Z, the witnesses observed an object from their home in Lavigne, Ontario. The weather was described as very clear with low clouds on the horizon.

**Object:** The object was described as a whitish blue light, flat and long, oriented horizontally. It was moving very fast from south to north, positioned just above the clouds on the horizon. The duration of the sighting was a minute and a half. The object traveled in a straight flight path with no turns and left no contrails.

**Aftermath:** The report was transmitted from 22nd NORAD Headquarters North Bay to the National Defence Operation Centre in Ottawa and the National Research Council.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Eric Brown、Rob Brown（兄弟）和 Glen Morse（继兄弟）。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** An unnamed civilian who requested anonymity.

**Sighting:** On April 18, 1977, at 7:20 p.m. local time, a witness observed an object over Mississippi Lake while looking through the window of a house in front of the lake. The sky was clear with the sun going down and no stars visible. The sighting lasted 3-5 minutes with no movement observed.

**Object:** The object was described as a red, round object with a tail. It was estimated to be 25 times the size of a star at 15 degrees elevation. It had an exhaust in the back that was wider than a jet's exhaust. There was also a small red flashing light to the left of the object. The object made no sound and suddenly disappeared.

**Aftermath:** The report was received by Annie on April 19, 1977, at 10:30.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 一名要求匿名的平民。

**目击：** 1977年4月18日当地时间晚上7点20分，一名目击者在湖前的一所房子里透过窗户观察到了一个物体。当时天空晴朗，太阳正在下山，没有星星可见。目击持续了3到5分钟，物体没有移动。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为一个带有尾巴的红色圆形物体。据估计，它在15度仰角处的大小是星星的25倍。它后部有排气，比喷气式飞机的排气更宽。物体左侧还有一个小的红色闪烁灯。该物体没有发出声音，并突然消失了。

**后续：** 该报告由Annie于1977年4月19日10点30分接收。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Susan Jolin, her mother, her father, and her brother.

**Date / Time:** April 18, 1977, between 0800Z and 0830Z.

**Location:** Edmonton, Alberta (Northwest quadrant of the sky).

**Sighting:** On April 18, 1977, between 0800Z and 0830Z, Susan Jolin and her family (mother, father, and brother) observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon in the northwest quadrant of the sky. The witnesses reported that the object was positioned well above the horizon. Throughout the duration of the sighting, the object exhibited erratic flight patterns, including hovering, dropping rapidly, pausing for a period of time, and subsequently climbing back up to near its original position. The observation was sustained for at least 30 minutes, as the object was still under observation by the family at 0830Z.

**Object:** The object was described as round in shape. In terms of scale, it appeared larger than a star but significantly smaller than the moon. A defining characteristic of the object was its continually changing color, which cycled between green, yellow, and blue. No sound was reported, and only one object was observed in that specific quadrant of the sky.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting occurred under clear sky conditions with some thin cirrus patches present. During the event, a weather forecaster at the unit was alerted and conducted a visual check of the sky; however, the forecaster was unable to spot the object reported by the Jolin family. No further identification of the object was established at the time of the report.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 苏珊·乔林（Susan Jolin）、她的母亲、父亲和兄弟。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年4月18日，0800Z至0830Z之间。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省埃德蒙顿（天空西北象限）。

**目击经过：** 1977年4月18日0800Z至0830Z期间，苏珊·乔林及其家人（母亲、父亲和兄弟）在天空的西北象限观测到一个不明空中现象。目击者报告称，该物体位于地平线以上相当高的高度。在整个目击过程中，该物体表现出不规则的飞行模式，包括悬停、快速下坠、短暂停留，随后又爬升回接近其原始位置的高度。观测持续了至少30分钟，因为直到0830Z时，该家人仍在观测该物体。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形。从比例上看，它看起来比星星大，但明显比月亮小。该物体的一个显著特征是其颜色不断变化，在绿色、黄色和蓝色之间循环。未报告有任何声音，且在该天空象限内仅观测到一个物体。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生时天空晴朗，仅有少量薄卷云。事件期间，该单位的一名天气预报员接到通知并对天空进行了目视检查；然而，预报员未能发现乔林一家所报告的物体。在报告发布时，该物体未得到进一步的确认。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** LT H. Kennedy (also referred to as Capt. H. Kennedy), Capt. G. Whelan, Pte. M. Marchand, Pte. M. Ascot, the crew of a Sea King helicopter, the crew of a Tracker aircraft, and the crew of a light aircraft.

**Date / Time:** April 19, 1977 (initial sighting at dusk); April 21, 1977 (subsequent aircraft observations).

**Location:** CFB Greenwood, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of April 19, 1977, at dusk, personnel stationed at the CFB Greenwood control tower—LT H. Kennedy, Capt. G. Whelan, Pte. M. Marchand, and Pte. M. Ascot—observed two strobe-type lights positioned 1,000 to 1,500 feet above the ground. These lights were located between five and ten miles southeast of the control tower. The lights moved in tandem as a pair, executing rapid maneuvers that covered 500 to 800 feet vertically and one mile horizontally. The sighting lasted for a duration of 15 to 20 minutes. The observers noted that the lights did not fade out, nor did they travel any significant distance from the general area before they disappeared. 

A follow-up report (supplementing operational report OPS 498) indicates that on April 21, 1977, three additional aircraft—a Sea King helicopter, a Tracker aircraft, and a light aircraft—observed a UFO while closing in on Greenwood from the southeast. These aircraft were positioned at distances of 20 miles, 10 miles, and 5 miles from the base, respectively. The UFO was observed moving relative to these aircraft, performing extremely fast, split-second maneuvers.

**Object:** The objects were described as two strobe-type lights. Despite the use of binoculars by the control tower personnel, no distinct physical shape could be determined. The movement was characterized as very rapid, involving sudden vertical and horizontal shifts, as well as "split-second" maneuvers observed by the flight crews on April 21.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The control tower observers reported the sighting to local authorities and radar. Greenwood radar confirmed the presence of one aircraft target located 32 miles east of the base; however, Halifax Terminal reported no IFR (Instrument Flight Rules) traffic in the area at the time of the sighting. The reports from the flight crews and tower personnel were compiled and formally transmitted to the National Research Council in Ottawa for further review.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_11_-_Pages_30.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** H. 肯尼迪中尉（亦被称为 H. 肯尼迪上尉）、G. 惠兰上尉、M. 马尚列兵、M. 阿斯科特列兵，以及一架海王直升机机组人员、一架追踪者飞机机组人员和一架轻型飞机机组人员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年4月19日（黄昏时分首次目击）；1977年4月21日（后续飞行器观测）。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省格林伍德加拿大武装部队基地（CFB Greenwood）。

**目击经过：** 1977年4月19日黄昏，驻扎在格林伍德基地控制塔的人员——H. 肯尼迪中尉、G. 惠兰上尉、M. 马尚列兵和M. 阿斯科特列兵——观察到两个频闪灯状的光点，位于地面上方1000至1500英尺处。这些光点位于控制塔东南方5至10英里处。两个光点成对移动，并进行了快速机动，垂直移动距离达500至800英尺，水平移动距离达1英里。目击持续了15至20分钟。观察者指出，这些光点在消失前并未减弱亮度，也没有离开该区域太远。

一份后续报告（补充了OPS 498行动报告）显示，1977年4月21日，另外三架飞行器——一架海王直升机、一架追踪者飞机和一架轻型飞机——在从东南方向接近格林伍德基地时观测到了一个不明飞行物（UFO）。这些飞行器当时分别距离基地20英里、10英里和5英里。据观测，该不明飞行物相对于这些飞行器进行移动，并执行了极快的、瞬间完成的机动动作。

**物体描述：** 这些物体被描述为两个频闪灯状的光点。尽管控制塔人员使用了双筒望远镜，但仍无法确定其具体的物理形状。其运动特征非常迅速，包括突然的垂直和水平位移，以及4月21日飞行机组人员所观察到的“瞬间”机动。

**调查/后续：** 控制塔观察员向当地有关部门和雷达站报告了此次目击事件。格林伍德雷达确认在基地以东32英里处存在一个飞行目标；然而，哈利法克斯终端区报告称，在目击发生时，该区域没有仪表飞行规则（IFR）下的空中交通。飞行机组人员和塔台人员的报告被汇总并正式提交至渥太华的国家研究委员会进行进一步审查。

**Witnesses:** David Kendrick, Laurie Wiggis, Ron O'Brien, and RCMP officers.

**Sighting:** Witnesses reported seeing lights in the sky, described as red-orange, yellow, and white, which appeared to glide into the water off Shag Harbor. One witness described a row of lights that moved in a gradual arc before descending into the water. Another witness reported seeing a single white light bobbing offshore.

**Object:** Unidentified flying objects described as lights, with some reports of a "row of lights" and others of a single light. The objects were observed gliding into the water.

**Aftermath:** Navy divers searched the area but found nothing. The RCMP and the RCAF were involved in the investigation. A spokesperson for the RCAF stated the department was "very interested" in the matter, noting it might be one of the "extremely rare cases where 'something concrete' may be found." Searches were conducted in water ranging from 20 to 40 feet deep.

**见证者：** David Kendrick, Laurie Wiggis, Ron O'Brien 以及加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 警官。

**目击：** 目击者报告称在沙格港 (Shag Harbor) 附近的天空中看到红橙色、黄色和白色的光，这些光似乎滑入了水中。一位目击者描述了一排光线在滑入水中前呈弧形移动。另一位目击者报告称看到一个白色的光点在离岸不远处漂浮。

**物体：** 不明飞行物，被描述为光点，部分报告称其为“一排光”，另一些报告称其为单一光点。这些物体被观察到滑入水中。

**后续：** 海军潜水员对该区域进行了搜寻，但一无所获。加拿大皇家骑警和加拿大皇家空军 (RCAF) 参与了调查。加拿大皇家空军发言人表示该部门对此事“非常感兴趣”，并指出这可能是“极少数可能发现‘具体实物’的案例之一”。搜寻工作在水深 20 到 40 英尺的区域进行。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Unspecified.

**Sighting:** The document discusses an analysis of an alleged UFO based on six photo prints. The analysis references conversations with the Ottawa and Gimli meteorological offices and Ottawa Hydro.

**Object:** The object is described as an oblate ellipsoid or potentially "cigar" shaped. Photo analysis suggests the object was rolling or yawing nearly 90 degrees. The report notes that the images cannot be associated with a torus shape. The analysis concludes the object was in free flight rather than controlled flight.

**Aftermath:** The report dismisses the possibility of the object being a football or a meteorological balloon. It notes that the object moved into the wind, contrary to the expected path of a balloon, and references specific wind data from 1800Z at 2000 feet and 3000 feet to support the conclusion that the object's movement was inconsistent with wind-driven balloon flight.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 未指明。

**目击：** 该文件讨论了基于六张照片对一个所谓不明飞行物（UFO）的分析。分析参考了与渥太华和吉姆利气象办公室以及渥太华水电局的对话。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为扁椭球体或可能是“雪茄”形。照片分析表明该物体有近90度的滚动或偏航。报告指出图像无法与圆环形状联系起来。分析得出的结论是，该物体处于自由飞行状态，而非受控飞行。

**后续：** 报告排除了该物体是橄榄球或气象气球的可能性。报告指出，该物体逆风移动，这与气球的预期路径相反，并引用了1800Z在2000英尺和3000英尺高度的风力数据，以支持该物体的运动与风力驱动的气球飞行不一致的结论。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Michalak, a 40-year-old industrial mechanic.

**Sighting:** The page reports that a Winnipeg man claimed to have seen a craft at Falcon Lake. He watched it for about 45 minutes and touched it. The object was described as having a red light, moving at an indescribable speed, and having a square door with three levels.

**Object:** The object is described as having a square door with three levels, two sliding sides, and one opening that appeared to be moved by hydraulic power. No welds or rivets could be seen. The witness reported a smell coming from inside the object.

**Aftermath:** Mr. Michalak's chest is burned, and he has experienced headaches and an upset stomach. His family doctor examined him. The Aerial Phenomena Research Organization is comparing his description to other reports. The National Research Council of Canada is the holding agency for this document.

**物体：** 该物体被描述为有一个带有三个层级的方形门，两侧可滑动，一个开口看起来是由液压动力驱动的。没有看到焊接点或铆钉。目击者报告说从物体内部传出一种气味。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Steve Michalak (50) and his son Mark (19).

**Sighting:** Mr. Michalak claims to have encountered two unidentified flying objects north of Falcon Lake on a Saturday. He describes the objects as 35 feet long and eight feet high with a three-foot protrusion on top, resembling stainless steel. He observed one object land and approached it, noting it had no visible welding or bolting. He reported seeing a brilliant violet color and hearing a whirring and hissing sound. He also claimed to hear voices that were distorted by the sound of the craft. The object eventually took off, leaving a bare, circular spot where leaves and grass were removed.

**Object:** Two stainless steel, cigar-shaped objects, approximately 35 feet long and 8 feet high, emitting a brilliant violet light and a whirring/hissing sound.

**Aftermath:** Mr. Michalak suffered chest burns and reported losing 12 pounds in two days, experiencing vomiting and a foul smell coming from inside him. He was treated at Misericordia Hospital. The RCMP at Falcon Lake stated they had no reports of any UFOs. The RCAF radar site at Beausejour and the Department of Transport's radar installation at Winnipeg International Airport reported nothing unusual on their screens.

**Witnesses:** Mr. S. Michalak of 14 Lindsay St., Winnipeg 9, Manitoba.

**Sighting:** On 20 May 1967 at approximately 1700 hours local time, Mr. Michalak observed two objects on the ground at Falcon Lake, Manitoba (49 degrees 41 minutes North latitude, 95 degrees 15 minutes West longitude). The objects were observed for approximately one half hour.

**Object:** The objects were saucer-shaped, approximately 35 to 40 feet in diameter and eight feet high. They were the colour of unpolished steel on the ground, changing to a heated metal colour upon departure. One object departed vertically, then headed south. The other object had an open door with a violet light preventing visibility inside. A whirring sound and indistinguishable voices were heard from within. The object rotated counter-clockwise before departing vertically and heading south.

**Aftermath:** Upon touching the object with his gloved left hand, Mr. Michalak's glove burned. His shirt was burned from exhaust panels on the outer edge of the object. He required medical treatment for burns on his stomach, lost twelve pounds, and was unable to eat. He reported smelling what he described as an electrical fire. The noise from the object increased in pitch to a high whine upon takeoff.

Mr. Michalak had previously been uncooperative regarding the site but agreed to assist after the gravity and implications were explained to him.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Stephen Michalak 先生、Thompson 先生 (APRO)，以及包括军方和政府官员在内的地面调查小组。

**目击：** 该文件涉及对 Falcon Lake 一处疑似物体着陆点的调查，此前 Michalak 先生曾有一次初步接触。加拿大国防部发现从该地点采集的样本具有相当高的放射性。

**物体：** 一个据称在现场着陆的未识别物体。

**后续：** 在 Michalak 先生同意带路后，一个地面小组于 1967 年 7 月 28 日对该地点进行了调查。小组成员包括来自加拿大皇家空军 (RCAF)、加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 以及卫生福利部的代表。Michalak 先生此前对该地点一直不予配合，但在向他解释了事件的严重性和影响后，他同意提供协助。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Michalak and Mr. Thompson.

**Sighting:** The page describes a follow-up investigation at a site near Falcon Lake. Mr. Michalak led a party to the location on 28 July. The site was found to be within 50 yards of an area searched on 1 June 1967, but was previously obscured by heavy bush.

**Object:** The site features a 15-foot diameter circle on a rock surface where moss and earth appear to have been cleared by high-velocity air. A small area of approximately 4 inches in diameter within the circle showed indications of radioactivity and was identified as having a Radium source.

**Aftermath:** DND personnel, including Cpl W. Reed and Cpl D. Shephard, utilized radiation detection instruments (Radiac Meter 5016-Gamma and CDV 700-Beta/Gamma). Four photographs were taken at the site to document the circle, the radioactive area, and the specific spot where Mr. Michalak allegedly made contact with the object's surface. A search for burned shirt particles at the contact point yielded no results.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Mr. Michalak 和 Mr. Thompson。

**目击：** 该页面描述了对猎鹰湖（Falcon Lake）附近地点的后续调查。Mr. Michalak 于 7 月 28 日带领调查组前往该地点。该地点位于 1967 年 6 月 1 日搜索区域的 50 码范围内，但此前因茂密的灌木丛而未被发现。

**物体：** 该地点在岩石表面有一个直径约 15 英尺的圆圈，圆圈内的苔藓和泥土似乎被高速气流清除。圆圈内有一个直径约 4 英寸的小区域显示出放射性迹象，经分析确认为镭源。

**后续：** 包括 Cpl W. Reed 和 Cpl D. Shephard 在内的国防部（DND）人员使用了辐射探测仪器（Radiac Meter 5016-Gamma 和 CDV 700-Beta/Gamma）。现场拍摄了四张照片，记录了圆圈、放射性区域以及 Mr. Michalak 声称与物体表面接触的具体位置。调查组对接触点的烧毁衬衫碎片进行了仔细检查，但未发现任何残留物。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Michalak.

**Sighting:** The page discusses an alleged landing site of an object approximately 35-40 feet in diameter. The report notes that the object would have had to rise directly upwards before proceeding in a southwesterly direction.

**Object:** The object is described as having a diameter of 35-40 feet. The report questions how an object of this size could have landed and ascended without making contact with or damaging the surrounding trees.

**Aftermath:** An intensive radiac check was conducted on the surfaces surrounding the site, but no other sources of radioactivity were located. Trees within the area were examined for heat burns or disturbances with no results. The report notes that Mr. Michalak consumes alcoholic beverages and was taken to a bar where he had consumed five beers the night prior to his initial encounter.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Mr. Michalak。

**目击：** 该页面讨论了一个直径约为35-40英尺的物体疑似着陆点。报告指出，该物体在离开时必须垂直上升，然后向西南方向移动。

**物体：** 该物体被描述为直径35-40英尺。报告质疑如此大小的物体如何在不接触或损坏周围树木的情况下着陆和升空。

**后续：** 对着陆点周围的表面进行了密集的辐射检查，但未发现其他放射源。对该区域内的树木进行了热灼伤或干扰检查，结果均为阴性。报告指出，Mr. Michalak 有饮酒习惯，并被带到他在5月20日初次遭遇事件前一晚饮用过五瓶啤酒的酒吧。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Michalak and Mr. Stuart Hunt.

**Sighting:** The page discusses an investigation into an incident involving Mr. Michalak, noting his behavior and alcohol consumption. It references an RCMP report regarding the removal of evidence from a site and the presence of a circle.

**Object:** The text mentions a "tape (metal)" that was reported to show signs of radioactivity, though it was left 100 feet from the circle. It is suggested this may have been contaminated through contact with samples.

**Aftermath:** Mr. Stuart Hunt examined the site and advised that samples he took showed no signs of radiation on his instrument. Mr. Hunt contacted W/C Robertson at CFHQ to submit his findings, expressing a personal thought that the source of radiation may have been planted, though he lacked firm convictions.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Mr. Michalak 和 Mr. Stuart Hunt。

**目击：** 该页讨论了对涉及 Mr. Michalak 的事件的调查，提到了他的行为和饮酒情况。文中引用了一份关于从现场移除证据以及现场存在一个圆圈的 RCMP 报告。

**物体：** 文中提到了一卷“磁带（金属）”，据报道显示有放射性迹象，尽管它被留在距离圆圈 100 英尺的地方。文中指出这可能是通过与样本接触而受到污染的。

**后续：** Mr. Stuart Hunt 检查了现场，并告知他采集的样本在他的仪器上没有显示出辐射迹象。Mr. Hunt 联系了 CFHQ 的 W/C Robertson 以提交他的调查结果，并表达了他个人的想法，即辐射源可能是被放置在那里的，尽管他并没有坚定的信念来支持这一说法。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** S/L P. Bissky (R.C.A.F.) is noted as having submitted a report on the sighting.

**Sighting:** The document refers to an alleged landing site of an unidentified flying object near Falcon Lake, Manitoba, reported on July 24, 1967.

**Object:** The page mentions soil samples, a burnt shirt, and steel tape collected from the site. Gamma-ray spectral analysis of these samples revealed activity levels of up to approximately 0.5 uCi of Ra-226 or its equivalent.

**Aftermath:** The Physics Section of the National Research Council monitored the samples on behalf of the R.C.M.P. Crime Detection Laboratory. Mr. S.E. Hunt traveled to Winnipeg on July 26, 1967, to meet with Mr. D. Thompson of the Manitoba Health Department to coordinate an investigation between the R.C.M.P., D.N.D., and health representatives, citing a lack of cooperation by the principals and initial difficulty in establishing the exact location of the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 报告中提到了加拿大皇家空军 (R.C.A.F.) 的 P. Bissky 中队长提交了相关报告。

**目击：** 该文件涉及 1967 年 7 月 24 日在曼尼托巴省猎鹰湖 (Falcon Lake) 附近发生的所谓不明飞行物着陆事件。

**物体：** 文件提到了从现场收集的土壤样本、一件烧焦的衬衫和钢卷尺。对这三个样本进行的伽马射线光谱分析显示，其放射性水平高达约 0.5 uCi 的镭-226 或其等效物。

**后续：** 加拿大国家研究委员会物理部门代表皇家骑警 (R.C.M.P.) 犯罪检测实验室对样本进行了监测。S.E. Hunt 先生于 1967 年 7 月 26 日飞往温尼伯，与曼尼托巴省卫生部的 D. Thompson 先生会面，旨在协调皇家骑警、国防部 (D.N.D.) 和卫生部门代表之间的调查工作，原因是当事人缺乏配合，且最初难以确定目击事件的确切地点。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Stephan Michalak, Mr. R. Kemp (Conservation Officer), S/L Bissky (RCAF), Cpl. Davis (RCMP), and Messrs. Thompson and Hunt (Manitoba Department of Health).

**Sighting:** The page details a field investigation into a UFO incident involving Mr. Stephan Michalak. Investigators visited Mr. Michalak at his residence at 314 Lindsay Street to discuss the site of the U.F.O. landing. Mr. Michalak was initially unwilling to take investigators to the site due to potential loss of work income.

**Object:** The report mentions samples of rock, soil, and vegetation collected from the U.F.O. site, as well as a burnt shirt and undershirt belonging to Mr. Michalak. Investigators noted a scorched grid pattern on his undershirt and photographs of burns on his abdomen. Radiation checks were performed on the samples using a scintillation counter; while the plastic bags containing soil and remnants showed radiation fields, the basement itself showed no evidence of loose contamination.

**Aftermath:** Investigators met with Mr. R. Kemp to visit a radium burial site at East Braintree. Mr. Michalak allowed investigators to take parts of the samples for further analysis. The report notes that Mr. Michalak handled contaminated soil with his bare hands and had difficulty washing them.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 斯蒂芬·米哈拉克 (Stephan Michalak)、R. 肯普先生 (Mr. R. Kemp，保护官员)、比斯基中队长 (S/L Bissky，加拿大皇家空军)、戴维斯下士 (Cpl. Davis，加拿大皇家骑警)，以及曼尼托巴省卫生部的汤普森先生 (Mr. Thompson) 和亨特先生 (Mr. Hunt)。

**目击：** 该页面详细记录了对斯蒂芬·米哈拉克先生涉及的一起不明飞行物事件的实地调查。调查人员前往米哈拉克位于林赛街 314 号的住所，讨论不明飞行物的着陆地点。米哈拉克先生起初因担心误工损失而不愿带调查人员前往现场。

**物体：** 报告提到了从不明飞行物现场收集的岩石、土壤和植被样本，以及米哈拉克先生的一件烧焦的衬衫和内衣。调查人员记录了其内衣上的烧焦网格图案，并拍摄了其腹部烧伤的照片。调查人员使用闪烁计数器对样本进行了辐射检查；虽然装有土壤和残留物的塑料袋显示出辐射场，但地下室本身没有发现松散污染的迹象。

**后续：** 调查人员会见了 R. 肯普先生，参观了东布伦特里的镭掩埋场。米哈拉克先生允许调查人员取走部分样本进行进一步分析。报告指出，米哈拉克先生曾徒手接触受污染的土壤，并难以清洗双手。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** S/L Bissky, F/O Smith, Cpls. Shepard and Davis (R.C.A.F.), Constable Zacharias (R.C.M.P.), Mr. Michalak, Mr. B. Thompson, and Mr. E. Campbell.

**Sighting:** The page describes an expedition to a UFO landing site at Falcon Lake Provincial Park on July 27, 1967. The site was identified using photographs taken by Life Magazine and confirmed by Mr. B. Thompson.

**Object:** The site contained a circular area of vegetation. A survey using a Tracerlab SU14 and a Civil Defence CDV 700 survey meter revealed a small area of contamination on a rock, specifically a smear measuring 0.5 x 8.0 inches, along with contaminated lichen and vegetation.

**Aftermath:** Samples of the contaminated rock and lichen were collected for analysis. On August 1, 1967, samples from the site and Mr. Michalak's residence were checked under U.V. light at the Environmental Sanitation Laboratory. The site samples indicated contamination with Radium luminous paint, while the house samples did not. Further inquiries were made at the Inland Cement Company to determine if industrial radium sources were involved, but the company denied using such sources.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** S/L Bissky, F/O Smith, Cpls. Shepard 和 Davis (R.C.A.F.), Constable Zacharias (R.C.M.P.), Mr. Michalak, Mr. B. Thompson 以及 Mr. E. Campbell。

**目击：** 该页面描述了1967年7月27日对猎鹰湖省立公园（Falcon Lake Provincial Park）一处不明飞行物着陆点的考察。该地点是通过《生活》杂志拍摄的照片识别出来的，并由 Mr. B. Thompson 确认。

**物体：** 该地点包含一个圆形的植被区域。使用 Tracerlab SU14 和民防 CDV 700 测量仪进行的调查显示，岩石上有一小块区域受到污染，具体表现为岩石裂缝一侧 0.5 x 8.0 英寸的污迹，以及受污染的地衣和植被。

**后续：** 采集了受污染的岩石和地衣样本进行分析。1967年8月1日，在 Norquay 大楼的环境卫生实验室使用紫外线检查了来自该地点和 Mr. Michalak 住所的样本。来自该地点的样本显示出镭发光涂料污染的迹象，而来自住所的样本则没有。随后对内陆水泥公司（Inland Cement Company）进行了调查，以确定是否涉及工业镭源，但该公司否认使用过此类放射源。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. B. Thompson, Mr. Hart, Mr. George Dyck, S/b Bissky, and Michalak.

**Sighting:** The page details follow-up investigations regarding soil samples allegedly collected from the Falcon Lake U.F.O. site. On August 3, 1967, investigators visited Mr. B. Thompson at his residence. Thompson provided a soil sample, which showed a 1.4 mev peak during a contamination check. Thompson, a representative for an outdoor advertising firm and member of APRO, appeared to be a "sloppy worker" and could not provide names of other investigating officers. He claimed a technician at the Winnipeg General Hospital had analyzed the samples without authorization.

**Object:** The document references soil samples purportedly from a "U.F.O. site" and mentions "Interstellar Vehicles" in relation to Mr. Hart, who claimed to be developing a device to detect them.

**Aftermath:** A separate visit was made to Hart Electronics, where no evidence of contamination was found in Mr. Hart's car or store. Finally, investigators contacted Mr. George Dyck at the Winnipeg General Hospital. Dyck confirmed he had the samples and intended to perform a second analysis to determine the isotope by its rate of decay.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** B. Thompson 先生、Hart 先生、George Dyck 先生、S/b Bissky 以及 Michalak。

**目击：** 该页面详细记录了对据称从猎鹰湖（Falcon Lake）U.F.O. 现场采集的土壤样本的后续调查。1967 年 8 月 3 日，调查人员走访了 B. Thompson 先生的住所。Thompson 提供了一份土壤样本，污染检查显示其具有 1.4 mev 的峰值。Thompson 是一家户外广告公司的代表，也是 APRO 的成员，他被描述为“工作马虎”，无法提供其他调查人员的姓名。他声称温尼伯总医院的一名技术人员在未经授权的情况下分析了这些样本。

**物体：** 文件提到了据称来自“U.F.O. 现场”的土壤样本，并提到了与 Hart 先生有关的“星际飞行器”，Hart 先生声称正在开发一种用于探测此类飞行器的装置。

**后续：** 调查人员随后走访了 Hart Electronics，在 Hart 先生的车内和店内均未发现污染迹象。最后，调查人员联系了温尼伯总医院的 George Dyck 先生。Dyck 证实他持有这些样本，并打算进行第二次分析，通过衰变率来确定同位素。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Michalak.

**Sighting:** The document references an alleged U.F.O. landing site and a subject named Michalak who sustained burns. Dr. F. Helmuth examined these burns and suggested they were thermal in nature. Michalak had been sent to Pinawa, Manitoba.

**Object:** An alleged U.F.O. landing site.

**Aftermath:** Dr. R.J. Walton provided samples for analysis. On August 1967, at 0930 hrs, a telephone call was made to the Manager of Lab Products Limited, who confirmed they did not use radium luminous or luminous paints for their products. The undersigned concludes that radioactive contamination of rock and lichens was found at the landing site, though the origin remains undetermined. Radiation levels were deemed not high enough to create a hazard to the general public.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Michalak。

**目击：** 文件提及一起所谓的U.F.O.着陆点事件，以及一名叫Michalak的当事人，他身上有烧伤痕迹。F. Helmuth医生检查了这些烧伤，认为它们属于热灼伤。Michalak曾被送往曼尼托巴省的皮纳瓦（Pinawa）。

**物体：** 所谓的U.F.O.着陆点。

**后续：** R.J. Walton医生提供了样本进行分析。1967年8月0930时，有人致电Lab Products Limited的经理，对方确认其产品未使用镭发光材料或发光涂料。签署人总结称，在着陆点发现岩石和地衣存在放射性污染，但污染源尚未确定。辐射水平被认为不足以对公众造成危害。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Stephen Michalak.

**Sighting:** On May 21, 1967, near Falcon Lake, Manitoba, the witness claims he was subjected to a blast of hot compressed air from a U.F.O. that landed near him.

**Object:** A U.F.O. that landed in the scrub bushes.

**Aftermath:** The witness suffered first-degree burns to his upper abdominal wall. He was treated at Misericordia Hospital. Symptoms included a band-like headache, moist forehead, depression, dazed state, and apathy. His undershirt showed burn holes with charred or singed edges. Subsequent medical examinations at Winnipeg General Hospital checked for radioactivity, but none was found. The patient lost 13 pounds, suffered from anorexia and nausea, and experienced a rash (urticaria) on June 1st and again on September 15th, the latter accompanied by weakness, dizziness, and throat tightness.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Stephen Michalak。

**目击：** 1967年5月21日，在曼尼托巴省猎鹰湖（Falcon Lake）附近，目击者声称他受到了一架降落在灌木丛中的不明飞行物（U.F.O.）喷出的热压缩空气冲击。

**物体：** 一架降落在灌木丛中的不明飞行物。

**后续：** 目击者上腹部受到一级烧伤，并在慈悲医院（Misericordia Hospital）接受治疗。症状包括带状头痛、前额潮湿、抑郁、神志恍惚和冷漠。他所穿的内衣上有带有焦黑或烧焦边缘的破洞。温尼伯总医院（Winnipeg General Hospital）随后的医学检查排除了放射性污染。患者体重减轻了13磅，出现厌食和恶心症状，并分别在6月1日和9月15日出现皮疹（荨麻疹），后者伴有虚弱、头晕和喉咙紧缩感。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary:

**Object:** An alien craft.

**Aftermath:** The author of the foreword notes that they were initially skeptical of UFOs but changed their mind after helping translate Mr. Michalak's manuscript. The text mentions that the Canadian Press carried a report on November 6, 1967, confirming the government had information regarding the investigation of Mr. Michalak's claims. CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_17_-_Pages_48.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** Stephen Michalak。

**目击：** 该页面提到了1967年5月20日在猎鹰湖（Falcon Lake）发生的一起外星飞行器着陆事件。

**物体：** 外星飞行器。

**后续：** 前言作者指出，他们最初对外星生命持怀疑态度，但在协助翻译Michalak先生的手稿后改变了看法。文中提到加拿大新闻社于1967年11月6日报道称，政府掌握了有关调查Michalak先生所称事件的信息。封面注释提到，当作者触摸该飞行器时，来自UFO的热量烧毁了他的帽子和衬衫，并熔化了他的手套。

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Four persons.

**Sighting:** The page describes the conclusion of a report regarding four observations made over an area of approximately seventy-five miles. The witness mentioned in this specific excerpt was driving his vehicle at the time of the sighting. He observed a light that remained stationary for about fifteen seconds before going out. He did not see the object itself, nor did he hear any explosion.

**Object:** An object of unknown origin, described as a light.

**Aftermath:** The reporting officer, Cpl. K.J. [unclear], notes that the four statements provided by the witnesses are identical in some respects, despite the witnesses being unrelated to one another. The writer concludes that the four individuals did observe an object of unknown origin.
CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** The witness and their sister.

**Sighting:** On February 2, 1969, at approximately 5:20 PM, the witness observed an object in the sky for about 15 minutes. The object moved very fast, traveling from the West across to the South before disappearing below the tree line. The witnesses went outside to get a closer look, noting that the object appeared to have heat waves around it.

**Object:** The object was initially white, oval-shaped, and higher in the center, with one bright light and a black thing on the end. Later, a second object appeared above the tree line, which was black, stretched out in length, and turned a pinkish-orange from one end to the other before disappearing.

CA-FOIA-Canada_-_FOIA_Part_27_-_Pages_78.report_summary_zh:
**见证者：** 目击者及其姐妹。

**目击：** 1969年2月2日下午5:20左右，目击者观察到一个空中物体约15分钟。该物体移动速度极快，从西向南移动，随后消失在树线下方。目击者走到室外观察，注意到物体周围似乎有热浪。

**物体：** 该物体最初呈白色，椭圆形，中间较高，带有一个明亮的灯光，末端有一个黑色物体。随后，在树线上方出现了第二个物体，呈黑色，长度被拉长，并从一端到另一端变为粉橙色，随后消失。

**后续：** 目击者对所见景象感到困惑。第二个物体似乎通过向外推移而从大气层中消失。
