**Sighting:** On the evening of September 25, 1976, at 2130Z, three witnesses—John Dunlop, Mr. Bill Omnet, and Mr. Teri Case—observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while located at a residence in Sheguiandah on Manitoulin Island. The sighting occurred under clear weather conditions, with only a few clouds present in the sky. The witnesses observed the object positioned to the west of the house. The observation lasted for a total duration of approximately 45 minutes.

**Object:** The object was described as a single, round, balloon-shaped entity. It was noted for being transparent in appearance. The altitude of the object remained unknown throughout the duration of the sighting. No sounds or specific movements were reported beyond its presence in the western sky.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation provided consists of two pages (165 and 166) detailing the same event. Both records confirm the consistent accounts of the three witnesses regarding the time, location, weather conditions, and the physical description of the object. No further official investigation notes, RCMP reports, or sketches were included in the provided file pages beyond these summary accounts.
CA-FOIA-Part_10-p165-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 约翰·邓洛普 (John Dunlop)、比尔·奥姆内特先生 (Mr. Bill Omnet)、泰瑞·凯斯先生 (Mr. Teri Case)

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年9月25日，21:30Z

**地点：** 马尼图林岛谢圭安达 (Sheguiandah, Manitoulin Island)（位于目击者住所西侧）

**目击经过：** 1976年9月25日晚21:30Z，三名目击者——约翰·邓洛普、比尔·奥姆内特先生和泰瑞·凯斯先生，在马尼图林岛谢圭安达的一处住所内观察到一种不明空中现象。目击发生时天气晴朗，天空中仅有少量云层。目击者观察到该物体位于房屋西侧。整个观测过程持续了约45分钟。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个单一的、圆形的、气球状实体。据记录，其外观呈透明状。在整个目击过程中，该物体的高度始终未知。除了它在西侧天空的存在外，未报告有任何声音或特定的移动轨迹。

**调查/后续：** 所提供的文档包含两页（第165页和166页），详细记录了同一事件。两份记录均证实了三名目击者在时间、地点、天气状况以及物体物理描述方面的一致陈述。除这些摘要记录外，所提供的档案页面中未包含进一步的官方调查记录、加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 报告或草图。

CA-FOIA-Part_10-p207-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Gordon Victor Alexander Beattie, Johan Blanche Marie Beattie, Daniel Victor Steele, Jennifer Lynn Steele, Mrs. Christina Victor Beattie (parent/interviewer).

**Date / Time:** October 23, 1976, at 7:45 p.m.; additional sighting by Gordon Beattie on October 25, 1976, at 5:15 a.m.

**Location:** 7 Braeburn Road, Spryfield, Nova Scotia.

**Sighting:** On October 23, 1976, at 7:45 p.m., four children—Gordon Beattie, Johan Beattie, Daniel Steele, and Jennifer Steele—were playing outside their residence under clear sky conditions when they observed an unidentified object. The children reported that the object traveled in a northerly direction before disappearing from view. While the children were initially unafraid during the encounter, their parents noted they exhibited fear afterward. Gordon Beattie, noted for his keen interest in and familiarity with military aircraft operating out of CFB Shearwater, was adamant that the object was not a conventional airplane. A secondary, separate sighting was reported by Gordon Beattie on October 25, 1976, at 5:15 a.m.

**Object:** The primary object observed on October 23 was described as a large, saucer-shaped craft. It featured a bright white light, likened to a car headlight, and a bright red light at the rear that possibly resembled flames. The object made no sound. Sketches provided by the witnesses depict the object as a dark, elongated shape with three thin protrusions or appendages extending from its sides and a plume or exhaust-like feature at its base. A separate sketch by Gordon Beattie regarding the October 25 sighting depicts an oval or eye-shaped object with a central core, a textured outer ring, and horizontal lines indicating light emission.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** On October 25, 1976, the RCMP Halifax Detachment conducted an investigation, patrolling to 18 Braeburn Road to interview the witnesses and Mrs. Christina Victor Beattie. To rule out conventional aircraft, Mrs. Beattie contacted Halifax International Airport; officials confirmed only two aircraft were in the area at the time (one flying from CFB Greenwood to Shearwater, and one from Bermuda to Halifax). The parents also reviewed local newspapers from the preceding days to ensure the children had not been influenced by external UFO reports. The RCMP concluded that no further action was required and forwarded the report (Message #64) to the National Research Council (NRC) Meteor Center in Ottawa. The case file (RG 77, Vol. 308) includes official RCMP reports, witness testimony, and hand-drawn sketches by Gordon and Johan Beattie.
CA-FOIA-Part_10-p207-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 戈登·维克多·亚历山大·比蒂 (Gordon Victor Alexander Beattie)、约翰·布兰奇·玛丽·比蒂 (Johan Blanche Marie Beattie)、丹尼尔·维克多·斯蒂尔 (Daniel Victor Steele)、詹妮弗·琳恩·斯蒂尔 (Jennifer Lynn Steele)、克里斯蒂娜·维克多·比蒂夫人 (Mrs. Christina Victor Beattie，家长/访谈者)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年10月23日晚上7:45；戈登·比蒂于1976年10月25日凌晨5:15另有一次目击。

**地点：** 新斯科舍省斯普赖菲尔德，布雷本路7号 (7 Braeburn Road, Spryfield, Nova Scotia)。

**目击经过：** 1976年10月23日晚上7:45，四名儿童——戈登·比蒂、约翰·比蒂、丹尼尔·斯蒂尔和詹妮弗·斯蒂尔——在住所外玩耍时，在晴朗的天空下观察到一个不明物体。孩子们报告称，该物体向北飞行，随后消失在视野中。虽然孩子们在目击过程中最初并不害怕，但家长们注意到他们事后表现出了恐惧。戈登·比蒂因对希尔沃特加拿大武装部队基地 (CFB Shearwater) 起降的军用飞机有浓厚兴趣且非常熟悉，他坚称该物体绝非传统飞机。1976年10月25日凌晨5:15，戈登·比蒂又报告了另一次独立的目击事件。

**物体描述：** 10月23日观察到的主要物体被描述为一艘巨大的碟形飞行器。它带有一盏明亮的白灯（类似于汽车前灯）和一盏位于后部的红灯，看起来可能像火焰。该物体没有发出任何声音。目击者提供的草图将该物体描绘为一个深色的长形物体，其侧面伸出三个细长的突起或附属物，底部有一个类似羽流或尾气的特征。戈登·比蒂关于10月25日目击事件的另一张草图则描绘了一个椭圆形或眼状的物体，具有一个核心、一个有纹理的外环，以及表示光线发射的水平线。

**调查/后续：** 1976年10月25日，加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 哈利法克斯分队进行了调查，巡逻至布雷本路18号，对目击者和克里斯蒂娜·维克多·比蒂夫人进行了访谈。为了排除常规飞行器的可能性，比蒂夫人联系了哈利法克斯国际机场；官方确认当时该地区仅有两架飞机（一架从格林伍德基地飞往希尔沃特基地，另一架从百慕大飞往哈利法克斯）。家长们还查阅了前几天的当地报纸，以确保孩子们没有受到外界不明飞行物报道的影响。加拿大皇家骑警认为无需采取进一步行动，并将报告（第64号信息）转发给了位于渥太华的国家研究委员会 (NRC) 流星中心。该案卷（RG 77, Vol. 308）包含了加拿大皇家骑警的官方报告、证人证词以及戈登·比蒂和约翰·比蒂的手绘草图。

CA-FOIA-Part_10-p224-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Stan Krukowski, Stanley Krukowski

**Date / Time:** November 2, 1976, between approximately 6:00 PM and 6:30 PM

**Location:** Traveling south from Provost, Alberta, toward Kirriemuir, Alberta; sightings occurred along the highway near the Sampson farm, the Mouly farm, Harry Delef’s farm, and the Grassy Lake area.

**Sighting:** On the evening of November 2, 1976, Mrs. Stan Krukowski and her husband, Stanley, observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while driving south from Provost toward their residence. The witnesses reported that the object was visible for a twenty-mile stretch of highway. Initially, the object was observed in the southwest sky, appearing as a large, round, red ball hovering over the Sampson farm. 

As the witnesses continued their journey, they noted that the object periodically shifted its appearance, transitioning into a bright white fluorescent light. Upon arriving at the Sampson farm, the witnesses observed the light move south toward the Kirriemuir area. The couple then turned west onto Highway No. 12, where their view of the object was intermittently obstructed by hills. As they passed the Mouly farm, the light was observed proceeding in a southwest direction, trending toward the west. By the time the witnesses reached Harry Delef’s farm, the light had shifted its trajectory to travel due south. The object remained visible for approximately thirty minutes before finally disappearing into the hills surrounding the Grassy Lake area. The witnesses explicitly stated their belief that the object was not a star or a planet.

**Object:** The object was described as a large, round entity. Its color shifted between a bright white light (described as fluorescent) and a dark red. At one point, the witnesses noted that it resembled a large orange in appearance, maintaining that apparent size even as it neared the horizon. The object was described as being suspended in the sky and displayed controlled movement, hovering and then traveling in various directions (south, southwest, and west) before disappearing. No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Official inquiries were conducted following the sighting. Captain Obyrne of C.F.S. Alsask was contacted regarding the event, and the Calgary Terminal Tower was also consulted. Both entities reported that there was no radar tracking or any other trace of the object recorded during the time of the sighting.
CA-FOIA-Part_10-p224-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 斯坦·克鲁科夫斯基夫人（Mrs. Stan Krukowski）、斯坦利·克鲁科夫斯基（Stanley Krukowski）

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年11月2日，大约下午6:00至6:30之间

**地点：** 从艾伯塔省普罗沃斯特（Provost）向南行驶，前往艾伯塔省基里缪尔（Kirriemuir）；目击事件发生在沿途公路，靠近桑普森（Sampson）农场、穆利（Mouly）农场、哈里·德莱夫（Harry Delef）农场以及草湖（Grassy Lake）地区。

**目击经过：** 1976年11月2日傍晚，斯坦·克鲁科夫斯基夫人和她的丈夫斯坦利在从普罗沃斯特驱车回家的途中，观察到一种不明空中现象。目击者称，该物体在长达20英里的公路上空均可见。起初，该物体出现在西南方的天空中，看起来像是一个悬浮在桑普森农场上空的巨大红色圆球。

随着目击者继续前行，他们注意到该物体的外观发生了周期性变化，转变为一种明亮的白色荧光。当到达桑普森农场时，目击者观察到光点向南移动，朝基里缪尔地区飞去。随后，夫妇俩向西转入12号公路，由于丘陵遮挡，他们对物体的视线时断时续。当他们经过穆利农场时，观察到光点正向西南方向移动，并逐渐向西偏移。当目击者到达哈里·德莱夫的农场时，光点的轨迹已转为正南方向。该物体持续可见约三十分钟，最终消失在草湖地区周围的丘陵中。目击者明确表示，他们坚信该物体绝非恒星或行星。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个巨大的圆形实体。其颜色在明亮的白光（被描述为荧光）和深红色之间变换。目击者曾指出，它看起来像一个巨大的橙子，即使在接近地平线时，其表观大小也保持不变。该物体被描述为悬浮在空中，并表现出受控的运动，先是悬停，随后向不同方向（南、西南和西）移动，最后消失。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生后，相关部门进行了官方调查。调查人员就此事联系了阿尔萨斯加拿大武装部队基地（C.F.S. Alsask）的奥伯恩（Obyrne）上尉，并咨询了卡尔加里终端塔台（Calgary Terminal Tower）。双方均报告称，在目击事件发生期间，雷达并未追踪到该物体，也没有记录到任何其他痕迹。

CA-FOIA-Part_10-p228-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Raymond Bedard (also recorded as Berard), Laurent Val, and Maurice Morin (a neighbour).

**Date / Time:** November 9, 1976, at 2215Z.

**Location:** Brochu River, Quebec.

**Sighting:** On the night of November 9, 1976, at 2215Z, three witnesses—Raymond Bedard (or Berard), Laurent Val, and their neighbour, Maurice Morin—observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon. The sighting lasted for a duration of between 45 minutes and one hour. Throughout the observation, the object maintained a position approximately 20 degrees above the horizon, traveling on a trajectory from the west toward the north-east. The witnesses reported that the object performed distinct vertical maneuvers, appearing to descend and then ascend. Specifically, the object descended at a 90-degree angle during one maneuver and later performed a second descent at a 30-degree angle.

**Object:** The object was described as oval-shaped. Its coloration consisted of a yellow center flanked by red sides. The object exhibited a blinking light pattern that varied in intensity throughout the duration of the sighting. No specific sound was noted in the reports, and the object’s movement was characterized by its unusual angular descents and ascents.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The primary witness (Raymond Bedard/Berard) initiated four separate phone reports regarding the event. The sequence of these reports reflects the witness's evolving interpretation of the sighting:
*   **First report:** An initial notification of the object.
*   **Second report:** A suggestion that the object might be a helicopter.
*   **Third report:** A formal identification of the object as a UFO.
*   **Fourth report:** A follow-up observation noting that a conventional plane was sighted in the same general location approximately 15 to 20 minutes after the UFO had disappeared from view. 

The documentation indicates that these reports were processed as part of the official record for the Brochu River sighting, though no further meteorological or radar data was appended to these specific pages.
CA-FOIA-Part_10-p228-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 雷蒙德·贝达德（Raymond Bedard，亦记录为 Berard）、劳伦特·瓦尔（Laurent Val）以及莫里斯·莫林（Maurice Morin，邻居）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年11月9日，22:15Z（祖鲁时间）。

**地点：** 魁北克省，布罗舒河（Brochu River）。

**目击经过：** 1976年11月9日晚22:15Z，三名目击者——雷蒙德·贝达德（或贝拉德）、劳伦特·瓦尔及其邻居莫里斯·莫林——观察到一种不明空中现象。目击过程持续了45分钟至1小时。在整个观察过程中，该物体始终保持在地平线上方约20度的位置，沿从西向东北的轨迹移动。目击者报告称，该物体进行了明显的垂直机动，表现为下降后又上升。具体而言，该物体在一次机动中以90度角垂直下降，随后又以30度角进行了第二次下降。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为椭圆形。其颜色由黄色的中心和红色的两侧组成。物体呈现出闪烁的灯光模式，且在目击期间光强有所变化。报告中未提及任何特定声音，该物体的移动特征是其不寻常的直角下降和上升。

**调查/后续：** 主要目击者（雷蒙德·贝达德/贝拉德）针对此次事件发起了四次单独的电话报告。这些报告的顺序反映了目击者对此次目击事件的解读演变：
*   **第一次报告：** 对该物体的初步通报。
*   **第二次报告：** 提出该物体可能是直升机的猜测。
*   **第三次报告：** 正式将该物体定性为不明飞行物（UFO）。
*   **第四次报告：** 后续观察记录显示，在不明飞行物消失约15至20分钟后，在同一大致区域观测到了一架常规飞机。

相关文件显示，这些报告已被处理并归入布罗舒河目击事件的官方记录中，但这些特定页面中并未附带进一步的气象或雷达数据。

CA-FOIA-Part_10-p244-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cpl Seath Jr (Photo Tech), Cpl(W) Seath VD (Adm Clk), Cpl(W) Hansen SJ (Adm Clk)

**Date / Time:** January 20, 1976, at approximately 2000 hours

**Location:** 127 Reece Ave W, Chilliwack, BC (with the object observed positioned above International Ridge, southeast of Chilliwack)

**Sighting:** On the evening of January 20, 1976, at approximately 2000 hours, three witnesses—Cpl Seath Jr, Cpl(W) Seath VD, and Cpl(W) Hansen SJ—observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon from their location at 127 Reece Ave W in Chilliwack, BC. The witnesses reported that the sky conditions were clear at the time of the sighting. The object was observed hovering or positioned above International Ridge, a geographical feature located to the southeast of Chilliwack. The duration of the sighting was sustained, lasting for approximately two hours.

**Object:** The object was described as a single, round entity characterized by the emission of different colored lights. No specific sound or complex movement patterns were noted in the reports, other than its prolonged presence in the sky above the ridge.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Following the observation, the witnesses took photographs of the object. At the time the reports were filed, these photographs were awaiting development. No further details regarding the contents of the photographs or subsequent official analysis were provided in the available documentation.
CA-FOIA-Part_10-p244-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 小西斯下士（照片技术员）、西斯·V.D.下士（女，行政文员）、汉森·S.J.下士（女，行政文员）

**日期 / 时间：** 1976年1月20日，约2000时

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省奇利瓦克市里斯大道西127号（观测到的物体位于奇利瓦克东南方向的国际岭上方）

**目击经过：** 1976年1月20日晚约2000时，三名目击者——小西斯下士、西斯·V.D.下士和汉森·S.J.下士——在位于不列颠哥伦比亚省奇利瓦克市里斯大道西127号的地点观测到一种不明空中现象。据目击者报告，目击时天空状况晴朗。该物体被观测到悬停或位于奇利瓦克东南方向的地理特征“国际岭”上方。此次目击持续时间较长，约为两小时。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个单一的圆形实体，其特征是会发出不同颜色的光。报告中未提及任何特定的声音或复杂的运动模式，仅记录了它在山脊上方天空中的长时间停留。

**调查/后续：** 目击事件发生后，目击者对该物体进行了拍照。在提交报告时，这些照片尚待冲洗。现有文档中未提供关于照片内容的进一步细节，也未提及后续的官方分析结果。

CA-FOIA-Part_10-p255-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Thomas Patterson and the reporting officer, G.E. Crowe.

**Sighting:** On December 16, 1976, at approximately 5:00 PM, Mr. Patterson reported seeing a bright light in the sky over Arctic Mountain, Carcross, Yukon Territory. The light appeared to be moving slowly to the right. The sky was very clear with hardly any clouds.

**Object:** The object was described as a bright light. The reporting officer observed the light using a 45-power spotting scope but could not identify any structure or detail other than the light itself. The object moved slowly to the southeast and disappeared at approximately 6:00 PM.

**Aftermath:** Aeradio Whitehorse was contacted and confirmed the light was not from an aircraft or a satellite. No other sightings were reported that evening. A telex was sent to the National Research Council in Ottawa, and a copy of the report was forwarded to them for their information.
CA-FOIA-Part_10-p255-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 托马斯·帕特森（Thomas Patterson）先生及报告警官 G.E. 克罗（G.E. Crowe）。

**日期：** 1976年12月16日。

**地点：** 育空地区卡克罗斯（Carcross），北极山（Arctic Mountain）上空。

**目击经过：** 1976年12月16日下午5点左右，帕特森先生报告称在育空地区卡克罗斯的北极山上空看到一束明亮的光。该光束似乎正缓慢向右移动。当时天空非常晴朗，几乎没有云层。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一束明亮的光。报告警官使用45倍观测镜对该光束进行了观察，但除了光束本身外，无法辨认出任何结构或细节。该物体缓慢向东南方向移动，并于下午6点左右消失。

**调查/后续：** 怀特霍斯航空无线电台（Aeradio Whitehorse）在接到联系后确认，该光束并非来自飞机或卫星。当晚未收到其他目击报告。一份电传已发送至渥太华的国家研究委员会（National Research Council），报告副本也已转发给他们以供参考。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p037-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Margaret Vincent, Mrs. George (Stephanie) Kingston, Vicki Watson

**Date / Time:** January 25, 1977, at approximately 10:30 a.m. PST

**Location:** Clinton Creek, Yukon Territory (specifically 514 Boundary Road)

**Sighting:** On the morning of January 25, 1977, Margaret Vincent, a part-time teacher and wife of the Clinton Creek Mine Manager, observed an unidentified object from her home. The sky was described as having a high, light-grey overcast. Mrs. Vincent was initially alerted to the event by a loud noise resembling an airplane, which was powerful enough to drown out her radio. 

Mrs. Vincent observed the object traveling in a southwesterly direction along the 40 Mile River. She estimated the object’s distance from her position to be between 1/4 and 1/2 mile, and noted it was approximately 150–200 feet higher than her own elevation. She watched the object follow the course of the river for four to five miles over a duration of approximately 1.5 to 2 minutes. Following the sighting, Mrs. Vincent contacted her neighbor, Mrs. George (Stephanie) Kingston, who confirmed hearing the sound of an airplane but did not witness the object itself. The file also notes that Vicki Watson was a witness associated with the event. Mrs. Vincent’s report was part of a broader context of local sightings reported since mid-December 1976, involving town maintenance crew members, family members, and neighbors.

**Object:** The object was described as a pulsating light, shifting between bluish-white and yellowish-white. It maintained an altitude of approximately 300–400 feet above the river ice. The object appeared to be 2–3 feet in diameter, with a possible dark armature visible to the right side. While the sound produced by the object was similar to that of a small airplane or helicopter, Mrs. Vincent explicitly stated that it did not appear to be either of those aircraft, nor did it appear large enough to carry an adult human.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) Dawson Detachment conducted an investigation, taking a formal statement from Margaret Vincent on February 2, 1977. The investigating officer noted that Mrs. Vincent held a responsible position in the community and was considered a highly reliable source. 

While the Dawson Detachment report initially referenced other potential sightings in the area since mid-December, the investigator later noted that this was the only UFO sighting formally reported to their office to date, and no other sightings in the Clinton Creek area had been brought to their attention. The file was officially considered concluded by the Dawson Detachment, though the RCMP noted they remained prepared to resume the investigation should further information or reports arise.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p037-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 玛格丽特·文森特 (Margaret Vincent)、乔治·金斯顿夫人（斯蒂芬妮·金斯顿）(Mrs. George (Stephanie) Kingston)、维基·沃森 (Vicki Watson)

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年1月25日，太平洋标准时间上午约10:30

**地点：** 育空地区克林顿溪（具体地址为边界路514号）

**目击经过：** 1977年1月25日上午，兼职教师、克林顿溪矿区经理的妻子玛格丽特·文森特在家中观察到一个不明物体。当时天空呈现高空浅灰色阴天。文森特夫人最初是被一阵类似于飞机的巨大噪音所惊动，该声音响亮到足以盖过她收音机的声音。

文森特夫人观察到该物体正沿着四十英里河（40 Mile River）向西南方向飞行。她估计该物体距离她所在位置约四分之一到半英里，并指出其高度比她所在位置高出约150至200英尺。她观察到该物体沿着河流航向飞行了四到五英里，持续时间约为1.5到2分钟。目击事件发生后，文森特夫人联系了她的邻居乔治·金斯顿夫人（斯蒂芬妮·金斯顿），后者证实听到了类似飞机的声音，但并未亲眼看到该物体。档案还记录了维基·沃森也是与该事件相关的目击者。文森特夫人的报告是自1976年12月中旬以来当地一系列目击事件的一部分，涉及城镇维修人员、家庭成员及邻居。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个脉冲光体，在蓝白色和黄白色之间变换。它保持在河冰上方约300至400英尺的高度。物体直径约为2至3英尺，右侧似乎有一个可见的深色框架结构。虽然该物体发出的声音类似于小型飞机或直升机，但文森特夫人明确表示它看起来并不像这两种飞行器，其体积也不足以搭载一名成年人。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）道森分局对此进行了调查，并于1977年2月2日正式记录了玛格丽特·文森特的陈述。负责调查的警官指出，文森特夫人在社区中担任重要职务，被认为是一个高度可靠的消息来源。

尽管道森分局的报告最初提到了自12月中旬以来该地区可能发生的其他目击事件，但调查人员后来指出，这是迄今为止正式向其办公室报告的唯一一起不明飞行物目击事件，且克林顿溪地区没有其他目击报告引起他们的注意。该档案已被道森分局正式结案，但加拿大皇家骑警表示，如果出现进一步的信息或报告，他们随时准备恢复调查。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p066-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. William Torrie, Mrs. Torrie (wife), and their son.

**Date / Time:** March 4, 1977 (0302Z – 0415Z) and March 6, 1977 (0350Z – 0420Z).

**Location:** Saltcoats, Saskatchewan (approximately 285 degrees from CFS Yorkton; sighting on March 6 occurred 3 1/2 miles northeast of Saltcoats).

**Sighting:** 
The event involved two separate observations by the Torrie family. On March 4, 1977, between 0302Z and 0415Z, Mr. William Torrie, his wife, and their son observed a single object from Saltcoats, Saskatchewan. During this initial sighting, the object was noted to be stationary.

A second sighting occurred on March 6, 1977, between 0350Z and 0420Z, involving Mr. and Mrs. Torrie. During this encounter, the object was observed 3 1/2 miles northeast of Saltcoats. The weather conditions were noted as cloudy overhead, though the sky remained clear in the specific area where the object was positioned. Unlike the stationary behavior reported on March 4, the witnesses observed the object moving toward the northwest. During this movement, the light was seen to fade and then brighten again. The object eventually passed behind a 30-foot-high shelter located approximately 70 yards away from the witnesses.

**Object:** 
The object was consistently described as triangular in shape. Regarding its appearance, it was characterized as a bright, yellowish-white light, estimated to be three times the size of a normal star. While the object was reported as stationary during the March 4 sighting, the March 6 observation documented movement toward the northwest, including fluctuations in brightness (fading and brightening). No sound was reported.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** 
The reports for both sightings were officially filed by CFS Yorkton. The documentation was forwarded to the National Defence Operations Centre (NDOC) in Ottawa and the National Research Council (NRC) for further review.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p066-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 威廉·托里先生（Mr. William Torrie）、托里夫人（Mrs. Torrie）及其儿子。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年3月4日（03:02Z – 04:15Z）及1977年3月6日（03:50Z – 04:20Z）。

**地点：** 萨斯喀彻温省索尔特科茨（Saltcoats, Saskatchewan）（约位于约克顿加拿大武装部队基地（CFS Yorkton）285度方位；3月6日的目击事件发生在索尔特科茨东北方向3.5英里处）。

**目击经过：**
该事件涉及托里一家两次独立的目击观察。1977年3月4日，在03:02Z至04:15Z之间，威廉·托里先生、其妻子及儿子在萨斯喀彻温省索尔特科茨观察到了一个单一物体。在这次初步目击中，该物体处于静止状态。

第二次目击发生在1977年3月6日，时间为03:50Z至04:20Z，目击者为托里夫妇。在此次遭遇中，该物体被发现位于索尔特科茨东北方向3.5英里处。当时的天气状况显示头顶上方多云，但物体所在区域的天空保持晴朗。与3月4日报告的静止状态不同，目击者观察到该物体正向西北方向移动。在移动过程中，其光芒时而暗淡，时而变亮。最终，该物体从距离目击者约70码处一座30英尺高的遮蔽物后方经过。

**物体描述：**
该物体被一致描述为三角形。在外形方面，它表现为一个明亮的黄白色光点，估计大小为普通恒星的三倍。虽然在3月4日的目击中该物体被报告为静止，但3月6日的观察记录了其向西北方向的移动，并伴有亮度波动（变暗及变亮）。未报告有任何声音。

**调查/后续：**
这两次目击报告均由约克顿加拿大武装部队基地（CFS Yorkton）正式存档。相关文件已被转交至渥太华的国家国防行动中心（NDOC）及国家研究委员会（NRC）作进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p071-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Cst. P.E. Schneider, S/Cst. Peter Paul Willier, S/Sgt. J.L. Laliberte, Cst. J.D. Millar, Mr. Walter George Esser, Mrs. Karin Esser, Manuela Esser (14), Marion Esser (12), and members of the Faust RCMP Detachment.

**Date / Time:** March 3, 1977 (approx. 10:00 P.M. – 10:20 P.M.); March 10, 1977 (approx. 9:40 P.M. – 10:15 P.M.).

**Location:** Slave Lake and Canyon Creek, Alberta (Lesser Slave Lake shoreline).

**Sighting:** This report documents a sighting wave occurring over two dates. On March 3, 1977, Walter Esser observed a bright light over Lesser Slave Lake from the Canyon Creek store. He alerted his wife, Karin, and daughters, Manuela and Marion, who watched the object for 20 minutes. The object moved west, then east, then back west, appearing silent and moving at the speed of a small plane. S/Cst. Willier arrived at the shoreline and observed the object with binoculars for 10 minutes, noting it floated at 1,000–1,500 feet, wobbled, and performed a "bouncing" motion while losing altitude. It disappeared, reappeared after 10 minutes, and moved parallel to the shore before vanishing.

On March 10, 1977, RCMP officers (Schneider, Willier, and Laliberte) observed a similar phenomenon from the southwest outskirts of Slave Lake. Cst. Schneider first spotted the object at 9:40 P.M. The observation lasted 30 minutes. The object performed both horizontal and vertical movements, maintaining an altitude of approximately 2,000 feet before eventually descending below the tree line to the west. A note in the file indicates that a similar sighting occurred one week prior to the March 10 event, matching the duration and timing of the officers' observations.

**Object:** The object was consistently described as cone-shaped or "bell-bottomed," tapering to a domed top. It was orange-amber in color, with some witnesses describing it as a bright spotlight half the size of the moon. It featured intense, pulsating, and flickering lights: bright red on the lower sections (specifically the lower left corner), and greenish or amber lights on the top and right sections. The lights were observed to rotate and vary in intensity. The object made no sound and, when viewed through binoculars, appeared to "shrink" or glow like "fire coals" as it moved away.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP conducted multiple interviews and on-site investigations. S/Cst. Willier took formal statements from the Esser family on March 7, 1977. During the March 10 event, Csts. Schneider and Willier utilized binoculars for detailed observation. Csts. Millar and Schneider, along with the Faust Detachment, attempted to intercept the object on March 3, but it did not reappear. Despite the use of cameras by officers, no photographic evidence was successfully captured. Walter Esser, an experienced observer of satellites and meteorites, explicitly stated the object did not match any known aerial phenomena. The RCMP concluded their investigation after no further sightings were reported.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p071-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** P.E. 施奈德警官 (Cst. P.E. Schneider)、彼得·保罗·威利尔高级警官 (S/Cst. Peter Paul Willier)、J.L. 拉利伯特参谋警长 (S/Sgt. J.L. Laliberte)、J.D. 米勒警官 (Cst. J.D. Millar)、沃尔特·乔治·埃瑟先生 (Mr. Walter George Esser)、卡琳·埃瑟夫人 (Mrs. Karin Esser)、曼努埃拉·埃瑟 (Manuela Esser，14岁)、马里昂·埃瑟 (Marion Esser，12岁)，以及福斯特 (Faust) 加拿大皇家骑警分局的成员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年3月3日（约晚上10:00 – 10:20）；1977年3月10日（约晚上9:40 – 10:15）。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省奴湖 (Slave Lake) 和峡谷溪 (Canyon Creek)（小奴湖湖岸）。

**目击经过：** 本报告记录了发生在两个日期的目击浪潮。1977年3月3日，沃尔特·埃瑟在峡谷溪商店观察到小奴湖上方出现一道亮光。他提醒了妻子卡琳和女儿曼努埃拉及马里昂，她们观察了该物体20分钟。该物体向西移动，随后向东，又折回向西，全程无声，移动速度与小型飞机相当。威利尔高级警官抵达湖岸，用双筒望远镜观察了该物体10分钟，指出它悬浮在1,000至1,500英尺的高度，摇晃不定，并在下降过程中表现出一种“弹跳”动作。它消失后，10分钟后再次出现，并沿着与湖岸平行的方向移动，随后彻底消失。

1977年3月10日，加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 警官（施奈德、威利尔和拉利伯特）在奴湖西南部郊区观察到了类似的现象。施奈德警官于晚上9:40首次发现该物体，观察持续了30分钟。该物体进行了水平和垂直移动，保持在约2,000英尺的高度，最终向西降至树线以下。档案中的一条记录显示，在3月10日事件发生前一周，曾出现过类似的目击事件，其持续时间和时间点与警官们的观察结果相符。

**物体描述：** 该物体被一致描述为圆锥形或“钟形”，顶部呈圆顶状。它呈橙琥珀色，一些目击者称其为一个大小约为月球一半的明亮聚光灯。它具有强烈、脉动且闪烁的灯光：下部（特别是左下角）为亮红色，顶部和右侧为绿色或琥珀色灯光。观察发现这些灯光会旋转且亮度会发生变化。该物体没有发出任何声音，通过双筒望远镜观察时，随着它的远离，它看起来会“缩小”或像“火炭”一样发光。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警进行了多次访谈和现场调查。威利尔高级警官于1977年3月7日对埃瑟一家进行了正式笔录。在3月10日的事件中，施奈德警官和威利尔高级警官使用了双筒望远镜进行详细观察。米勒警官和施奈德警官以及福斯特分局曾试图在3月3日拦截该物体，但它并未再次出现。尽管警官们使用了照相机，但未能成功获取任何摄影证据。作为一名经验丰富的卫星和陨石观测者，沃尔特·埃瑟明确表示该物体不符合任何已知的空中现象。在没有收到进一步的目击报告后，加拿大皇家骑警结束了调查。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p086-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Roger David Miller (Air Traffic Controller), Harvey Richard Brinson (Air Traffic Controller), and the pilot of a Canadian Forces C-130 aircraft.

**Date / Time:** March 15, 1977, at approximately 9:00 P.M. Newfoundland Standard Time.

**Location:** Gander International Airport, Newfoundland (observed from the Gander Control Tower).

**Sighting:** On the evening of March 15, 1977, two air traffic controllers, Roger David Miller and Harvey Richard Brinson, observed an unidentified flying object while on duty in the Gander Control Tower. The atmospheric conditions were reported as clear with thin scattered clouds and visibility of 30 miles (with cloud ceilings noted at 30,000 feet). The object was sighted at a 320-degree magnetic bearing from the tower. The controllers estimated the object’s distance at 10 to 15 miles away, hovering at an altitude of 2,000 to 3,000 feet. The object remained in a fixed position for a duration of four and a half to five minutes before disappearing very quickly. Additionally, the pilot of a Canadian Forces C-130 aircraft, while approaching and landing at Gander Airport, also observed the object; the pilot expressed the belief that the object was a planet.

**Object:** The object was described as spherical in shape with irregular edges. In terms of size, it appeared to be approximately one-eighth the size of the moon, though another account described it as "medium size," comparable to an aircraft. The object exhibited varying luminosity, ranging from the brightness of a star to slightly brighter, and displayed bursts of light. It cycled through colors, shifting between red, orange, and white. No sounds were heard by the witnesses during the observation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was documented by the Gander Detachment of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). The official report was prepared and signed by Constable A.D. Lloyd and forwarded by Staff Sergeant L.R.H. of the Gander Detachment. The documentation, including the details of the sighting and the witness accounts, was transmitted to the National Research Council (NRC) Planetary Sciences Section in Ottawa, Ontario, for further review.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p086-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 罗杰·大卫·米勒（Roger David Miller，空中交通管制员）、哈维·理查德·布林森（Harvey Richard Brinson，空中交通管制员），以及一架加拿大空军C-130运输机的飞行员。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年3月15日，纽芬兰标准时间晚上9:00左右。

**地点：** 纽芬兰甘德国际机场（从甘德机场控制塔观测）。

**目击经过：** 1977年3月15日晚，两名空中交通管制员罗杰·大卫·米勒和哈维·理查德·布林森在甘德控制塔值班时，观测到了一个不明飞行物。据报告，当时大气条件晴朗，有少量零散云层，能见度为30英里（云底高度约为30,000英尺）。该物体位于控制塔磁方位320度方向。管制员估计该物体距离约10至15英里，悬停在2,000至3,000英尺的高度。该物体在固定位置停留了四分半钟到五分钟，随后迅速消失。此外，一架加拿大空军C-130运输机的飞行员在接近并降落甘德机场时也观测到了该物体；该飞行员认为该物体是一颗行星。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为球形，边缘不规则。就大小而言，它看起来约为月球大小的八分之一，但另一份报告将其描述为“中等大小”，与一架飞机相当。该物体亮度多变，从星光亮度到略亮不等，并伴有光束闪烁。它在红色、橙色和白色之间循环变换颜色。观测期间，目击者未听到任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）甘德分遣队记录在案。官方报告由A.D. 劳埃德（A.D. Lloyd）警官编写并签署，并由甘德分遣队的L.R.H.参谋警长转交。包括目击细节和证人陈述在内的文件已被送往位于安大略省渥太华的加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）行星科学部门进行进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p135-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mr. Thorn, Mr. Marigan, Heather Bohanan (also spelled Bonahan), Wayne Bohanan (also spelled Bonahan), and Ron Kelly.

**Date / Time:** May 16–17, 1977. Specific sighting times recorded include 162155, 162200, 162205, and 162355 local time.

**Location:** Hart Highway, British Columbia.

**Sighting:** A series of sightings occurred over the Hart Highway area under cloudy conditions, with a recorded cloud base of 15,000 feet. Multiple witnesses—Mr. Thorn, Mr. Marigan, Heather Bohanan, Wayne Bohanan, and Ron Kelly—observed the phenomenon outdoors. The first sighting occurred at approximately 1622 hours (with specific logs noting 162155 and 162205). The witnesses observed a single object moving from the northeast to the southwest at a high rate of speed, positioned just below the cloud layer. The duration of this initial sighting was recorded as three to four minutes. A second sighting occurred later at 162355 hours. This second event was described as similar to the first, though it featured a distinct exhaust trail and was observed at a lower altitude of 1,000 to 2,000 feet. Throughout the duration of the sightings, no sound was reported by the witnesses.

**Object:** The object was described as a round, red ball, approximately seven feet in diameter. A notable feature reported by the witnesses was the presence of windows visible along one side of the craft. The object was observed through binoculars, which allowed for the identification of these specific structural details. It maintained a fast speed during its transit and, during the second sighting, emitted an exhaust trail while flying at an altitude of 1,000 to 2,000 feet.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The sighting was formally documented and transmitted through official military and government channels. Reports were relayed from CFS Baldy Hughes to the Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) and National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ) in Ottawa. Additionally, the data was forwarded to the National Research Council (NRC) Radio and Electrical Engineering Division for further review. No specific sketches or meteorological analysis beyond the cloud base data were provided in the summary files.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p135-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 索恩先生 (Mr. Thorn)、马里根先生 (Mr. Marigan)、希瑟·博哈南 (Heather Bohanan，亦拼作 Bonahan)、韦恩·博哈南 (Wayne Bohanan，亦拼作 Bonahan) 以及罗恩·凯利 (Ron Kelly)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年5月16日至17日。记录的具体目击时间包括当地时间16日21:55、22:00、22:05以及23:55。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省，哈特公路 (Hart Highway)。

**目击经过：** 在多云天气下，哈特公路地区发生了一系列目击事件，记录的云底高度为15,000英尺。多名目击者——索恩先生、马里根先生、希瑟·博哈南、韦恩·博哈南和罗恩·凯利——在户外观察到了这一现象。首次目击发生在约22:00（具体记录显示为21:55和22:05）。目击者观察到一个单一物体正处于云层下方，以极高的速度从东北向西南方向移动。此次目击持续了三到四分钟。第二次目击发生在随后的23:55。第二次事件的描述与第一次相似，但该物体留下了明显的尾迹，且飞行高度较低，约为1,000至2,000英尺。在整个目击过程中，目击者均未报告听到任何声音。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个直径约七英尺的圆形红球。目击者报告的一个显著特征是飞行器一侧可见窗户。通过双筒望远镜观察，目击者得以辨认出这些具体的结构细节。该物体在飞行过程中保持高速，在第二次目击时，它在1,000至2,000英尺的高度飞行并留下了尾迹。

**调查/后续：** 该目击事件已正式记录并通过官方军事和政府渠道进行传递。报告由巴尔迪休斯空军基地 (CFS Baldy Hughes) 转达至渥太华的救援协调中心 (RCC) 和国防总部 (NDHQ)。此外，相关数据还被转发至加拿大国家研究委员会 (NRC) 无线电与电气工程部门进行进一步审查。摘要文件中未提供除云底数据以外的具体草图或气象分析。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p136-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Heather Bohanan (28), Tony Bohanan (37), Wayne Bohanan (19), Ron Kelly (19), Mr. Thornton, and Mr. Madigan.

**Date / Time:** May 16, 1977; 9:55 PM – 10:05 PM Pacific Time.

**Location:** 2281 Walker Rd., Prince George, British Columbia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of May 16, 1977, at approximately 9:55 PM, a group of four witnesses—Heather Bohanan, Tony Bohanan, Wayne Bohanan, and Ron Kelly—observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while at 2281 Walker Rd. The weather conditions were noted as clear, with only a small cloud formation present to the south. The witnesses observed the object moving from the north toward the south. The object hovered in the middle of the horizon at an altitude of approximately 1,000 feet before climbing vertically to an altitude of 2,000 feet. Following this ascent, the object accelerated and disappeared into the clouds. The duration of this specific sighting was approximately 5 minutes.

Separately, at 10:05 PM, two additional witnesses, Mr. Thornton and Mr. Madigan, reported observing a different object. Their account described a round, red ball traveling across the sky from the northeast to the southwest. This sighting lasted for a duration of 3 to 4 minutes.

**Object:** The primary object observed by the Bohanan group and Ron Kelly was described as oblong in shape, red in color, and approximately 40 feet in length. It featured a brighter red, exhaust-like projection at one end. The object made no sound during its maneuvers. The secondary object observed by Mr. Thornton and Mr. Madigan was described as a round, red ball approximately 7 feet in diameter.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP handled the initial report and documented the statements. The investigating officers noted that all observers appeared to be reliable individuals who were visibly shaken by their experiences. The RCMP contacted Canadian Forces Base (C.F.B.) Baldy Hughes regarding the events. C.F.B. Baldy Hughes confirmed that they had received two other reports of sightings in the same area on that date. The official documentation was subsequently forwarded to the National Research Council for further review.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p136-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 希瑟·博哈南（Heather Bohanan，28岁）、托尼·博哈南（Tony Bohanan，37岁）、韦恩·博哈南（Wayne Bohanan，19岁）、罗恩·凯利（Ron Kelly，19岁）、桑顿先生（Mr. Thornton）以及马迪根先生（Mr. Madigan）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年5月16日；太平洋时间晚上9:55 – 10:05。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省乔治王子城，沃克路2281号（2281 Walker Rd., Prince George, British Columbia）。

**目击经过：** 1977年5月16日晚约9:55，四名目击者——希瑟·博哈南、托尼·博哈南、韦恩·博哈南和罗恩·凯利在沃克路2281号观察到一种不明空中现象。当时天气晴朗，仅南方有少量云层。目击者看到该物体从北向南移动。物体在地平线中央悬停，高度约1000英尺，随后垂直攀升至2000英尺高度。上升后，物体加速并消失在云层中。此次目击过程持续了约5分钟。

另外，在晚上10:05，另外两名目击者桑顿先生和马迪根先生报告称观察到了另一个物体。他们的描述显示，这是一个圆形的红色球体，从东北方向飞向西南方向。此次目击持续了3到4分钟。

**物体描述：** 博哈南一行人和罗恩·凯利观察到的主要物体被描述为长方形，呈红色，长度约40英尺。其一端有一个更明亮的红色、类似排气装置的突出物。该物体在机动过程中未发出任何声音。桑顿先生和马迪根先生观察到的第二个物体被描述为一个直径约7英尺的圆形红色球体。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）处理了初步报告并记录了证词。调查警官指出，所有观察者看起来都是可靠的人，且对所经历的事情感到明显不安。加拿大皇家骑警就此事联系了巴尔迪休斯加拿大武装部队基地（C.F.B. Baldy Hughes）。该基地证实，他们当天在同一地区还收到了另外两起目击报告。官方文件随后被转交至加拿大国家研究委员会（National Research Council）作进一步审查。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p159-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Bill Ronald Desson (also referred to as Bill Dessn/Desson), Jean Desson.

**Date / Time:** April 29, 1975 (3:52–3:54); a secondary sighting occurred on May 7, 1977, at 10:50 P.M.

**Location:** Vars/Kemptville, Ontario (specifically near the Clothier Street bridge in Kemptville for the 1977 event).

**Sighting:** On April 29, 1975, Bill Ronald Desson, then 12 years old, observed a UFO from inside his home. He noted the object was initially noticed due to its "darkness and speed." The object emerged from a cloud, flew in front of it, and then disappeared behind another cloud. The total duration of the sighting was approximately three minutes. Upon seeing the object, the witness went to his bedroom to retrieve a camera and successfully took a photograph of the object as it emerged from behind a cloud. The witness reported hearing a "very constant, disturbing" noise during the event. He described the object as "spinning" and noted that it moved in a straight line with a "slight trail." The witness experienced a state of shock and excitement, continuing to scan the sky after the object vanished. A separate, potentially related report mentions a sighting lasting approximately 6 seconds, observed from "beside a road," with the witness using a digital watch to track the time.

A second sighting involving Bill Desson occurred on May 7, 1977, at 10:50 P.M. near the Clothier Street bridge in Kemptville. This report was filed in May 1977 with Jean Desson.

**Object:** The object was described as a "U.F.O." that moved in a straight line, leaving a "slight trail." It was observed to be "spinning." While specific dimensions are not provided, a sketch from the 1975 event indicates the object’s position relative to the horizon at approximately 45 and 60 degrees. The object was noted for its speed and its ability to disappear and reappear behind cloud cover.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The documentation consists of multiple National Research Council of Canada (NRC) UFO reporting forms. The witness, Bill Ronald Desson, demonstrated a significant interest in the subject, noting in his 1977 report that he had read 13 books on UFOs. The files include sketches of the object's elevation relative to the horizon. Despite the witness taking a photograph of the object, no physical evidence or ground disturbance was recorded in the provided files. The RCMP and NRC records (RG 77, Vol. 308) categorize these as standard sighting questionnaires. The witness later moved from the Kars area, as noted in his correspondence.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p159-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 比尔·罗纳德·德森（Bill Ronald Desson，亦作 Bill Dessn/Desson）、简·德森（Jean Desson）。

**日期 / 时间：** 1975年4月29日（3:52–3:54）；另一次目击发生在1977年5月7日晚上10:50。

**地点：** 安大略省瓦尔斯（Vars）/肯普特维尔（Kemptville）（1977年的事件具体位于肯普特维尔的克洛西尔街（Clothier Street）大桥附近）。

**目击经过：** 1975年4月29日，时年12岁的比尔·罗纳德·德森在家中观察到了一个不明飞行物（UFO）。他指出，该物体最初引起注意是因为其“黑暗的色调和极快的速度”。物体从云层中显现，飞过云层前方，随后消失在另一片云层之后。目击过程总时长约为三分钟。目击者在看到物体后回到卧室取相机，并成功拍下了物体从云层后方显现时的照片。目击者报告称，在事件过程中听到了一种“持续且令人不安”的噪音。他描述该物体处于“旋转”状态，并指出它沿直线移动，带有“轻微的尾迹”。目击者当时处于震惊和兴奋的状态，在物体消失后仍持续扫描天空。另一份可能相关的报告提到了一次持续约6秒的目击事件，目击者当时位于“路边”，并使用数字手表记录了时间。

比尔·德森参与的第二次目击事件发生在1977年5月7日晚上10:50，地点位于肯普特维尔的克洛西尔街大桥附近。该报告于1977年5月与简·德森共同提交。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为一个“UFO”，沿直线移动，留有“轻微的尾迹”。观察发现其处于“旋转”状态。虽然未提供具体尺寸，但1975年事件的一份草图显示了该物体相对于地平线约45度和60度的位置。该物体的特点在于其速度极快，且能够穿梭于云层后方进行隐现。

**调查/后续：** 相关档案包含多份加拿大国家研究委员会（NRC）的UFO报告表。目击者比尔·罗纳德·德森对该课题表现出浓厚兴趣，他在1977年的报告中提到自己已经阅读了13本关于UFO的书籍。档案中包括了物体相对于地平线高度的草图。尽管目击者拍摄了物体的照片，但提供的档案中并未记录任何物理证据或地面干扰。加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）和国家研究委员会（NRC）的记录（RG 77, Vol. 308）将这些归类为标准的目击调查问卷。根据其通信记录，目击者后来搬离了卡尔斯（Kars）地区。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p201-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Pvt. Michael Marchand (ATCA/QTCA)

**Date / Time:** July 25, 1977, at 0040Z

**Location:** 21 Lochlomond, CFB Greenwood, Nova Scotia

**Sighting:** On July 25, 1977, at 0040Z, Pvt. Michael Marchand observed an unidentified aerial phenomenon while standing in the yard of his residence at 21 Lochlomond, located on the grounds of CFB Greenwood. The witness tracked the object for a total duration of 15 seconds. During this time, the object was observed moving rapidly in a trajectory from the south to the north. The path of the object took it directly across the face of the moon. The sighting concluded when the object moved behind cloud cover and disappeared from view.

**Object:** The object was described as circular in shape and white in color. It was positioned at an altitude above the cloud layer. Its luminosity was noted as being less intense than that of the moon. No sound was reported, and the object exhibited rapid, consistent movement across the sky until it was obscured by clouds.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** Official inquiries were conducted by CFB Greenwood personnel to determine the nature of the object. Greenwood Tower confirmed that there was no known local air traffic in the area at the time of the sighting. Furthermore, a review of Greenwood radar data indicated that nothing was detected or held on the radar screens during the period of the observation. Meteorological conditions at the time of the sighting were recorded as 100 SCTD (scattered) with 200 thin broken clouds, with an estimated cloud opacity of 2/10 and 3/10.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p201-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 二等兵迈克尔·马尚 (Michael Marchand) (ATCA/QTCA)

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年7月25日，0040Z（祖鲁时间）

**地点：** 新斯科舍省格林伍德加拿大武装部队基地 (CFB Greenwood)，洛赫洛蒙德 (Lochlomond) 21号

**目击经过：** 1977年7月25日0040Z，二等兵迈克尔·马尚在位于格林伍德加拿大武装部队基地内的洛赫洛蒙德21号住所院子里，观察到一种不明空中现象。目击者对该物体进行了总计15秒的跟踪观察。在此期间，该物体被观察到正从南向北快速移动。其飞行轨迹直接穿过了月球表面。当物体移动到云层后并消失在视野中时，目击过程结束。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，呈白色。它位于云层上方的高度。据记录，其亮度不及月球。目击者未报告任何声音，且该物体在被云层遮挡前，在天空中表现出快速、持续的移动。

**调查/后续：** 格林伍德加拿大武装部队基地的人员进行了官方调查，以确定该物体的性质。格林伍德塔台确认，在目击发生时，该地区没有已知的当地空中交通。此外，对格林伍德雷达数据的审查显示，在观察期间，雷达屏幕上未探测到或锁定任何目标。据记录，目击时的气象条件为100 SCTD（疏云），伴有200英尺高的薄碎云，估计云层遮蔽率为2/10至3/10。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p231-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Mrs. Mary Schooling, one unnamed female companion.

**Date / Time:** August 11, 1977, at approximately 21:50 hours Pacific Daylight Time.

**Location:** Near the corner of Maple Road and West Coast Road, Sooke, British Columbia.

**Sighting:** On the evening of August 11, 1977, Mrs. Mary Schooling and an unnamed female companion were in the vicinity of Maple Road and West Coast Road in Sooke, BC. The witnesses reported that the sky was clear and sunny at the time of the observation. According to their accounts, the object hovered over the Sooke Basin for a short duration. After hovering, the object initially headed in an easterly direction before suddenly changing course to head west, continuing in that direction until it was completely out of sight.

**Object:** The object was described as silver in color and shaped like a zeppelin, though notably smaller in size. The witnesses observed red markings on what they perceived to be the back of the craft. The object lacked any visible wings or a tail. During the sighting, the object produced a soft humming noise.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The incident was officially reported by Cst. D.H. Fare of the Sooke Detachment of the RCMP. During the follow-up process, it was suggested to Mrs. Schooling that the object might have been a meteor fragment, as such phenomena were expected to be visible in the sky over the following days. Mrs. Schooling explicitly rejected this explanation, refusing to believe the object was a meteor fragment. No further information regarding the incident was obtained by the Sooke Detachment RCMP.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p231-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 玛丽·斯库林（Mary Schooling）女士，以及一位未具名的女性同伴。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年8月11日，太平洋夏令时间约21:50。

**地点：** 不列颠哥伦比亚省苏克市（Sooke），枫树路（Maple Road）与西海岸路（West Coast Road）交汇处附近。

**目击经过：** 1977年8月11日晚，玛丽·斯库林女士与一位未具名的女性同伴位于不列颠哥伦比亚省苏克市的枫树路与西海岸路附近。据目击者称，观测时天空晴朗且阳光明媚。据她们描述，该物体在苏克湾（Sooke Basin）上空悬停了片刻。悬停后，物体最初向东飞行，随后突然改变航向转向西，并持续向该方向飞行，直至完全消失在视野中。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为银色，形状像齐柏林飞艇，但体积明显较小。目击者观察到在她们所认为的飞行器后部有红色标记。该物体没有任何可见的机翼或尾翼。在目击过程中，物体发出了一种柔和的嗡嗡声。

**调查/后续：** 该事件由加拿大皇家骑警（RCMP）苏克分局的D.H.法尔（D.H. Fare）警员正式记录。在后续调查过程中，有人向斯库林女士提出该物体可能是一块流星碎片的推测，因为预计未来几天天空中会出现此类现象。斯库林女士明确拒绝了这一解释，不相信该物体是流星碎片。加拿大皇家骑警苏克分局未获得有关该事件的更多信息。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p242-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Eli Androchuk, Helen Androchuk (mother of Eli Androchuk), S/Sgt. R.H. Rowell, Cst. R.A. St. Martin.

**Date / Time:** August 13, 1977, at approximately 3:00 A.M. Mountain Standard Time.

**Location:** Seba Beach, Alberta; specifically observed near the Sundance Power Plant, Lake Wabamun, and along Highway No. 16.

**Sighting:** At approximately 3:00 A.M. on August 13, 1977, Eli Androchuk was driving from Edmonton toward Seba Beach when he observed a bright, clear white light in the sky near the Sundance Power Plant. He noted that the light appeared in place of the usual red warning lights on the plant's chimneys. Eli followed the object while driving south on Highway No. 16. The object was initially stationary, then began performing vertical and horizontal movements, including rising and "jiggling." It disappeared behind a hill, only to reappear near the horizon. Eli observed the object for 20 to 25 minutes before waking his mother, Helen Androchuk, to witness the event as well. After reporting the sighting to the RCMP, Eli observed the object for one additional minute, noting it was still moving south and rising before he retired to bed. The sky was reported as clear with very good visibility throughout the duration of the sighting.

**Object:** The object was described as circular, appearing like a star but significantly larger—estimated by some accounts as being approximately one-quarter the size of a full moon. It emitted a brilliant white light that shone at an angle from a central point. While some reports noted the light intensity remained constant, others indicated the light density changed at times. The object exhibited erratic movement, including jiggling, rising, and horizontal travel. No sound was heard during the observation.

**Investigation / Follow-up:** The RCMP received a complaint regarding the sighting at 4:05 A.M. An official patrol of the Sundance Power Plant and the surrounding area was conducted by S/Sgt. R.H. Rowell and Cst. R.A. St. Martin of the Stony Plain Detachment. The patrol arrived at 4:35 A.M. and concluded their search at 5:20 A.M. with negative results. Eli Androchuk provided a formal written statement to the authorities. The reporting officers noted that the witness appeared to be sincere in his account.
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p242-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 伊莱·安德罗丘克 (Eli Androchuk)、海伦·安德罗丘克 (Helen Androchuk，伊莱·安德罗丘克的母亲)、R.H. 罗威尔参谋警长 (S/Sgt. R.H. Rowell)、R.A. 圣马丁警员 (Cst. R.A. St. Martin)。

**日期 / 时间：** 1977年8月13日，山区标准时间凌晨3:00左右。

**地点：** 阿尔伯塔省塞巴海滩 (Seba Beach)；具体观测点位于瓦巴蒙湖 (Lake Wabamun) 的圣丹斯发电厂 (Sundance Power Plant) 附近，以及16号高速公路沿线。

**目击经过：** 1977年8月13日凌晨3:00左右，伊莱·安德罗丘克在从埃德蒙顿开车前往塞巴海滩的途中，发现圣丹斯发电厂附近的天空中出现了一道明亮、清晰的白光。他注意到这道光出现在发电厂烟囱上通常显示红色警示灯的位置。伊莱在沿16号高速公路向南行驶时一直跟随该物体。该物体起初处于静止状态，随后开始进行垂直和水平移动，包括上升和“抖动”。它消失在山后，随后又在地平线附近重新出现。伊莱观测了该物体20到25分钟，之后叫醒了他的母亲海伦·安德罗丘克一同见证。在向加拿大皇家骑警 (RCMP) 报告后，伊莱又观测了该物体一分钟，注意到它仍在向南移动并上升，随后他便回房休息了。据报告，整个目击过程中天空晴朗，能见度极佳。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为圆形，看起来像一颗星星，但体积明显更大——据一些说法估计，其大小约为满月的四分之一。它发出的耀眼白光从中心点向外倾斜照射。虽然一些报告指出光强保持恒定，但另一些报告则显示光密度有时会发生变化。该物体表现出不规则的运动，包括抖动、上升和水平移动。观测过程中未听到任何声音。

**调查/后续：** 加拿大皇家骑警于凌晨4:05接到关于此次目击事件的投诉。斯托尼平 (Stony Plain) 分队的 R.H. 罗威尔参谋警长和 R.A. 圣马丁警员对圣丹斯发电厂及周边地区进行了正式巡逻。巡逻队于凌晨4:35抵达，并于凌晨5:20结束搜寻，但未发现任何结果。伊莱·安德罗丘克向当局提供了正式的书面陈述。负责的警官指出，目击者在陈述时表现得非常真诚。

CA-FOIA-Part_11-p270-claude.report_summary:
**Witnesses:** Unspecified.

**Sighting:** The page describes two sightings occurring at 9:00 P.M. in 1975. The locations are identified as 3) Deckin Ave, Toronto Harbour Front area, and 4) Broadview & Danforth Riverdale Park area.

**Object:** The object is described as silver with holes and smoking. It features black wings, a yellow tail light, and is described as "hazy & smoky." The sound associated with the object is described as a "missle sound."

**Aftermath:** The document notes that the observer was "also under influence of hash & liquor." It further states that many more sightings have occurred but were only audible, always ending in the phrase "don't tell anybody."
CA-FOIA-Part_11-p270-claude.report_summary_zh:
**目击者：** 未详。

**日期：** 1975年晚上9:00。

**地点：** 3) 多伦多海滨区（Toronto Harbour Front）的迪金大道（Deckin Ave）；4) 河谷公园（Riverdale Park）的布罗德维尤与丹佛斯路口（Broadview & Danforth）。

**物体描述：** 该物体被描述为银色，带有孔洞且冒着烟。它具有黑色机翼和黄色尾灯，外观被描述为“模糊且烟雾缭绕”。与该物体相关的声音被描述为“导弹声”。

**调查/后续：** 文件指出，观察者当时“也处于大麻和酒精的影响下”。文件中进一步说明，此后还发生了许多目击事件，但仅能听到声音，且总是以“不要告诉任何人”这句话结尾。
